Sports.title: Andoni Iraola insists Man Utd have advantage despite Liverpool watching drone training footage
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola insists Man Utd have advantage despite Liverpool watching drone training footage

Liverpool host Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday for Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge after his training session was spied on by a rogue drone operator

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola gave his take on Manchester United's drone incident

Andoni Iraola has insisted that it is Liverpool who will be at a disadvantage when they face Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday.

‌



‌



United come into the weekend 18th in the Premier League table with one win from their 10 matches so far. It will be Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge since jetting in from his previous job in the United States on Wednesday.

‌



Pochettino is facing a huge task to turn around his struggling side and matters weren't helped when a rogue drone operator filmed his first training session on Thursday and uploaded the footage to YouTube. The 12-minute clip has since been deleted, but it appeared to reveal details of Pochettino's tactical work on the training pitch.

‌



Iraola has admitted that he was sent the video and, while he said he felt sorry for Pochettino, he rejected the idea that United had been put at a disadvantage by the drone.

"They sent me yesterday the footage," Iraola said in his pre-match press conference. "But I think the important part is that it shouldn't be legal. It happened to United but it could happen today to me in training you know.

‌



"Yesterday you had access to our training, the cameras in the corridors for 15 or 20 minutes, I don't know how much. You know who's training with us, who didn't train. We know the same (with United).

"But it's not [about] the matter of the advantage, it's about the fact that someone can do this... I think there's a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect and I don't think it's nice for any club, honestly."

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino has only had a few days to work before the Liverpool game (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Iraola even feels that because Pochettino is starting from a clean slate at United, his Liverpool analysis team have been unable to prepare as they would usually.

Asked about knowing Pochettino well, Iraola replied: "We've faced each other and obviously he has lots of Premier League games behind him that we can look at.

‌



"We can look at games from the US, but it's true that they have this small advantage that we don't have references to prepare. They can go different ways and, honestly, we don't know right now."

United have decided not to take legal action against the drone operator, who issued a grovelling apology on Friday morning. A statement read: "I would like to speak about yesterday's incident. A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.

‌



View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino's first Manchester United training session was filmed by a drone (Image: YouTube)

"My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time. I had wrongly presumed that with it being close to the start of the session that no meaningful training sessions would have started so would have been some harmless warming up shown.

Article continues below

"I also wrongly assumed that the training session would have been open to various media outlets. I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.

"I would also like to state that Liverpool Football Club or any other football club were not involved in my decision to film at Carrington yesterday. The video has been removed from my channel."

Sports.title: Nations League quarter-final draw RECAP: England face Norway as route to semis confirmed
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel's England have drawn Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals after topping Group C

England will take on Norway in the Nations League quarter-final - and then face either Germany or Belgium in the semis should they send the Vikings packing.

France will take on Spain, and the Netherlands will play Portugal in the other quarter-finals, with one of the four potentially facing England in the final should Thomas Tuchel's men keep progressing.

The Three Lions topped Group C in the run-up to the knockout stages, with only World champions Spain bettering Tuchel's men on matchday one.

Since then, England won every fixture that followed, seeing off Czech Republic 2-0 and 3-0 and battering Croatia 7-0 and 2-1 to set up a much-anticipated rematch with Spain.

Tuchel's men came out on top this time round in a thrilling 3-2 victory, clinching the group's top spot on goal difference and cruising into the knockout stages of this year's tournament.

England will now face Norway in March. Ireland and Wales also found out their play-off opponents this Friday.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher takes swipe at Mauricio Pochettino and warns Man Utd over key 'issue'
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher takes swipe at Mauricio Pochettino and warns Man Utd over key 'issue'

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of Manchester United for the first time on Sunday and returns to England with a point to prove after a spell as manager of the USA

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino has started work at Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher has warned Manchester United about Mauricio Pochettino's 'recurring issue' of failing to win the biggest matches in his previous jobs. United have turned to Pochettino, 54, following their worst-ever start to a Premier League season, languishing in the relegation zone after 10 games.

‌



‌



The Argentine arrives with a reputation of improving young players and raising his teams' physical output, but also with a lack of trophies and a short lifespan in roles since he left Tottenham in 2019, such as at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea. Carragher believes that Pochettino should be 'grateful' for United's decision, noting that the club turned him down on previous occasions.

‌



"Although the United States impressed as World Cup hosts, (Manchester) United are not turning to Pochettino because of his international management career," Carragher wrote in his column for the Telegraph. "In 2025 his side lost to Panama in the Concacaf Nations League semi-final, and Mexico in the Gold Cup final.

‌



"A recurring issue with Pochettino, which continued with the US team, is an inability to get over the line in the most consequential, winnable matches, resulting in a lack of big trophies.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"An ongoing debate centres on whether his work at Spurs deserves to be acclaimed for the manner in which he built a side who were in contention to be English and European champions, or scrutinised more critically because they won nothing."

The Liverpool legend does, however, feel that Pochettino and United are well matched for each party's circumstances. Carragher added: "The most successful relationships are often built on good timing. If United and Pochettino thrive together, a mutually beneficial alliance born out of circumstance rather than grand design might finally bring stability to Old Trafford.

‌



"Pochettino could not have imagined such an opportunity to achieve what he could not manage during his first two stints in the Premier League: evolving from a brilliant coach into an elite one who can win the biggest trophies.

Do you agree with Jamie Carragher? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Jamie Carragher says that Mauricio Pochettino's CV is lacking silverware (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

"The Argentine returns to England with a big reputation, but not enough on his CV to back up glowing testimonials. This must be one of his motivating factors - the chance to end any sniping and justify the claims of those who are adamant he is one of the most talented coaches of his generation.

‌



"It is indicative of how Pochettino's career was going, and how quickly football’s landscape can change, that United overlooked his claims for the job on previous occasions."

Pochettino faces a baptism of fire in his first outing as United manager. On Sunday, the Red Devils travel to Liverpool bidding to win only their second league game of the season.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta confirms Arsenal FPL ban after one of his players leaked team news
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta confirms Arsenal FPL ban after one of his players leaked team news

Mikel Arteta has taken action to stop team news leaking before Premier League matches after winger Christos Tzolis inadvertently dropped a major hint before the Liverpool game

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta has implemented a ban involving Fantasy Football

Mikel Arteta has confirmed that he has banned his players from including Arsenal stars in their Fantasy Premier League teams in an effort to stop team news leaking.

‌



‌



Arsenal winger Christos Tzolis inadvertently hinted at his recovery from an injury earlier this month through his activity on FPL. Tzolis sat out of three Premier League matches with a hamstring injury before returning for the 1-0 win over Liverpool on November 1.

‌



His comeback into the starting XI at Anfield was predicted by FPL fans, who had spotted that the Greek had selected himself as captain for that weekend, strongly hinting at his involvement.

‌



It was then spotted that Tzolis had transferred himself, Ezri Konsa and Riccardo Calafiori out of his FPL team the next week, following reports that Arteta had taken action.

Speaking ahead of Arsenal's trip to play Newcastle on Saturday evening, Arteta addressed the matter. He said: "With Christos, with the squad, with my kids as well. They are constantly asking me about the line-ups as well because they want to know.

‌



"It's a topic. This is the kind of things that are happening in our society right now and it's something new, we haven't dealt with it and we have to put new things in place.

"But obviously the confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and what you're trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret. And we will take measures to make sure that doesn't happen."

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 3 Images Christos Tzolis has got rid of himself and two Arsenal teammates from his FPL team (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

‌



Asked directly whether that meant players could no longer select themselves on FPL, Arteta replied: "Yeah."

Arsenal are not the only team to have taken action against FPL, with Chelsea having issued a reminder to staff recently over the potential for leaks. It came after news of Joao Pedro's injury surfaced before a match, with the FPL community noticing that Morgan Rogers' brother had sold the in-form striker.

‌



In 2021 the subject was a hot topic in the Premier League after Andy Robertson transferring out his Liverpool team-mate Sadio Mane was spotted by fans, who correctly predicted he must be injured.

View 3 Images Joao Pedro's injury was leaked via FPL recently (Image: Darren Walsh, Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

‌



An FPL bot then spotted that Jack Grealish must be injured after his Aston Villa team-mates Matt Targett, Conor Hourihane and Neil Taylor, as well as two Villa staff members, transferred Grealish out before a game against Leicester.

Villa boss Dean Smith was fuming after the 2-1 loss, saying: "If it's coming out of our training ground then I will find out where that's coming from and reprimand where it's coming from." He reportedly banned his players and staff from playing FPL in response.

Article continues below

"Sometimes you make a team selection and players speak to friends on other teams and talk about what you do," was how Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola responded. "Sometimes it happens and it is incredibly unethical and unprofessional but you cannot control it."

Sports.title: 'Standout candidate Murray should be Davis Cup captain one day'
Sports.content:
Great Britain's outgoing Davis Cup captain Leon Smith hopes "standout candidate" Andy Murray will one day take the role he is vacating after more than 16 years.

Smith took over from John Lloyd in 2010 following a humiliating loss to Lithuania that left Britain facing relegation to the bottom level of the historic competition.

Harnessing the talents and commitment of Murray, who he coached as a junior, Smith led Britain back to the top tier and, only five years later, to a first title since 1936 when they defeated Belgium in 2015.

Murray won all 11 singles and doubles rubbers he contested in 2015, as well as 33 out of 36 in singles in the competition overall.

The 39-year-old, who is currently head coach to Jack Draper, paid tribute to Smith, saying: "Winning the Davis Cup in 2015 with Leon as captain was one of the proudest moments of my career.

"He did a great job of bringing everyone together and making sure we all felt we had a part to play.

"I've obviously known Leon a long time, since he coached me as a kid. I think the most fun we had together was when I was playing Davis Cup and Leon was on the bench.

"I wish Leon all the best as he steps down, and good luck to the new captain."

Smith: Murray should be captain one day

Image: Leon Smith is vacating the role as skipper after more than 16 years

Smith, whose final tournament will be next week's Finals in Bologna, where Great Britain face Germany in the quarter-finals, hopes Murray will one day take the role.

"I think it is timing for him, he's busy with his life," Smith said. "He obviously is the standout candidate, isn't he? For all the attributes and more.

"Hopefully it's something he's interested in the future.

"The Davis Cup, it's not just the ties itself. It's being at the events. It's supporting the players and their personal coaches on their journeys.

"And it's also the Olympics and his history in the Olympics is second to none.

"So I do hope it's something he does in the future, but I respect that it's not for him right now, and I can understand it.

"But I really hope at some point in the future that he does take it on."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking in February, Smith discussed the current state of the British team and how far they can go in the Davis Cup

'Greg Rusedski deserves to be in conversation'

Image: Former British No 1 Greg Rusedski is a strong candidate to take over the role from Leon Smith

Speaking on Sky Sports Tennis, Andy's older brother Jamie discussed the role with Gigi Salmon and Tim Henman.

The seven-time Grand Slam doubles champion said: "I think that's an interesting way to see how they're going to go about it. I think there's probably quite a few people that would quite fancy it.

"I think Greg [Rusedski] as well, with everything that he's done in his career, would definitely deserve to be in that conversation.

"I'm sure Andy will get asked about his interest levels. He certainly should be given everything that he's done for tennis in our country."

Henman reflected on Smith's tenure by saying: "A big part of that role was making sure that Andy turned up to play and then giving him the environment to go out and perform as well as he could.

"Andy at that time was loving playing Davis Cup, representing his country and the team went from strength to strength.

"When Leon started, they were at the bottom of professional tennis, but they worked their way up to lifting the trophy in Belgium."

Sports.title: Celtic suffer Baur injury blow
Sports.content:
Celtic midfielder Mika Baur faces a lengthy period on the sidelines with an ankle injury.

The German midfielder, who signed from Paderborn in the summer, is facing around ten weeks on the sidelines with the injury.

He left Celtic Park on crutches after he was forced off during their 1-0 win against Kilmarnock before the international break.

Manager Martin O'Neill said: "He'll be out for some considerable time. It's a real shame, he was playing great for us."

"There's talk about ten weeks, but I spoke to Mika yesterday and he's a quick healer. There are things he can't do for a while; his foot's in a boot.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Baur suffered the injury in Celtic's Scottish Premiership win against Kilmarnock

"He was on fire, he was doing great for us. It is a blow and it seemed so innocuous as well.

"I thought he'd been kicked, but it was the other foot he landed on and he's just gone over on it."

Celtic could also be without Benjamin Nygren for Saturday's Scottish Premiership return against St Mirren.

The midfielder missed the second of Sweden's recent double-header, with O'Neill confirming his absence from club training.

He said: "Nygren didn't train today, but we'll see how he is in the morning - he's got a sore heel. He's been feeling it for a couple of weeks."

Image: Celtic's Benjamin Nygren missed training with a "sore heel"

Celtic face a gruelling five-match stretch of games over the next two weeks, with a visit to Portugal to face Torreense in the Europa League after St Mirren.

They then travel to Hearts, live on Sky Sports, before taking on Dundee at Dens Park, then a home game against St Johnstone.

The defending champions are four points ahead of Old Firm rivals Rangers at the top of the Premiership, having played a game more.

Cheavon Clarke catapulted himself into the top tier of the cruiserweight division with his stunning stoppage victory over Chris Billam-Smith.

Billam-Smith is a highly-experienced world champion, well known for hard-fought victories over the likes of Lawrence Okolie and Richard Riakporhe.

"I've always been world class. It's just waiting on the world to catch up and see it. That fight gave me the opportunity to do that. We're getting there," Clarke told Sky Sports.

When they fought at the Copper Box Arena earlier this month, Clarke did something no one had managed before - he dropped Billam-Smith (twice in fact) and stopped him.

"To Chris' detriment, he's a tough guy and in boxing it's not the place to be tough," Clarke said. "History is a great tell of the future. Every tough guy has a day where he's not tough no more. Unfortunately that was Chris' day."

Clarke has come back from defeat himself and doesn't rule out Billam-Smith doing the same.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chev Clarke bounced back from being put down twice in the fourth round as he went on to stop Jack Massey in the seventh round of their cruiserweight classic.

"There was talks of this after the fight, but who knows? What does it do for Chev's career right now, bearing in mind that I'm currently ranked above him," Clarke said.

"I'm looking to fight the guys above me and trying to make what makes sense for me."

2m ago 13.55 EST Manchester United chief executive officer Omar Berrada has defended the club’s managerial turnover and transfer strategy, insisting the Premier League side remains committed to long-term stability despite going through three permanent managers in less than ⁠three seasons. Michael Carrick became the seventh permanent manager sacked by United since Alex Ferguson retired ⁠after delivering the club’s 20th league title in 2013. He is also the third ​manager dismissed since Jim Ratcliffe became ‌a minority owner in ‌2024. “If you think about the fact that we’ve had three permanent managers in ‌less than three seasons, clearly we haven’t achieved the stability that we want to,” Berrada told Sky Sports. “There are different circumstances as to why it didn’t work out with Erik [ten Hag'], Ruben [Amorim'] and now Michael. And we’re always learning. We’re always trying to improve and understand what has failed.” Berrada defended the club’s approach, saying United would continue ⁠to invest when suitable opportunities emerged but would not be pressured into ​overspending. “We’re actually happy ​with the players that we bought,” ​Berrada said. “We need to stay disciplined. We need to buy ​the right players for ‌the right value ​at the ​right time. There’s no point in us spending £40m or £50m for players that we’re not convinced are going to add value to the team.” Reuters Share

28m ago 13.29 EST A brutal day for Ian Evatt yesterday, who was sacked as head coach of Blackpool … on his 45th birthday. Blackpool put out a happy birthday message in the morning and seven hours later, released this statement: Blackpool Football Club can announce that Ian Evatt has departed his role as Head Coach after 12 months in charge. During a hugely successful playing career at Bloomfield Road, Ian made over 250 appearances for the Seasiders. In his six years at Blackpool, he played a vital role in the Club’s memorable rise from League One to the Premier League, which included two successful play-off campaigns. The Club thanks Ian for all of his efforts during his time at Bloomfield Road. Steve Thompson will take charge of the team for this weekend’s fixture, along with Stephen Crainey, Stephen Dobbie and Steve Banks. Blackpool are 20th in League One, just above the relegation zone. They host Wigan on Saturday. View image in fullscreen Ian Evatt (centre) applauds the Blackpool fans after the draw at Sheffield Wednesday earlier this month. The Women’s Super League game was level at 1-1 when Jenna Clark tucked the ball into the net after ­Arsenal had failed to clear a corner, but the assistant referee disallowed the goal for offside against Vivien ­Endemann. 1h ago 12.32 EST St Mirren’s independent supports’ association, Smisa, has been given a chance to cement its control of the club after the charity Kibble, founded in the 19th century and which defines its core purposes as “supporting at-risk children and young people (aged five to 26) across the UK”, decided to sell its 27.5% stake in the club. Smisa, who already own 51%, are being given first option to buy their shares. This from the club’s website: Kibble became part-owner in March 2020 alongside SMiSA. The arrangement, a top-flight club owned by its fans and run in partnership with one of the country’s biggest charities, is believed to be unique in European football. Its aim was to use the club as a platform for Kibble’s young workforce development programme. Since then, more than 200 young people have gained training, employment, education and support through the partnership. Shared use of the Marbill Coaches Stadium and Ralston training ground has given the charity’s work a home at the centre of the Paisley community. The club has stabilised over the same period, with turnover rising year-on-year. Its latest set of accounts for the year ending May 2026 is due to be published soon. Kibble’s board believes its part in the club’s story is complete and with St Mirren on a stable footing, the change in shareholding gives the club and SMiSA members the opportunity to consider how it grows from here. Mark Macmillan, chief executive of Kibble, said: “When we joined SMiSA as part-owners in 2020, we wanted to show what a football club and a children’s charity could achieve together. More than 200 young people have trained, worked, learned and found support through this partnership, and Paisley is better connected for it. “We set out to do a job and we’ve done it. Kibble came in to make a difference for young people, not to be a long-term investor in a football club. With the club in a good place, now is the right moment to step back and give St Mirren the freedom to shape its next chapter.” St Mirren are currently eighth in the Scottish Premiership. Share

4h ago 10.09 EST Overlap, underlap or sit back? How Premier League teams use their full-backs Overlapping. Underlapping. Inverted. Traditional. The role of full-back has evolved dramatically. Once a defensive-first position that provided some auxiliary attacking support, the role has developed into something far more multifaceted. Just ask right-back Ben White, who – with Riccardo Calafiori on the left – has been an important figure in Arsenal’s superb start to the campaign. Talking a few years ago, he said: “Playing full-back the way [Mikel Arteta] wants is completely different to any other manager. To play full-back for him, you’ve got to be a centre-midfielder, a centre-back, a winger and a No 10.” Between them, White and Calafiori have contributed to six goals for Arsenal already in the Premier League this season (White: three assists; Calafiori: one goal, two assists). No other defender has registered more than three goal involvements so far. The Arsenal duo are a great illustration of the impact full-backs can have. But, with the position more demanding than ever before, how does each Premier League team deploy theirs? Read the latest insight from the Opta Analyst: Overlap, underlap or sit back? 4h ago 09.58 EST Pochettino will have element of surprise an Anfield, says Iraola Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola fears Mauricio Pochettino will have a tactical advantage over him on Sunday because the new Manchester United manager is coming in fresh. We don’t have the references that we have against other teams.” One advantage Iraola could have looked to exploit was the drone footage posted on YouTube of Pochettino’s first training session at Carrington, but the Liverpool manager was quick to criticise the YouTube channel that posted the video. “They were sending me the footage yesterday, but I think the important thing about this is that it shouldn’t be legal. Sports.title: Tom Brady in talks over buying Chelsea stake after Birmingham City exit
Sports.content:
Tom Brady is in discussions about buying a small stake in Chelsea. The NFL legend sold a minority share in Birmingham City this month after three years, a move sources said was to pave the way for investing at Stamford Bridge.

Brady was a guest of Chelsea when they won the Club World Cup in New Jersey last year and was seen celebrating with the players after their remarkable 3-0 final win over Paris Saint-Germain.

The seven-time Super Bowl winner is understood to have a good relationship with Behdad Eghbali, whose fund, Clearlake Capital, owns 86.5% of Chelsea after Todd Boehly and Mark Walter sold their shares in September.

Brady bought into Birmingham in August 2023, less than a year after his second and final retirement from the NFL, after the club’s takeover by Tom Wagner’s Knighthead Capital.

Brady was appointed chair of the club’s advisory board and had a prominent role in the 2025 Amazon Prime documentary Built in Birmingham: Brady & The Blues, which made headlines when he questioned the “work ethic” of Wayne Rooney, who was the manager.

In announcing Brady’s departure the club said: “Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years.”

Brady owns a minority stake in the NFL team Las Vegas Raiders, which he purchased alongside Wagner.

Chelsea declined to comment.

Sports.title: Football Daily | The Premier League resumes: here’s our almost essential club-by-club recap
Sports.content:
WHERE WERE WE?

Just like taking the Manchester United job or listening in on a conversation with Stephen Warnock, the men’s international break can be a long, hard slog, a domestic hiatus so long that we can forget both basic hygiene and how the clubs are faring in the Best League in the World™: the Championship the Premier League. So after desperately trying to break into either tears or just a smile at Harry Kane’s appearance record – no dice, unfortunately – here is a rundown on the state of play for each club, as we prepare for a weekend of football that might actually make us feel something.

1 Arsenal There are some genuinely likable things about the Gunners – Bukayo Saka, Paul Merson being a bit giddy, Ben White’s apathy to it all – but Arsenal fans were a lot easier to manage when they weren’t this good. It’s theirs to lose, etc.

2 Brighton Turns out all you need to turn your club into genuine title contenders is a world-class recruitment programme and Pascal Gross to accidentally realise that he’s the second coming aged 35.

3 Manchester City Enjoy it while it lasts, lads.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Fernández and Erling Haaland in high spirits at City training. Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty Images

4 Liverpool These lot haven’t been title contenders since Mohamed Salah started playing like Robert Snodgrass and haven’t looked like vastly improving since replacing the right-winger with various different, expensive left-wingers.

5 Chelsea Anything could and probably will happen with the Blues, and that’s not a compliment.

6 Everton The Toffees should be worse than last season – Iliman Ndiaye has left, Jack Grealish issued a grovelling apology after going awol, their only striker is Thierno Barry – but instead they are much, much better. David Moyes, the genius grandpa of the league at 63, will set a new Everton record for games managed this weekend (593).

7 Bournemouth The Dorset Hydra from Greek mythology. Every time you cut off its head, or sell a defender to PSG or Real Madrid, they come back stronger. Since Alex Scott was injured on 3 October, Bournemouth lost at Chelsea and then won eight on the bounce. Make it make sense.

8 Brentford This underdog narrative is wearing a little thin now. Brentford are just a well-oiled football machine but they have no mates and worse, no enemies. What a sad little life. Enjoy Tin Pot qualification. We hope it makes you very happy.

View image in fullscreen Brentford: decent. Photograph: Andy Skinner/Action Plus/Shutterstock

9 Leeds The Yorkshire club might be 78% Dominic Calvert-Lewin at this point, so only Lucas Radebe knows where they will be when the striker gets knacked, but Daniel Farke is doing a fine job with Leeds in the top half. For now.

10 Aston Villa It would be hard for any club to lose Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins, Youri Tieleman and Emi Martínez in one transfer window and improve. Not much more to say. Why do we like Zion Suzuki so much? Genuinely not sure.

11 Tottenham Whisper it, but are Spurs back (to being a mid-table team again)?

12 Newcastle One win in six and a kit that looks like a barcode means it’s been a poor campaign thus far, which Matthias Jaissle and co will hope to resurrect this weekend against – checks notes – the champions. Ah.

13 Hull City A remarkable achievement that the promoted side are not anywhere near the bottom three considering there is absolutely nobody, including Sergej Jakirovic, who can name 11 current Hull players off the top of their heads.

View image in fullscreen Oli McBurnie: we knew he was in the team. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

14 Ipswich Town Shining bright like Gary O’Neil’s teeth. Keep this up and they might even survive.

15 Fulham Quick tip for Álvaro Arbeloa: when you said on Friday that “Fulham is not a jail – everyone that is here is because they want to be here”, it really makes it sound like Fulham is actually a jail, which nobody wants to be in. Roll on Manchester City (A)!

16 Nottingham Forest It’s entirely believable that Forest will follow up their 3-1 win over Manchester City with victory at Bournemouth this weekend. It’s also entirely believable that Oliver Glasner will be sacked by Christmas and Forest will be playing in the Championship next season. It’s all part of the Evangelos Marinakis Experience, baby.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

17 Coventry City Genuinely quite nice to see that sky blue kit back in the top flight. All Cov fans would snap your hand off for 17th come the end of the campaign.

18 Manchester United Mauricio Pochettino has the chance to do something very, very funny over the next few months.

View image in fullscreen A drone’s eye view of Old Trafford, earlier. Photograph: Gary Oakley/MB Media/Getty Images

19 Sunderland Turns out qualifying for Europe isn’t all it’s made up to be.

20 Crystal Palace The Eagles are surely too good to go down? Their trip to Coventry this weekend absolutely stinks of a six-pointer. Hard not to believe that Thomas Frank’s lovely locks will sort out the mess in south London. Imagine if Adam Wharton had Thomas Frank’s hair? OK, that’s enough Football Daily for today.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his ‌United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time. I fully accept it was unethical on my part. I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely ‌hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match” – a drone operator who filmed United’s first ⁠training ⁠session under their new head coach at Carrington has apologised for what he called a “total error of judgment”. Welcome to Manchester, Mauricio.

View image in fullscreen It’s not hard to get a picture of Mauricio Pochettino in his training kit. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images

double quotation mark I’m a bit late to the party in terms of commenting on the ‘perfume in Poundland’ litigation (Football Daily letters passim). However, I can’t help thinking that David Beckham could have avoided all of this palaver if he’d arranged for Dior to manage his line of fragrances – it seems to have worked out swimmingly for Robbie Sauvage” – Paul Taverner.

double quotation mark Oh my days, the Memory Lane picture (yesterday’s full email edition) of Eric Gates and Kevin O’Callaghan playing Breakout was surely crying out for an Escape To Victory reference, with the Ipswich and Republic of Ireland winger O’Callaghan famously playing the goalkeeper that had his arm broken to allow Sly Stallone’s character to join the team in their erm … breakout! Nearly time for the traditional Christmas airing of this classic as well” – Dave Griffiths.

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Dave Griffiths. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

Sports.title: Premier League news: Grealish available again for Everton, Maresca hints at City tweaks
Sports.content:
1. Grealish returns after four games missed David Moyes has confirmed Jack Grealish is fit and available for Everton’s visit to Brentford on Monday after his recent disciplinary breach. Grealish missed Everton’s past four games mainly as a consequence of missing training before last month’s Carabao Cup win over Newcastle. His last appearance for the team was in the 2-0 loss to Chelsea on 17 October, but Moyes is now prepared to welcome the playmaker back into the fold. “He’s back in training and back in around the team,” the Everton manager said. The 31-year-old played in a behind-closed-doors fixture against Derby last week and apologised on social media for being unable to help the team, who have performed well in his absence. Moyes said of the apology: “I don’t do social media but I’ve heard about it.” Asked whether he had received a similar apology from Grealish in person, the Everton manager added: “We’ve just been getting on with our work. We’ve got a lot of other players here who we need to focus on as well, I can’t just concentrate on one player, and I’ve been trying to make sure everybody gets the right preparation for our next game against Brentford.” The Scot backed Jordan Pickford to respond strongly to the threat from James Trafford to his England place after the Leeds goalkeeper’s inclusion and impressive display in the Nations League win over Spain. “I don’t think it will have a great effect on him,” claimed Moyes. “If you’re playing for England you will always have other players chasing you. I still think Jordan Pickford is out there on his own at the moment. If anything, he’s getting better. It will be good for us now that he’s getting competition [with England].” Andy Hunter

2. Maresca backs Fernández but hints at tweaks Enzo Maresca has said he may need to tweak the balance of Manchester City’s midfield amid their faltering Premier League form. City went into the November international break on the back of three consecutive defeats in the league, having begun the campaign with seven wins on the bounce. Maresca’s side are third in the table, six points off leaders Arsenal, and face Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday. Maresca defended Enzo Fernández, whose performances have prompted debate over his best position and whether he leaves City’s team unbalanced. Maresca has mostly opted to play the £125m signing from Chelsea deeper in midfield alongside fellow summer recruit Elliot Anderson, with the more defensive-minded Ayyoub Bouaddi, who also arrived in the summer, largely a substitute. View image in fullscreen Enzo Fernández’s inclusion has often left City’s midfield without balance. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Neal Simpson/Apl/Sportsphoto “For sure there are things we need to do better in terms of balance,” Maresca said. “But the same midfield that won seven games in a row is the same midfield that lost three games in a row. “We won games with Enzo, we lost games with Enzo. I know that when there is a defeat, we are all looking for the reason why. Sometimes we probably need more balance, we need different kinds of players. [It] depends a little bit on the game. The idea is to continue in attack in the same way, creating chances, but finding a balance when we defend.” Maresca also dismissed the notion that any uncertainty surrounding City’s financial case with the Premier League has negatively affected recent performances. It has been nearly two months since City were found guilty of more than 100 charges related to breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, and they are waiting for the outcome of their appeal. All three of City’s league defeats have come since the ruling. “I don’t think the players are thinking too much about the noise,” Maresca said. “I don’t think they are worried about it.” Dominic Booth

Sports.title: Bukayo Saka may not return for Arsenal before Christmas, Mikel Arteta admits
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has said Bukayo Saka may not return before Christmas as the Arsenal forward continues his rehabilitation from a thigh injury.

Saka has been out since limping off against Bayern Munich at the end of last month, and it is understood he has yet to resume light training. Arteta revealed more tests during the international break confirmed the England forward did not need surgery and that he was expected to be out for another four weeks.

When asked whether Saka could be fit for the game against Manchester United on 20 December, Arteta was unsure. “I cannot be that specific,” he said. “In four weeks’ time a lot of things can happen. Maybe it is three and then it is five.

“At the end, there are a few elements. One is the healing of that tissue – and we cannot predict exactly when that tissue is going to be in the best condition to push it. Then there is the rehab plan that we have now, what he needs to do in the gym, what he needs to do in terms of treatment and on the field.”

Arsenal will also be without Martín Zubimendi for Saturday’s trip to Newcastle after the Spain midfielder picked up a hamstring injury against England last Sunday. Otherwise Arteta has a clean bill of health, with William Saliba poised to return after a long-term back injury, although Max Dowman remains suspended after his red card against Fleetwood.

Christos Tzolis is expected to start but Arteta revealed Arsenal’s players were now banned from selecting themselves or any teammates in the Fantasy Premier League game after the Greece forward’s team was leaked before the win over Liverpool on 1 November. Tzolis had been out injured for several weeks but picked himself for the trip to Anfield, alerting their opponents. He is believed to have played his wildcard to remove all the Arsenal players from his squad.

“We haven’t dealt with it [before] and I wanted to put new things in place,” said Arteta. “But obviously confidentiality is something critical because it’s about trust and about what you are trying to do. That should be kept as a huge secret and we’ll take measures to make sure it doesn’t happen.”

Sports.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season
Sports.content:
The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged.

Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing.

There have inevitably been outliers. Tottenham have tumbled by at least 10 places after matchweek 10 in the past two seasons and Newcastle (in 2021-22), Crystal Palace and Everton (both 2017-18) have risen from the relegation zone at this point to the safety of mid-table by May.

But even moving one position across the remainder of the season can make an enormous difference to a team on the fringe of the Champions League qualification spots, or to those that sit 17th or 18th after 10 games. Not since 2006-07 have the bottom three clubs with 28 matches to go all been relegated.

This fact feels especially relevant this season given two of the three teams in the drop zone have changed their manager since the previous round of matches. Sunderland have stood by Régis Le Bris but he is the favourite to be the next Premier League manager to leave their post. If we can reasonably assume at least one of the clubs currently 18th to 20th will be in the top flight in 2027-28, which is best placed to survive?

It is going to be very tough for Crystal Palace. Opta’s underlying data model implies they are where they deserve to be in the table, whereas Manchester United and Sunderland should be much higher. The largest improvement Palace’s new manager, Thomas Frank, engineered between weeks 10 and 38 at Brentford was two places, which will not cut it this season. Palace have to take inspiration from the 2024-25 season, in which they also had seven points after 10 games yet rose to finish 12th.

Mauricio Pochettino’s Chelsea were 11th going into their 11th game in 2023-24 before ending sixth. As they were also 11th in early April, they made a much shorter dash to the finish line, though. Pochettino’s teams usually improve as campaigns wear on, with Tottenham rising three places after week 10 in each of his first three seasons with the club. A similar lift in his new role would not make this season a rousing success for United but it would stave off the unthinkable idea of relegation.

For someone to escape, someone else must take their place. Ignoring the possibility that the answer to “who?” may be Manchester City, the team in 17th are inevitably the ones most at risk. Of the 13 sides in the past decade who were outside the drop zone after 10 games but went down, six were fourth-bottom going into matchweek 11.

Given that the points gap between first and 20th (20) was last lower at this stage in 2015-16, those figures may be more pertinent than position this season. Leeds in 2022-23 and Bournemouth three years earlier had 13 points after 10 games but were relegated, as did Blackpool in 2010-11 and Middlesbrough two seasons before them.

Only nine clubs are now above that bar, with Aston Villa, Newcastle and Tottenham among those who are not. The table is unlikely to change too much before the end of the campaign but there is a distinct chance that a secure-looking side will perish.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s Lisa Baum: ‘I believe in us. I think it’s all about the small margins’
Sports.content:
Lisa Baum is 19, for the next few days at least, but you wouldn’t know it. The Germany forward plays with a maturity that explains why she was handed her Arsenal debut in their opening game of the season, less than two months after joining.

Baum had been told that the 2025 European champions had a vision for her but that coming in as a young player she would have to be patient. Ten minutes into her debut against Brighton, in Crawley, the young winger scored what would be the winning goal.

“It was unbelievable,” says Baum, speaking in a small meeting room at Arsenal’s London Colney training ground with a maturity that matches her play. “Everything just went so quick. I just shot, my brain was just switched off, it just came out.”

That win kickstarted Arsenal’s season but it quickly stalled. In the league, the team went five games without a win. After a 2-0 defeat by OL Lyonnes in the Champions League on Thursday night, Arsenal have five wins from their opening 15 games. It is far from the season they, or many others, envisaged.

Sunday’s final home game of the year, against West Ham, offers an opportunity to take some positivity into the international break, after which Arsenal face three away fixtures before the winter pause.

View image in fullscreen Lisa Baum celebrates after scoring 10 minutes into her Arsenal debut against Brighton. Photograph: Alex Burstow/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

“I believe in us,” says Baum. “I think it’s all about the small margins. Sometimes it’s luck, sometimes it’s in the final decision-making, sometimes it’s how close we are to a goal that doesn’t go in. But we work really hard in every training session and on trying to keep ourselves up mentally and physically. We’re trying to push through the barrier that we maybe have right now, but we get a lot of trust from the staff and coaches. Everybody really believes in each other and I think it’s not going to take long before we’re through this part of the journey.”

Overall, Arsenal have not been playing particularly badly. They have been creating chances and dominating games but struggling to translate that into goals and points. In October, Baum earned a first senior Germany call-up and made her debut off the bench at half-time against Australia, having previously featured for teams from the under-16s to under-23s.

Quick Guide Taylor: Pro Ref says Liverpool goal against Arsenal should have stood Show The Liverpool head coach, Gareth Taylor, says Pro Ref has accepted it made an error in disallowing a goal his side thought they had scored during this month's 2-1 defeat by Arsenal at Anfield. The Women’s Super League game was level at 1-1 when Jenna Clark tucked the ball into the net after ­Arsenal had failed to clear a corner, but the assistant referee disallowed the goal for offside against Vivien ­Endemann. Replays showed the delivery had been ­inadvertently played off an Arsenal foot rather than being a deliberate forward pass from the home side. There is no VAR in the WSL. Taylor, whose side host Chelsea in the WSL on Saturday, said on Friday: “We have had an acceptance of a mistake from the corner that we scored from, where we should be 2-1 up at half-time. [There was] no apology, but we accept that there was an error made on their part and that game can look different.” Tom Garry Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Baum moved to Germany when she was four. Born to a Tanzanian mother and German father, she spent her first years in Dar es Salaam in Tanzania. They swapped a city with a population of about four million for Ahrensbök, a municipality with a population of just over 8,000 near the Baltic coast. “I think my mum had the hardest time out of us in the family, with the move to Germany,” she says. Baum says she and her brother, Dennis, “learned to adapt easily”.

Baum doesn’t remember her years on the east coast of Africa but when she went back three or four years ago, some sort of memory was triggered. “It was a feeling, or feelings,” she says. “It was so good to grow up there. It was warm, it was the beautiful beaches, it was having all your family around. I was in kindergarten or I was in the water a lot – I love to swim.”

View image in fullscreen Lisa Baum, in action for Arsenal at Anfield, played for RB Leipzig last season. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

She started playing football after the move to northern Germany, desperate to copy Dennis. “My father played football when he was younger – he was a goalkeeper – but he stopped when he didn’t really enjoy it any more. My mum wasn’t a big fan of me playing; she dressed me like a girly girl, with princess dresses and that kind of stuff, but I was never really like that at that age. I always wanted to follow my older brother – I wanted to wear his clothes. He started playing football before me and I wanted to be like him.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Baum would play on the side of the pitch at her brother’s club until a parent said she should be playing too. After playing with various local teams she joined Hamburg’s academy. She worked her way into the first team and they won promotion to the second tier in her first season. In the 2024-25 season they reached the DFB-Pokal semi-finals and the top flight. Baum moved to RB Leipzig and scored five goals in 27 games before Arsenal swooped.

“Everything was just so quick,” she says of the move to London. Training required getting used to: “Everything was so sharp, everything was technically excellent, like 10 out of 10. I was quite nervous and had some clumsy actions.”

The transfer also involved swapping an average attendance last season of 1,651 for one of 33,808. “It’s unbelievable,” says Baum of playing at the Emirates Stadium. “I had only played in a big stadium once before. You can’t even believe how much the fans give you when you step on the pitch. There’s so much support, that of course we need in this current time. I think Arsenal is a club that holds on to us, on to the team, and gives us a lot of strength.”

View image in fullscreen Lisa Baum with the wrist strap she wears in memory of her brother, Dennis. Photograph: Europa Press Sports/Europa Press/Getty Images

Look closely at Baum’s left wrist when she plays and you will usually see a strip of white tape around it. Sometimes it has something written on it. She’s done it “since that day” – the day in 2022 when Dennis died in a car accident, aged 17.

The brother that inspired her on to a pitch is with her on it at the highest level. “The next time I was on the football pitch, I just felt I wanted to do that,” she says. “I feel like it’s given me a different kind of strength and confidence. Sometimes I don’t write anything, but it’s about just having the physical feeling that he is with me.”

Sports.title: Liverpool fan found not guilty of racial abuse after Antoine Semenyo withdraws from case
Sports.content:
A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the Manchester City forward withdrew his support for the prosecution.

Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool magistrates court on Friday in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting abuse during the Premier League match between Liverpool and Semenyo’s former club Bournemouth at Anfield on 15 August last year.

But Simon Jones, prosecuting, said: “Following recent contact made with Mr Semenyo, he has indicated he is no longer supportive of proceedings and the prosecution do not consider it is appropriate to compel him. In those circumstances we offer no further evidence in the case.”

District judge Mary Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty to the charge of racially aggravated behaviour.

Quick Guide How do I 

Semenyo, who left Bournemouth for Manchester City in January, had been due to give evidence last month but the trial was adjourned halfway through when Mogan was taken to hospital after a seizure.

The court had heard Mogan, in a wheelchair, shouted racial abuse at Semenyo as he went to take a throw-in about 30 minutes into the game. He was alleged to have said: “Hurry up and take the throw-in, you black bastard.”

Opening the case last month, Mr Jones said: “That racial abuse was shouted directly at Antoine Semenyo, who was close to him. Mr Semenyo briefly froze, as he couldn’t believe what the male had said.”

Mogan then shouted: “I’m talking to you, you cunt,” the court heard. Witnesses also said they saw him throw his chewing gum at the footballer.

Semenyo reported the incident to the referee and Mogan was removed from the stadium at half-time. Mogan, who had an intermediary with him in court, told police in interview that Semenyo had called him a cripple after he shouted at the player to “hurry up”.

Mogan declined to comment as he left court.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino is right and Mark Cuban is wrong – US soccer is screaming for relegation change
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino is right and Mark Cuban is wrong – US soccer is screaming for relegation change

Lionel Messi did not choose to sign with an MLS team because he wanted to play in the greatest football/soccer league in the world.

Messi chose to align himself with Inter Miami and David Beckham as he approaches 40 years old because the living Argentina legend wanted to keep playing the biggest sport in the world while building his global brand in America.

7 Messi leads MLS in scoring this season but is in the final era of his career Credit: AFP

Would MLS be better with relegation and promotion?

Of course, there are other reasons why the greatest footballer in history keeps scoring goals in Major League Soccer, which significantly trails the NHL in annual revenue.

Messi entered the weekend with 26 goals, ahead of the likes of Petar Musa and Sam Surridge.

That was during the same week when the pros and cons of relegation and promotion were debated from California and Florida to Manchester and London.

World Cup winner and Vancouver Whitecaps star Thomas Muller is the latest big name to call out the MLS topic that won't go away.

"There is no relegation. There is no big pressure," Muller told Global News. "There is, ‘Oh, yes, we do a rebuild.’

"Nobody is happy to lose, but it’s totally different when you fight for getting relegated.

"Maybe, you lose budget for the next year, the whole club. You lose people working at the club. When the budget changes, it’s totally different for fans."

Muller won 33 trophies, including two Champions Leagues and 13 Bundesliga titles, so the Whitecaps midfielder knows what he speaks.

Vancouver also tops the MLS Western Conference with 64 points, which make Muller's comments even more searing -- especially after new Manchester United manager and former USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino effectively said the same thing.

"If you start in MLS and you haven’t won a game in three months and you’re at the bottom, what’s the consequence if there’s no promotion or relegation, no international competition?" Pochettino told El Pais.

7 Mauricio Pochettino wanted more out of soccer in the USA Credit: getty

7 Thomas Muller called out the 'pressure' of MLS football without relegation Credit: Getty

"American sports reward losers! But soccer is different: If you reward those who don’t win … If you don’t have goals, you don’t fight. If I lose, what happens? Nothing. They just fire the coach."

Compare that passion to the words of new MLS commissioner Larry Berg, who immediately pushed back against adding real jeopardy to a soccer season.

“I can understand the appeal for the fans, (but) I don’t think it’s a great way to build a league," Berg said in August.

"I don’t think it’s a way to get stadiums built, get training facilities built, and to have owners invest in rosters and all the other things you need to do.

“So the great thing about promotion and relegation for fans is that the jeopardy is quite severe. But I think there are other ways to create jeopardy during the regular season, (and) again in the play-offs, during the play-offs, to get to the next round. That’s what we want to focus on.”

What Berg could have said is that San Diego FC paid a whopping $500million expansion fee to enter MLS in 2023, and that is why Major League Soccer owners still fear relegation and promotion so much.

7 Tyler Adams spoke out in favor of MLS relegation to help the league Credit: getty

7 America's best soccer players take their professional talent overseas Credit: Getty

The costs are too high, the real investment on return is still a long time away, and MLS is still trying to find a spot on the same TV that is dominated by the NFL, NBA, MLB, college football, college basketball, NHL, WNBA, auto racing, golf, tennis and so much more in America.

"He (Pochettino) is wrong. If you need external motivation to compete, you shouldn’t be on the court/pitch/field, in any capacity," former Dallas Mavericks owner Mark Cuban tweeted.

Ex-USMNT and Premier League goalkeeper Brad Friedel has seen both sides of the game in America and England.

Friedel's words leading up to the historically large 2026 World Cup still stick with me five months later.

"No one's making money in the football there, soccer there," Friedel exclusively told talkSPORT.

"So my worry is, does this last for another ten years? Because, I mean, how many billionaires are out there, billionaire consortiums, that are going to pay $500million franchise fees?

7 Brad Friedel wondered about the financial future of MLS Credit: getty

7 Mark Cuban pushed back against Pochettino's relegation rant Credit: Getty

"That's why you see so many American owners coming over to Europe. Why? Because you own stadium, you own land, you own training ground. And you're not paying $500 mil upfront for a franchise fee system that, if everyone keeps losing money, what happens with the franchise fee eventually?

"It invariably is going to go down -- unless they get the media rights deal. If they get the media rights deal, then everything will be great."

Pochettino and Muller are 100 per cent right -- the lack of relegation and promotion are holding back soccer in America.

But when CF Montreal (MLS) is worth more than AFC Bournemouth (Premier League) and Burnley (Championship), it's no wonder that MLS owners aren't willing to watch their cash burn on the whims of one down year.

"I would like to see (promotion and relegation) in MLS, in the U.S. I think that would add to the competitive nature of the league," USMNT and Bournemouth star Tyler Adams said in 2025.

"It just gives everyone a lot more to play for when you know there's a risk of going down when you don't play well, so it adds a little bit more pressure, adds a little bit more nerves and excitement for the fans as well. So hopefully one day it's in MLS."

MLS has made solid strides under Don Garber, who will step down as commissioner at the end of the year.

It's on Berg and MLS owners to listen to the truth that Pochettino, Muller and others have spoken.

The power, pain and history of the English football pyramid can't be recreated in the USA.

But there are other modern ways to make Major League Soccer more respected on a global stage.



Will Gavin, Brian T. Smith, former NFL star Efe Obada and a collection of special guests debate the biggest talking points across the NFL, soccer, NBA and more.

Sports.title: Manchester United CEO defends controversial transfer decision in rare interview
Sports.content:
Omar Berrada has defended the lack of reinforcements in defence at Manchester United by citing their disciplined approach to transfers.

United spent in the region of £155million on three midfielders - Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans - during the summer.



3 With Luke Shaw unable to regularly play due to fitness woes, United's decision not to sign a new left-back was controversial Credit: Getty

Goalkeeper Karl Darlow also signed on a free transfer, but no new faces arrived in a back line that conceded 50 goals in the Premier League last season.

One area of concern was the left-back position as Luke Shaw remains inconsistent with fitness and United have no natural back-up option.

Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui, both right-backs, have played in the role when needed but with little success.



Newcastle star Lewis Hall was a target before he signed a new deal at St. James' Park.

However, club CEO Berrada has insisted that United are determined not to be caught overspending on players.



Berrada defends United transfer activity

"When you look at the other areas of the pitch, and there's a lot of discussion about the back line," he explained to Sky Sports. "But we did come into it thinking: we have depth.

"We have nine players that can play in the back line, in the back four positions. So that's why we looked primarily at investing in the midfield. But we were always looking for opportunities.



"I think it's been widely reported that we were looking at potentially the left-back position as a reinforcement.

"I think what we've seen in the back line is we've had injuries, it's taken Matthijs de Ligt longer than we would want it to get back.

"Unfortunately, Luke Shaw suffered a muscle injury that meant he was out for five or six weeks.

3 Berrada is aware that United could have bought a new left-back, but explained that they wanted to be disciplined in the market Credit: Getty



"So could we have signed an additional defender to straighten the depth and the quality? Yes, but we have to find the right players and you have to find the right players at the right value.

"There's no point in us spending £40million, £50million for players that we're not convinced are going to add value to the team.

"So it's always about being disciplined and finding the right opportunities and getting the right players that are going to take us forward."

Berrada added: "When I talk about being disciplined, I talk about not overspending on players that don't necessarily add quality to the team.



"Because when you sign a player that doesn't work out for Man United, it becomes very difficult to move that player on or to get the sale we want. And that can set us back.

"So when I talk about being disciplined, I'm not talking about necessarily not spending to get the top players.

3 Pochettino could be set to land new defensive options at United when the transfer window opens Credit: Getty

"We have the ambition to win, to win the Premier League, to win the Champions League, to win the domestic cups. And for that, we need top talent.



"So when we find the right opportunities, we will spend. But what we don't want to be doing is spending just for the sake of it."

United could reinforce their defence in the January transfer window to back their new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

talkSPORT understands that Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson is an option at Old Trafford.

The 29-year-old has been a long-term target for the club and worked with Pochettino at the United States men's national team.



His Fulham teammate Calvin Bassey is on their centre-back shortlist, as well as Brentford captain Nathan Collins.

Referee pick for Liverpool vs Manchester United

talkSPORT BET have priced the former Oxford and Luton boss as 5/4 favourite to be named the League One club's next permanent manager. A full odds list can be found here.

The Tangerines hierarchy are on the hunt for a new manager following the sacking of Evatt earlier in the week after a run of just one league since August, a streak spanning 10 matches, leaves them sat with only goal difference separating them from the relegation zone.

The Lancashire club had started the season well under Evatt, who had been at the club since last October, having also spent seven years at Bloomfield Road as a player, as the 45-year-old guided them to the top of the League One table three games into the campaign, with seven points from their opening few matches.

However, since the start of September, the Englishman could only manage a further five points from the following 10 matches, which now leaves down in 20th position and looking precariously over their shoulders rather than up the table.

Rather aptly, Bloomfield is the favourite to take over the Bloomfield Road hot seat. The 42-year-old has been out of a job since June after failing to keep Oxford in the Championship last season.

The Englishman has spent the majority of his footballing life on the books at Wycombe, representing them as a player for 18 years before working as a coach with the club following retirement and then spent two years as the Buckinghamshire side's manager from 2023 to 2025.

The majority of Bloomfield's management experience has come in League One, a division in which he has managed at least in part of the last four season, and where he had Wycombe in the automatic promotion places in January 2025 in his second full season in charge before packing his bags to head to Championship side Luton.
