Sports.title: Tom Brady in talks over buying Chelsea stake after cutting Birmingham ties
Sports.content:
Tom Brady in talks over buying Chelsea stake after cutting Birmingham ties

Tom Brady is in talks to buy a minority stake in Chelsea, talkSPORT understands.

The NFL legend is looking to invest in the Premier League giants after cutting ties with Birmingham City.



3 Brady is in talks to buy a stake in Chelsea after cutting ties with Birmingham Credit: Getty

Brady exited St. Andrew's earlier this month, three years after joining the Championship outfit as a minority investor.

He had also been working as an advisory board chairman for the club under owners Knighthead Capital.

During his time at the club, Blues won promotion back to the second-tier as League One champions in 2025.



Their title-winning campaign saw the club set a new EFL points record as they ended the campaign with 111 points.

Brady in Chelsea talks

Having departed Birmingham, though, Brady could now be set to join the ownership structure at Stamford Bridge.



The seven-time Super Bowl champion is in negotiations over purchasing a small stake in the Blues.

talkSPORT understands the sale of his Birmingham shares was done with investing in Chelsea in mind with talks said to have gone positively.



Brady was previously a guest of the club at the Club World Cup in the USA in 2025, a tournament that Chelsea won.

Meanwhile, he has a positive relationship with owner Behdad Eghbali.

Chelsea's parent company, BlueCo, are open to the idea of micro-investment if the right strategic partners present themselves with Brady viewed as someone who has an affinity with the club's brand.

3 Brady has a good relationship with Chelsea owner Eghbali Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Meanwhile, Chelsea's Women's Team adopted a similar strategy with NBA star Giannis Antetokounmpo acquiring a small stake in February.



The Iranian-American billionaire's Clearlake Capital has full control of Chelsea following Toddy Boehly and Mark Walter's exits in September.

Eghbali co-founded the private equity firm with Jose Feliciano in 2006.

Clearlake Capital co-led BlueCo's takeover of the club alongside Boehly four years ago.

As well as his ownership, Eghbali is currently one of six directors on the Blues' board.



Brady's sports investments

Brady could now be set to join Chelsea's ownership group amid his investment talks with the club.

3 Brady is widely regarded as one of the best quarterbacks in NFL history and has won seven Super Bowls Credit: Getty

As well as his time at Birmingham, he co-owns the Las Vegas Aces WNBA franchise.

Meanwhile, he also bought a minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders in 2024, sealing a return to the NFL.



Brady spent 22 years in the league with the New England Patriots and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

He is widely regarded as one of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history after being named Super Bowl MVP a record five times.

Sports.title: Man United CEO Omar Berrada breaks silence on Man City connection after guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada has said he is not concerned about being drawn into Manchester City's legal proceedings.

Berrada had worked with Man City from 2011 to 2024 in multiple roles before taking up his current position at Old Trafford.

2 Berrada (left) has spoken out about his old club Man City's guilty verdict after they were charged with breaching the Premier League's financial rules Credit: AFP

In 2011, he joined City and ran their international business department before working as their director of partnerships.

Then, from 2016, he was appointed Man City's chief operating and became chief football operations officer at City Football Group in 2020, a role he held up until his switch to Man United.

In September, City were found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018.

That means that their wrongdoings would have been taking place when Berrada was part of the club's hierarchy.

And he has now been asked whether he is worried about any punishment coming his way should City's appeal fail.

Berrada on City charges: "I wasn't involved"

"I'm not concerned," Berrada, who has not spoken publicly since June, said, in an interview with Sky Sports.

"I want to be very clear about this: I wasn't involved in any wrongdoings. I wasn't involved in the proceedings. There are no allegations against me.

"In that sense, there will be no surprises."

On potentially spear-heading any compensation claims against his old club with United, he added: "I don't want to comment on that because right now, it's an ongoing process.

"When it runs its course, then we'll take a view of what is our position as Manchester United."

2 Berrada (left) was part of Man City's hierarchy for almost all of the years they have been found guilty of breaching rules Credit: Getty

Had Berrada spoken about his City connection before?

After joining Man United in October 2024, questions were raised about any implications for him if City were found guilty.

Hearings had already started about the charges that year, so of course, questions were asked of Berrada's involvement.

It was reported at the time that United had asked the CEO whether he could be implicated at all before appointing him.

And it was also stated that the Red Devils were confident that no repercussions could come Berrard's way.

In fact, he said when asked about the potential for punishment at the time: “I can’t comment about my previous role.

"I’m fully focused on Man United, I think we have very strong foundations to continue growing, and to win without losing money.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta imposes ban on Arsenal players after one indirectly leaked team news
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta imposes ban on Arsenal players after one indirectly leaked team news

Mikel Arteta has banned Arsenal players from including themselves in their Fantasy Premier League teams.

The Gunners stars have also been told not to select their teammates in a bid to crack down on indirectly leaked team news.

3 Arteta has banned Arsenal players from including themselves or their teammates on FPL Credit: Getty

It comes after Christos Tzolis' inclusion in the starting line-up against Liverpool earlier this month was given away ahead of time.

Eagle-eyed fans spotted that the Greece international had brought himself back into his team as well as making himself captain.

The move all-but confirmed Tzolis was set to start at Anfield on November 1.

He went on to make his comeback in the 1-0 victory over Liverpool after missing six matches with a hamstring injury.

Tzolis started on the left-wing for the Gunners as they maintained their lead at the top of the table.

The summer signing had been sidelined since the start of October after sustaining an injury on international duty.

Arteta's FPL ban

Arteta is now desperate to avoid a repeat of his team selection becoming obvious prior to Premier League outings.

Speaking during his pre-match press conference on Friday, he explained: "With Christos, with the squad, with my kids as well.

"They are constantly asking me about the line-ups as well because they want to know.

"It's a topic. These are the kind of things that are happening in our society right now and it's something new, we haven't dealt with it and we have to put new things in place.

3 Tzolis indirectly leaked that he was set to start against Liverpool earlier this month Credit: Getty

"The confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and what you're trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret and we will take measures to make sure that doesn't happen."

When asked if those measures have now been taken, Arteta replied: "Yes."

Arsenal team news

Arsenal return to action away against Newcastle United on Saturday.

The two sides meet at St. James' Park, with kick-off at 5.30pm as the Gunners aim to extend their lead at the top of the table.

Arteta's side are currently five points clear of nearest challengers Brighton after winning nine of their opening ten matches.

Their defeat to the Seagulls in September remains the only blemish on their league record so far this term.

3 Arteta's side return to action away at Newcastle this weekend Credit: Getty

Ahead of the match, Arteta confirmed that Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are sidelined through injury.

Saka's lengthy absence is set to rule him out for another month, whilst the latter misses out after picking up a hamstring issue on international duty.

Meanwhile, William Saliba could make his long-awaited return to the side.

The defender has not featured so far this season having suffered a back injury in France's World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain in July.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino warns Man United cannot be stuck in the past as he sets out his vision for the club - and confirms Bruno Fernandes WILL remain captain amid contract stand-off
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino has warned that Manchester United cannot be stuck in the past as he begins the job of dragging the biggest club in English football out of the Premier League relegation zone.

Pochettino faces a huge first game in charge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, and he is determined to make a fresh start at United uninhibited by the history of the club.

‘We arrived with the idea to create something from scratch, from our own ideas and philosophy, in the way that we love to work. I think our job is to adapt and to go ahead a little bit,’ he said at Carrington.

‘The culture of the club and the identity of the club is very clear. It's an historic club with years being one of the best clubs in the world. It's difficult to find another club the size of Manchester United. It needs to be in a different place than we are now, no?

‘But I don't think too much in the past. If we want to create something different and positive, and the people feel proud about that, it's about building our own way here. Thinking on what happened yesterday is not going to help. You cannot be stuck in the past.’

Pochettino’s appointment at United has been a whirlwind after the Argentine oversaw his final two games in charge of the US national team before flying through the night to start work on Wednesday.

Mauricio Pochettino spoke to the media for the first time as Man United boss on Friday

‘I think it's a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool, and now our focus is 100 per cent on Liverpool,’ he added.

‘My first target is to sleep, but I cannot sleep – only three or four hours per day – but I think the target is to know the people, the staff, all the people here in the club, and of course the players and try from the beginning to have a positive impact.’

Pochettino admits he has missed being involved in day-to-day coaching at club level, saying: ‘Of course, we missed it a lot. We are animals of the grass. We like to feel the grass, we need to smell the grass and to help the players to improve every day.

‘It's true that it's a different job when you are in the national team, but I think we are much better coaches now.’

The 54-year-old told United that he wants to be involved in the all the key decision-making and transfers despite only being named as the club’s head coach.

Pochettino demanded more control during his five years in charge of Tottenham, and the difference between manager and head coach has also been a bone of contention at United in recent years.

Manchester United travel to rivals Liverpool on Sunday searching for their first league win since August

Ruben Amorim was sacked after taking on the United hierarchy over his job title, while Erik ten Hag refused to give up his power to veto transfers.

Pochettino said: ‘I know that being a head coach, I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday and I'm going to pick the starting 11.

‘I'm going to make the changes and of course that, in the future, I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen in the squad. That is (why) in the end, Manchester United is a football club, no?

‘During all my (career), when I started at Espanyol, head coach, coach, manager. In the end, it's not changing too much because I think the way that we work is indifferent to the title description.

‘If you are manager it’s not necessarily that you have all the decisions. Maybe you are a coach and have more power in the decision.’

Pochettino revealed that he met most of the players individually at Carrington on Thursday, including captain Bruno Fernandes who cut a frustrated figure towards the end of Michael Carrick’s time in charge.

Pochettino confirmed that out-of-form Bruno Fernandes will remain as United captain

‘Bruno is our captain and I think he's a very important player, but all the players need to feel that they are important from the top to the bottom,’ said Pochettino.

‘Yesterday we spent three hours chatting in an individual way in my office with all the players.’

Concerns have been raised over the players’ fitness and attitude under Carrick this season, with the statistics suggesting that United have not been running enough.

‘That's a good question, no?,’ said Pochettino. ‘It’s a debate that I don't like to go into because I think we cannot talk about things without context, and data is about context. I think it's very dangerous to talk. We are here not to denounce things, we are here to build something.’

Pochettino later shared a message on Instagram thanking supporters for their 'warm welcome' and declared the Red Devils 'cannot afford to waste a moment'.

'An intense first few days. Thank you to everyone for a warm welcome,' the Argentine wrote.

'We cannot afford to waste a moment. All our energy and attention is focused on preparing for Sunday.

'We can say many things, but what matters is the work we do and what we show on the pitch.'

Sports.title: Man United chief Omar Berrada distances himself from Man City's Premier League charges - as Enzo Maresca insists his stars are unaffected by guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has insisted he was not involved in any wrongdoing at his former club Manchester City – but refused to rule out taking action against them if their appeal fails.

In his first sit-down interview in five months, broadcast on Friday, Berrada tackled a range of topics concerning United but his links to City, from whom he joined United in 2024, were also brought up. He worked at the club during some of the period that City were found to have broken Premier League rules.

Back in September, an independent regulatory commission found City guilty of a multitude of charges brought against them by the Premier League, with financial offences ranging between 2009 and 2018.

The scathing verdict determined that City had 'artificially inflated' their revenues and reduced costs through 'disguised funding' schemes such as 'sham' contracts.

Berrada joined City in 2011 before going on to become their chief operating officer in 2016, raising questions over whether he could end up implicated if City – who vehemently contest the charges – fail in their appeal.

'I'm not concerned,' Berrada insisted. 'I want to be very clear about this, right. I wasn't involved in any wrongdoings. I wasn't involved in the proceedings; there are no allegations against me, and in that sense there will be no surprises.'

Asked if United would push for compensation should City's guilty verdict be upheld on appeal, Berrada remained tight-lipped.

Omar Berrada joined Manchester City in 2011... and moved across the city 13 years later

Berrada has become one of the main sources of anger among United fans who have campaigned against the owners and the board

'I don't want to comment on that because right now it's an ongoing process,' he added. 'When it runs its course we'll take our view of where is our position as Manchester United.'

Berrada was not used as a witness in the original investigation and there are no allegations directed specifically to the now-United CEO.

City boss Enzo Maresca, meanwhile, insisted that the guilty verdicts handed down to Manchester City for financial chicanery have not affected his players despite three consecutive Premier League defeats.

City fell six points behind defending champions Arsenal in the weeks before this month’s international break amid a slew of individual high-profile errors that led to claims of Maresca’s squad being preoccupied by the uncertainty surrounding the club.

The Premier League have a range of available sanctions to them were City to lose an appeal set for next month. Those would likely result in relegation to the Championship.

But Maresca does not equate that looming doomsday backdrop with a worrying run of form before they face Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday lunchtime.

‘I don't think the players are thinking too much about that,’ Maresca said. ‘If we want to relate the noise with the defeats, look at [Aston] Villa away. We had so many chances, for instance Iliman [Ndiaye] hit the post, or Brighton where the keeper was man of the match.

Enzo Maresca insists his stars are not thinking about the impact of the guilty verdict

Erling Haaland says he is 'incredibly' happy to be a City player and tops the Premier League scoring charts with nine so far this campaign

‘Then [Nottingham] Forest when Erling [Haaland] had the chance to score for 2-2. I don't think the players are focused on the noise. I don't think they are worried about that.’

Haaland claimed to be ‘incredibly happy’ about being a City player in a defiant interview with Norwegian television earlier in the week, although few others have addressed the problems publicly.

Marc Guehi has previously said the players are ‘relaxed’, while Phil Foden refused to discuss it when asked.

Maresca has spent the past fortnight analysing City’s ten league matches and has admitted that the team requires more balance after conceding too many goals to turnovers or counter attacks.

‘I was not thinking that we were doing everything well when we were winning games and I'm not thinking that we did everything wrong when we lost games,’ the Italian added.

‘For me it is the beginning of something long. I think we are attacking well because we are creating chances and overall we are controlling games.

‘There are moments we are not controlling and we have to realise the reasons why and do better. We are conceding goals and most are avoidable from my point of view.’

There have been occasions – like the first goal at Forest – when City’s building from the back has put them in serious trouble. Josko Gvardiol lost the ball at the City Ground after no midfielder had shown for possession.

Maresca said: ‘We reviewed things during the break. The idea is to continue to attack in the same way and try to find the balance when we defend or when we are building like what happened for the first goal against Forest.

‘When you are building and you lose the ball in the build-up it's difficult to build with that.’

Sports.title: Chelsea slapped with huge £150,000 fine after 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' fan chants in last season's FA Cup tie at Charlton
Sports.content:
Chelsea have been slapped with a significant £150,000 fine by the Football Association for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic more than ten months ago.

It was alleged that in the 56th minute, the visiting supporters at the Valley sang ‘f*** the Pope and the IRA’. A charge followed, and Chelsea were hit with their fine, along with being given an action plan to follow and a formal warning as to their future conduct.

Chelsea tried to appeal being fined £150,000 for the sectarian chanting. They wanted it either removed completely, or at least substantially reduced.

The club attempted to argue that it was excessive despite admitting that approximately 2,500 of their fans may have taken part in the offensive singing. They also noted how Millwall were previously not fined for the same chant occurring.

Their appeal was dismissed and the full scale of their punishment was upheld.

In a statement, Chelsea said of the chanting: ‘We unequivocally condemn this behaviour. Sectarian abuse – chanting that creates division targeted towards a particular religious or political group – and discriminatory language of any kind has no place in our football club.

Chelsea have been hit with a £150,000 fine for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic back in January

CHELSEA STILL WITHOUT JOAO PEDRO Leeds United have been handed a big boost as Chelsea will go into their Saturday clash without their star striker Joao Pedro, who has yet to return to training. Since the Brazilian was sidelined, Chelsea have won only one of their three Premier League games played, beating a beleaguered Manchester United under Michael Carrick. Otherwise, they have lost to Tottenham Hotspur and Sunderland without scoring. Joao Pedro is still nursing a thigh problem, and has not yet made it outside with his team-mates as Leeds visit Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Chelsea will, however, have Moises Caicedo available after his injury scare during the international break with Ecuador. ‘He's not fit yet to train with the team, so we need to wait a bit longer,’ Alonso confirmed on Joao Pedro. He’s not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see game by game how he's feeling. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.’ Chelsea will have Emiliano Martinez available after recovering from his broken jaw suffered at Everton on October 17. The goalkeeper required surgery following his collision with Jarrad Branthwaite. Alonso confirmed he no longer needs to wear a mask, having been training without it, and the 34-year-old Argentinian could be in line for his first club appearance since his injury. On Mike Penders, the 21-year-old Belgian who largely impressed while filling in for Martinez, Alonso said: ‘Mike has done very good things. We know the progression he had, that he overcame a difficult moment for sure after the first game (against Tottenham), but after he's done better. He’s improving and with these minutes his development has been good.’ There is some confusion among Chelsea supporters as to the type of football that Alonso wants to see. When asked to explain his desired identity, the Spaniard did not quite tell us what it is. ‘We are building it,’ he said. ‘This is a process, this is a goal for us. We feel that this is our idea of how we want to play, knowing the context, knowing the Premier League, that we are prepared with whoever we are facing and that we are competitive.’

‘Such behaviour only serves to cause hurt to others and does not represent the values we hold as a club. We want to create a safe and inclusive environment for all, and we have a shared responsibility in delivering this.’

They added: ‘We understand that further incidents risk additional sanctions against the club and are doing everything we can to inform and educate supporters, as well as develop our existing initiatives to prevent, detect and respond to discrimination in future. We know Chelsea fans do not want to see any form of discrimination in our game, and we ask for their support in fostering a welcoming environment at Chelsea matches going forward.’

Sports.title: Jack Grealish's Everton olive branch: Star IS available to return to first team after being axed for skipping training without permission in 'breach of club discipline'
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish's Everton olive branch: Star IS available to return to first team after being axed for skipping training without permission in 'breach of club discipline'

Jack Grealish has been offered an olive branch by Everton boss David Moyes and the sanctioned star is available for selection this weekend.

The Manchester City loanee was punished by the club for failing to report to training sessions and missed several matches. He has not featured for four games: one because of illness, then a ‘breach of club discipline’ and a lack of fitness thereafter.

But Grealish will be considered for the squad when the in-form Toffees travel to Brentford on Monday night. Moyes confirmed Grealish is fit and available, saying: 'He’s back in training and back in and around the team.'

The 31-year-old issued a public apology on Instagram, to which Moyes said: 'I don’t do social media but I’ve heard about it.'

On whether the pair have held talks, the Scot added: 'We’ve just been getting on with our work.

'We’ve got a lot of other players who I need to put a lot of focus on as well, I can’t just concentrate on one player. I’ve been trying to make sure that everybody’s getting the right preparation and getting ready for our next game against Brentford.'

Jack Grealish is available for Everton again after serving his punishment and regaining fitness

A presentation from Blues past and present. 🤝



Leon Osman and James Tarkowski surprise David Moyes with a memento as he sets a new record for games managed for Everton Football Club (593). 💙 pic.twitter.com/tzFuGeUhFW — Everton (@Everton) November 20, 2026

Grealish's social media apology came after he featured in a behind-closed-doors match during the international break.

'Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training!' Grealish wrote. 'I want to apologise to the fans (and) everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

'I love playing for this club (and) can't wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt.

'See you all soon (blue heart)'.

Everton have won their last three games and go into Monday’s match sixth in the table.

At the start of his press conference Moyes was presented with a framed memento of his time in charge by defender James Tarkowski and former player Leon Osman after he set a new club record of 593 games in the hotseat.

Moyes said: 'It’s something that I’m really thrilled about but, if I’m being honest, it’s not something I really think about. I understand I’ve suddenly become the manager who’s had more games at Everton than anybody before and that’s a real honour and privilege to be put in that position.'

Sports.title: 'He was his twin's carer from the word go': Will Joseph's parents reveal astonishing backstory of new England hero who's deaf in one ear, their Twickenham tears seeing his five tries against Japan and why he thought he'd never win another cap
Sports.content:
'He was his twin's carer from the word go': Will Joseph's parents reveal astonishing backstory of new England hero who's deaf in one ear, their Twickenham tears seeing his five tries against Japan and why he thought he'd never win another cap

To truly understand the making of England's new try-scoring superstar Will Joseph you must begin with his twin brother, Alex.

Alex has learning difficulties and epilepsy so Will – or William as he is to his mother, Philippa – had to learn how to muck in from an early age.

It goes some of the way to explaining why their father, Ivan, had a tear in his eye after watching Will score five tries at Twickenham in England's victory over Japan last Saturday.

'William has been Alex's carer from the word go,' Philippa tells me on the phone this week. 'As far as William's living memory goes, he's always been there and looked after Alex. He's a humble, kind person because his default has always been to make sure Alex is OK.

'During breaktimes at primary school, Will would spend half of the time getting Alex's coat on or off,' adds Ivan.

'He didn't get much of a break himself. That nurturing means he has always put others before himself. That's shaped him into the person we see today.'

Will Joseph touches down spectacularly during his dazzling five-try performance against Japan last weekend at Twickenham

(From left), Will Joseph with his sister Hannah and brothers Alex and Jonathan

Will is the latest sporting success story in the Joseph family. His sister, Hannah, plays netball for England and their eldest brother, Jonathan, the former centre, won 54 Test caps and toured New Zealand with the British & Irish Lions.

Will and Jonathan are identikit players despite the 11-year age gap. Both stand 6ft tall, have similar jawlines, cover centre and wing and they have the same hop and glide across the pitch. As of last Saturday, they have both scored Test hat-tricks for England.

'It's quite interesting how they've ended up in the same place when their journeys have been quite different,' explains Philippa. 'With Jonathan, we lived in a small house in Derby without much space. William grew up in the south when we were 10 or 15 years further on and much more established as a family.

'Both William and Jonathan played a lot of tennis. As the first-born, Jonathan would have all the kit, the big Wilson bag, and I'd be there watching with two little boys in the pushchair. Everything was set up for him to succeed.

'Because of the family dynamic with Alex, William pretty much had to get on with it himself. He couldn't be needy, he had to fit in. He had very, very different parenting.'

As a youngster, Jonathan was often chasing a rugby ball down the touchlines at Derby RFC, where Ivan played until he was 40. Will spent his youth following his brother's career. He flew out to Italy with the family to watch Jonathan play alongside a host of future Test stars for England in the Under 18s World Cup.

'William grew up around these kinds of people, having rugby balls thrown at him in all directions,' says Philippa. 'We used to have these parallel sofas in the lounge. Hannah would be lying on one sofa, Jonathan on the other, and they would launch balls at each other while they watched TV.

'William would be in the middle of it all, 14 months old, running around in a nappy trying to catch this funny-shaped ball.

'The family were obsessed with sport so it was just the norm for William,' says his mum Philippa

Joseph puts the hard work in during England training at Pennyhill Park

'The family were obsessed with sport so it was just the norm for William. Because of Jonathan, he spent a lot of his younger years with friends and family at Twickenham, chatting to famous rugby players.

'When he joined George Ford in England camp, he said, 'It's so weird because I just remember coming out to watch you playing for England Under 18s in Italy when I was at primary school'.'

Like Jonathan, William was enrolled at the famous rugby breeding ground of Millfield School in Somerset. From the age of 13, he was mentored by London Irish academy coach James Lightfoot-Brown, who is now his club coach at Gloucester.

'I played with JJ a couple of times in the London Irish academy and I couldn't believe the obvious physical similarities,' says Lightfoot-Brown. 'Knowing what JJ had done, we had a great opportunity to mould Will's game around that.

'His family were incredibly supportive. They had a little camper van that they'd all travel down to training in. They had a lot of love and care for London Irish because of what JJ had been through there.'

Yet for all of their physical similarities, the siblings have contrasting personalities. 'When Jonathan was growing up, he had an air of confidence,' says Ivan. 'I wouldn't call it arrogance, but he feared nobody. He thought he could beat anybody.

'Generally speaking, Will is quite a humble individual. But there was one occasion around 2016, when he was 11 or 12 and Jonathan was playing for Bath. We were in the marquee behind the stand, with some fellow Bath supporters, and J had a good game.

'Will always carried a ball around with him, just like J did, and this lady, an estate agent, asked him: 'Do you think you'll be as good as your brother when you grow up?' He responded: 'I'll be better than him.'

'As a kid Will (left) was asked: 'Do you think you'll be as good as your brother when you grow up?' He responded: 'I'll be better than him''

Joseph earned a surprise England call-up from Eddie Jones as an apprentice in 2022. He was capped against Australia a week before his 20th birthday

'Will always appeared humble and meek and mild, but that showed me there was a burning fire in there. His confidence is internalised. He has a lot of inner strength.'

Will excelled through age-group rugby. He broke into the London Irish first team as a teenager, earning a surprise England call-up from Eddie Jones as an apprentice in 2022. He was capped against Australia a week before his 20th birthday but the following season his club were declared bankrupt.

'Will was on a really positive trajectory at London Irish,' says Lightfoot-Brown. 'If the club hadn't gone under, we would have seen him excelling in an England shirt far sooner.

'I've seen him do some things on rugby pitches that other people simply aren't capable of. From the Wellington Under 15s festival, where he could just run around everyone, to some of the moments he had for London Irish.

'We had Will and Henry Arundell coming off the bench and ripping up games. It was frightening. He's so fast but he's not just someone who can run with the ball. He's a 13 who can play on the wing at a very high level.'

Will moved to Harlequins after London Irish went bankrupt, although he struggled to break into the team. He suffered setbacks – including becoming deaf in his left ear – and eventually relocated to Gloucester with his team-mate and house-mate, Will Trenholm.

'He's needed to be resilient because he's gone through a hard time,' says back-rower Trenholm. 'He nearly got a hearing aid because of a problem with his ear. It happened during a pool session at Quins. He came out of the water and his ear just wouldn't pop.

Joseph has been one of the PREM's standout performers with Gloucester this season

Joseph takes his time to score the second of his five tries against Japan on Saturday

'He thought he had liquid in it and it was a bit quieter for the first few days. It got worse over time so he went to the doctors. They tried to sort it out but it got slowly worse to the point where he's now deaf in his left ear.

'If you watch his post-match interviews after the Japan game, you can see that he has to lean in with his right ear. The answer he gave to the second question had nothing to do with the question they asked!

'Sometimes you have to repeat the call to him on the pitch. He'll have to run up and double check. He obviously prefers being on the left wing. I asked him if it affected his balance at all. It did at the start but he's adapted to it brilliantly. He doesn't really think about it too much now.'

Will has been one of the PREM's standout performers this season with Gloucester, who have been the surprise package and sit second through five rounds after finishing eighth last year. He has wowed team-mates with his ability to light up the pitch, second only to Immanuel Feyi-Waboso for defenders beaten per carry.

'The way he moves just reminds me of JJ... I keep thinking JJ's outside of me!' says England centre Henry Slade, who has now played Test rugby alongside both Joseph brothers.

'I know JJ really well. I played for a number of years with him. It's cool that I'm getting to do it with his brother now. The way they move is so similar, both of them are such incredible athletes.

'Will's very, very fast – winger speed so really, really quick. He's an incredible talent, we've just got to get him the ball and let him do some damage.'

Will with his family, most of whom were at Twickenham last weekend to cheer him on

'Will is humble and kind because his default has always been to make sure his brother Alex is OK. That's shaped him into the person we see today'

Borthwick wants 'fire' from England against All Blacks Steve Borthwick has urged his England stars to 'bring the fire' in Saturday's crunch Nations Championship clash with a wounded New Zealand. After impressive wins over Australia and Japan, the national team face their toughest challenge of the autumn so far with the All Blacks next up. Dave Rennie's side are reeling after a first loss to Wales in 73 years, but have recalled their big guns for the visit to Twickenham. England head coach Borthwick has vowed his team will be bang up for the test after he named George Furbank and Seb Atkinson in a strong starting XV. 'I see the players bring fire and pride when they're wearing their club shirts,' Borthwick said. 'I want them to bring that in an England shirt. I've been really pleased with how the players have started the games. 'Emotion is a key part. I sense the players are physically ready to go, but also mentally. These last couple of weekends, the players have produced performances that have made their families proud and the England fans proud. 'We want to make sure we put out that level of performance this weekend. We know it's going to be a fierce encounter and we know what a quality side New Zealand are.' Full-back Furbank, centre Atkinson and flanker Ollie Chessum have all been recalled for the All Blacks after missing the hammering of Japan due to injury. So too is No 10 Fin Smith, who is back to lead the team. Borthwick's XV this weekend is the same as that which put 45 points on Australia, except for Will Joseph who replaces the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso on the wing after scoring five times against Japan. New Zealand have global superstars Will Jordan, Jordie Barrett, Damian McKenzie and Codie Taylor back for England after they missed their shock loss in Cardiff. In November last year, England produced one of their impressive performances under Borthwick to beat the All Blacks 33-19. Now, the task is to produce a repeat. A big New Zealand response is expected. Of the 47 past meetings between the two teams, England have won just nine. 'It would be disingenuous for me say that when the team's playing New Zealand, the players don't feel the excitement every rugby fan feels,' Borthwick said. 'They are an incredible team. They have such a rich history and the games between England and New Zealand have been quite tight between the two teams over the last few years now. We came out on the right side a year ago and we came out on the wrong side the year before that, on three occasions. The players are super excited, as are the fans. 'That's always the case in games like this. I've looked at their (New Zealand's) last number of games closely. 'What I think they've done this week is name a team of experience with as many caps they could. That's the changes they've made. They're a very different team. It's a very different proposition of a team this week.' By Alex Bywater

Apart from Alex, the whole family were at Twickenham to watch Will's breakthrough appearance last weekend. 'Alex stayed at home with a carer,' says Ivan. 'He's not that much into rugby. Music is what makes Alex tick.

'He's a big Michael Jackson fan, and he always listens to music. So that's his thing. He's aware of rugby. He says, 'My brother plays for England' but it doesn't rock his boat, as it were.'

Philippa adds: 'Alex had uncontrolled seizures until about six months ago. We're now going through a phase where we've got really good control. For the first time in about four years, he's able to do things that he enjoys doing.

'We take Alex to these daytime nightclubs. There was a Michael Jackson tribute event in Oxford recently. As a good brother, William did his bit and came along. We all try to support each other and they all do their bit to support Alex.

'Until the rugby took off, that's what we were doing on Saturday afternoons. Now we're coming along to support William playing for England. What he's achieved is quite remarkable. I'm overwhelmed with pride.'

'It feels like deja vu, to a certain extent,' says Ivan. 'Because we've gone through all of this with Jonathan, we know what's coming. For Will, it feels like time has been suspended for four years since his first cap. He pointed out that the bedrooms at Pennyhill Park haven't changed much.

'I was close to tears after the game on Saturday. I've seen him slouched on the sofa, watching the game on TV, wishing that he could be out there. Four years between Tests is a long time.

Will celebrates with his father Ivan and sister Hannah at Twickenham last weekend. 'I was close to tears after the game,' says Ivan

'A lot has happened during that time. He didn't know if his time would come again. It's been one thing after another for Will. He's had to quietly build himself back up.

'Two years ago, I was diagnosed with early-onset Parkinson's. It's a shortage of dopamine in the brain but the medication I'm on is basically compensating for that. My life hasn't changed significantly and watching Will's success brings me great pleasure.'

Pride is the overwhelming feeling in the Joseph family. For so much of his life, Will has been the one looking out for others. Now, after all of the challenges, it is his turn to enjoy his moment in the spotlight.

And in English rugby, the spotlight doesn't shine much brighter than this Saturday when the All Blacks come to Twickenham.

Sports.title: Man United CEO Omar Berrada insists the team have IMPROVED since the transfer window in his first interview in five months - but does accept criticism of leadership has been fair
Sports.content:
Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada insists the team got 'fundamentally better' after this summer's transfer window, as he warned ‘spending just for the sake of it’ is not the route to putting United back on top.

In his first sit-down interview in five months, Berrada tackled topics ranging from the relationship between the Glazers and Ineos, the imminent departure of youngster JJ Gabriel, the decision not to sign a left back in the summer, as well as the decision to push ahead for a new stadium despite supporter backlash on matchdays.

The United chief has been at the centre of furious protests and anti-ownership chanting at matches this season, alongside Director of Football Jason Wilcox, and he accepted that criticism of United's leadership has, mostly, been fair.

In an interview that aired shortly after new head coach Mauricio Pochettino spoke to the media for the first time, Berrada was pressed on how much accountability falls at his door with United heading to Anfield this weekend 18th in the Premier League table.

'I think if you think about the fact we've had three permanent managers in less than three seasons, clearly we haven't achieved the stability that we wanted, that's for sure,' Berrada told Sky Sports.

'When it doesn't work out with the coach or the manager, we are all responsible. Myself, the football leadership, everyone who is involved around the coach and the staff and the players. We have to continue improving and getting better.

Manchester United's CEO Omar Berrada finally fronted up in an interview with Sky Sports

Michael Carrick's sacking was yet another managerial change at United, with the hierarchy under massive scrutiny and Mauricio Pochettino now in the hotseat

'There are different circumstances why it didn't work out with Erik [ten Hag], and Ruben [Amorim], and now Michael [Carrick], and we are always learning and, as I said, trying to improve and understand what has failed.

'The challenge is we're trying to find the right manager for the squad that we have with a specific set of skills in that moment to make them perform at their best level.

'It's true, we have to accept the criticism that we haven't been able to achieve that stability with one coach and our aim is to do that as soon as possible. Of course, we hope now that Mauricio coming in will give us that stability that I think we all need.'

Berrada's links to Manchester City, where he worked prior to joining United, were brought up, not least given he worked at the club during the period that City have had charges brought against them.

'I'm not concerned,' Berrada insisted.

But at his new home there are issues aplenty, not least having got another managerial appointment wrong, sacking Carrick less than six months after handing him a two-year deal, and so it was put to Berrada: is the club actually progressing?

'It's not good enough, not acceptable and that's why we've made the change that we made so that we can move forward,' he concluded.

(L-R) Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Berrada and Jason Wilcox have drawn plenty of ire from Man United fans

'But we are laying the foundations for sustained growth, to put us in a position where we can be competitive consistently. It's not always been that.

'Last year we finished third, we were happy with the squad, we were happy with the way we were going. And now, a few months later, we are not where we need to be. But the foundations are there and I am convinced that we are heading in the right direction. Very positive.'

Sports.title: Huge crowd gathers for funeral of Irish boxer Lee Reeves after he passed away following knockout in the ring and three-month coma
Sports.content:
Huge crowd gathers for funeral of Irish boxer Lee Reeves after he passed away following knockout in the ring and three-month coma

Huge crowds have gathered today for the funeral of Irish boxer Lee Reeves who died this week.

The 31-year-old died in hospital on Monday after being placed in a medically induced coma following a fight in August.

After being knocked down twice in the 10th round, the Irish southpaw was carried from the ring on a stretcher following his defeat to fellow countryman Gary Cully and taken to hospital.

His promoters, Queensberry, later revealed he was in a 'critical but stable' condition before undergoing surgery.

Reeves was then placed in an induced coma, where he remained until his death three months later, surrounded by his family.

Along with being a professional boxer, Reeves was a serving member of the 12th Infantry Battalion out of Sarsfield Barracks, an ambassador for Limerick Treaty Suicide Prevention and a model.

A large crowd gathered at the Church of Our Lady, Queen of Peace for the funeral mass in Roxboro, Limerick, on Friday, with thousands also tuning in to a livestream of the service.

Dreams by The Cranberries played in the church as the coffin carrying Reeves' body, draped in the Irish tricolour, was carried inside.

Irish boxer Lee Reeves died on Monday after spending three months in a medically-induced coma

Family members accompanied the hearse carrying the coffin of boxer Lee Reeves arriving at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, for his funeral with full military honours on Friday

Members of the Irish Defence Forces carry the coffin of boxer Reeves out of Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, on Friday

It had been brought to the church on an adapted gun carriage, as part of the military honours for the service.

His Defence Forces cap was also placed on the coffin.

Reeves' boxing gloves and belt, his Bible, and a pizza box were among items placed at the altar to represent his interests including his love of his religion – along with photographs of the Limerick-born boxer.

The mass heard tributes from some of his four sisters: Louise, Shannon, Jodie and Jessie, who described him as 'one of the greatest men on this earth' and 'an inspiration to everyone he met'.

Jodie told the funeral mass that Reeves was a family man who 'did everything' for his sisters.

'He was my mother's whole life, and she was his. He dedicated every fight to her, and no doubt made her proud.

'She was his number one supporter from day one.

'You were a father to us all, and that even includes Dad.'

She added: 'Nothing is going to be the same without you around, but I promise you'll never be forgotten.'

Jodie, also reading a tribute from Reeves' father, said: 'You had a heart and a presence that touched so many lives.'

Continuing that tribute, she added: 'God knows how much we will miss you, and how much of a piece of our hearts will go with you. Rest easy, son.'

Reeves had been carried out of the ring on a stretcher after his defeat to his countryman Gary Cully and taken to hospital (Source: Instagram/Lee Reeves)

A car is pictured following the funeral cortege of Reeves as it leaves Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, after his funeral mass on Friday

Wreaths and tributes are seen on display before the funeral of boxer Lee Reeves at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick,on Friday

Shannon said: 'I will miss you every day that I'm on this earth.'

She added: 'You never deserved this, brother, but it's not the end.

'Your story will live on, and your legacy will live on.'

Outside, a large screen and several framed photographs depicted images of Reeves and his loved ones as well as his boxing gloves.

The images carried captions such as 'brother', 'son', 'nephew', 'uncle' and 'pride of Limerick'.

Attendees included Mayor of Limerick John Horan as well as Defence Forces colleagues including the General Officer Commanding 1 Brigade, Brigadier General Caimin Keogh and Officer Commanding 12th Infantry Battalion, Lieutenant Colonel Ian Harrington.

Reeves was placed in a medically-induced coma and had emergency surgery after a junior welterweight fight in Dublin on August 1.

He had won 16 of his 18 bouts after turning professional in 2018, with several of his fights in Canada and Colombia.

The hearse is pictured carrying the coffin of boxer Lee Reeves arriving at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, for his funeral with full military honours, on Friday

Family members stand behind as soldiers from the Irish Defence Forces place the coffin of boxer and serving soldier Reeves on an adapted gun carriage at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, on Friday

Reeves' August clash with final opponent Gary Cully saw the 31-year-old knocked down twice in the 10th round

He was also a contestant on BBC reality show, Survivor, in 2023.

Defence Forces head chaplain Fr Paschal Hanrahan said Reeves showed physical courage in the boxing ring but also moral, courage and integrity in his mental health advocacy.

'We hold in our prayers today his colleagues serving overseas at this time with the 128th Infantry Battalion in Unifil, along with their chaplain Fr Piotr, who I know are gathered at this very moment in prayer for Lee.

'With all the agility and dexterity of a professional boxer, Lee moves seamlessly from being a model to being a role model in the Defence Forces.

'And those who served with him in Sarsfield Barracks saw our Defence Forces values in the way that he lived.'

He added: 'They saw his respect in the way he treated people, his loyalty in the way he stood by his comrades, and his selflessness in the time he gave to those who needed encouragement.'

Reeves, who was nicknamed 'El Champo', had won 16 of his 18 professional bouts since turning professional in 2018, and had been challenging Cully for the vacant BUI Celtic light-welterweight title.

He had been knocked down twice in the 10th round against Cully before being taken out of the ring, and in his tribute message for his opponent, Cully admitted that he was still in shock at how their match had ended.

Members of the Irish Defence Forces walked in procession alongside the coffin of boxer and soldier Reeves on an adapted gun carriage at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, on Friday

'I still remember the stadium days when I used to watch Lee in the nationals, the weight above me, and (I would) always be impressed by his fights and his flashy gear,' Cully wrote.

'What a character and a gent. It's never been nothing but love between us champ, can't really believe I'm writing this but RIP brother.'

Sports.title: How Mykhailo Mudryk's unsolicited interview turned into a moany mess: With gaffes galore - including his Arsenal 'dream' - the £89m man hasn't endeared himself to either Spurs or Chelsea, writes KIERAN GILL
Sports.content:
Not for the first time, Mykhailo Mudryk was in a good position, and displayed poor judgement. This time, it was away from the pitch, in a two-hour, sit-down, tell-all interview involving gaffes galore.

Criticising London for its 20mph speed limit, saying 'it's hard to follow these rules, however much I'd like to' after his latest driving ban, and how the wealthy are taxed 45 per cent on these shores.

Naming 'Ukraine' when asked which is the best city in the world – he may have misunderstood the question, so we will let him off with that one – and admitting he signed contracts without reading them while denouncing the deals done by his former representatives.

Then there was his interviewer, a grinning chap called Dmitry Gordon, asking him if he speaks to his four cats in English, and why he wears earrings, and if girls send him pictures. Bizarre enquiries. Had Chelsea or Tottenham Hotspur known about this interview happening – and Daily Mail Sport understands they were not informed – then we cannot imagine either Premier League club would have liked such lines of questioning.

Nor will they, or their fanbases, be too fond of the 25-year-old Ukrainian explaining his move to England in the first place. He revealed how much he wanted to play for Arsenal, describing it as his 'dream' as he blamed his old agent for pushing him to Chelsea for the money.

What was supposed to be an opportunity for Mudryk to tell his side of the story, after a doping ban which cost him two years of his career, resembled more of a moany mess.

Mykhailo Mudryk's interview was a bizarre mess and showed his utter naivety

The Ukrainian winger was given a one-year driving ban in December last year

By the end, the seriousness of his allegations against the Ukrainian national team with regard to his failed drugs test were softened by the nonsensical own goals much more likely to set social media alight.

Such as the naivety of a Chelsea player on loan at Tottenham appearing to pine for Arsenal, and saying he still wants to win the Ballon d'Or, which is only ever an admission prone to being patronised online even if a sign of his ambition.

A reminder: Mudryk signed for Chelsea from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023 for £89million. He struggled, never looked like a winger worth such a fee. Frighteningly fast, but did not know how to use his weaponry properly in the Premier League. Graham Potter was his manager when he arrived. A few months later, it was Frank Lampard. A month after that, Mauricio Pochettino.

Then he was suspended for two years, during which time Chelsea supported his insistence that he was innocent and continued to pay his salary, believed to be worth around £100,000 per week.

While banned, he turned up in Wroclaw, Poland the day before the 2025 Conference League final, apparently there to collect his medal in case Chelsea won. Enzo Maresca was unaware, only learning that he was in the city when we told him at his pre-match press conference.

Upon Mudryk's return to football in the summer of 2026, Chelsea decided he needed to leave on loan, and another one of the Premier League's big-six sides gave him his second chance.

Tottenham called. Brentford, Brighton, Leeds and Coventry were among those also willing, but Roberto De Zerbi promised to give him a platform to prove his talents.

He appeared once, as a 74th-minute substitute away at Nottingham Forest in September. Then he disappeared, injured, and his only sighting since has been here, on YouTube, as a 'Guest of Gordon'.

Chelsea will also be unhappy about Mudryk's interview and were not informed about it

De Zerbi defends injured Mudryk Mykhailo Mudryk's is still two weeks away from a Tottenham return after a suffering setback to his recovery from an ankle injury. Mudryk, who has played only 16 minutes since joining on loan from Chelsea, clashed with the Ukrainian FA this week when he blamed them for his positive drug test which ruled him out of football for almost two years. He also risked the wrath of Spurs fans by admitting he only made the move across London to recover his fitness before returning to Stamford Bridge where Blues boss Xabi Alonso was 'counting on him'. And he managed to annoy both Chelsea and Spurs fans by revealing, during the same YouTube interview, that he wanted to sign for Arsenal when he moved to the Premier League in January 2023 but his agent forced through the move with the best commission. 'I can understand the fans, but Mudryk is a good guy,' said Spurs boss De Zerbi, who worked with the Ukraine international at Shakhtar Dontetsk and convinced him to resist interest from Brentford and Coventry and be reunited in North London. 'He's a good player. He suffered a lot for the situation in the last couple of years. He has just one thing to do, show on the pitch his qualities, show on the pitch that now he's playing for Tottenham. Tottenham is a big club, like the other clubs, not less at all.' Chelsea paid £86million for Mudryk but he made little impression before he was hit with a four-year ban in 2024, which was wiped out this summer enabling him to return to competition. 'He has no responsibility in this part,' said De Zerbi. 'Now his focus is just on the ball or just on the football. He has a big chance to play with us because Tottenham is a big club. He knows very well the coach, he knows very well the style of play. 'He knows I give him total confidence to show what he is. So to move the focus in the right direction, in a good direction. But I think he's working hard to recover and to play earlier.' Mudryk made his Spurs debut as a sub at Nottingham Forest in September but injured an ankle in training a few days later. He was initially expected to be out for two months with Saturday's game against Ipswich his target to return. 'The plan was to be available for Ipswich or Sunderland,' said De Zerbi, who will serve a touchline ban against Ipswich for three yellow cards. 'Then he felt not pain but he was not comfortable last week. And they take two weeks more, and step by step we're going to see the situation.' By Matt Barlow

While there should be sympathy with Mudryk, who had to bite his tongue while banned and spending what he described as 'millions' on trying to clear his name, he made a poor choice in the platform chosen to finally speak up.

At one stage, he is asked bluntly whether he considered killing himself. 'No, that's not a way out,' he replied. The title of the video on YouTube, unhelpfully, mentions 'suicidal thoughts' regardless of his answer.

Mudryk may have thought it would help to talk so openly, especially to clarify those he holds responsible for the two years he lost as a footballer.

But he hardly endeared himself to his current club, Tottenham, or to his parent club, Chelsea, to whom he is still contracted into the 2030s.

He likened them to chaos, explaining: 'I came to a Chelsea that was, and perhaps still is, in the middle of a rebuild. It's not the Chelsea that existed under the previous owners, which was stable, had a clear system, coaches, without this constant galloping who knows where.'

Such comments are unlikely to be well received when read by the club's hierarchy, while he also said on Chelsea's managerial merry-go-round: 'The coaches themselves don't know what tactics they'll play. They come to the club and try one set of tactics. Whether it works or not, they try another.'

When Mudryk returns from his ankle injury, he will have to hope his football can do the talking. After this, neither Tottenham nor Chelsea are likely to want him to speak again any time soon.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes 'ready' for Newcastle return as Mikel Arteta sets Arsenal star challenge
Sports.content:
It was the scene that summed up Newcastle's summer.

Bruno Guimaraes greeted Matthias Jaissle, the club's new manager, at a training camp in Spain. But he wasn't there to say hello. He was there to wave goodbye.

The midfielder had already made up his mind on a move to Arsenal, whose £75million bid was enough to make Newcastle blink once more in a summer of change at St James' Park. After Jaissle's brief attempt to convince him to stay, the Brazilian followed boss Eddie Howe and two other star players, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, out the door.

Guimaraes was the last of those four to leave and he'll be first to come back, as Arsenal head north to resume their Premier League title charge on Saturday. Mirror Football assesses his time with the Gunners so far and, despite things looking rosy on the surface, why Mikel Arteta wants more from him.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Arteta's challenge

Guimaraes must've been feeling on top of the world when, after an impressive performance to help Arsenal beat Hull 1-0 in their final game before the international break, he received a standing ovation from the Emirates crowd. It was already his 14th appearance for the Gunners, in which he's scored a commendable two goals, and arguably his best.

But Arteta brought him back to Earth post-match with a cutting comment. "He's still not there," the Arsenal manager stated.

‌



"He's much better, he's hitting serious levels now, but we can still take the player to another level. I told him in the dressing room - he's very good, he had a massive impact, he owned a lot of moments in the game. But there is still much more to come."

Guimaraes' all-action performance and 111 touches, the most in the match, clearly wasn't enough for Arteta, who explained his eyebrow-raising appraisal this week. "It's about impact," the Gunners boss said. "The amount of things he can do to influence the game and own the game.

"He's getting better at it. And he will get better at it when the relationships and understanding of what we do increases day by day."

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta believes that there's 'more to come' from Bruno Guimaraes (Image: Joe Prior/Visionhaus via Getty Images)

‌



Warning from Rice

After years spent squaring off in midfield, there's now a bromance blossoming between Guimaeres and Declan Rice. The pair have heaped praise on each other since the day Guimaeres joined Arsenal and have become Arteta's first-choice midfield duo.

But perhaps a quote from Rice illustrates why their gaffer isn't satisfied yet. The England international said in a recent interview with GQ Magazine that he warned former team-mate Christian Norgaard, another midfielder with Premier League experience, that it can take nearly a full season to get to grips with what Arteta wants.

"You're not going to grasp this for like six, seven months," Rice recalled telling Norgaard. "With our manager, he doesn't care who you are. You're getting detail. You're going into the game knowing everything."

Guimaraes is grateful for Rice's advice, too, telling ESPN while on international duty: "I'm learning from him - learning a lot from him - since he's a very technical player.

‌



"I think we have one of the best midfields in Europe here, yes, given the number of players we have. Anyway, I think Declan is a guy who's been helping me a lot; I felt right at home."

Do Arsenal have the best midfield in the Premier League? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Declan Rice has warned Bruno Guimaraes about adapting to Arsenal's system (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Up for the fight

As Arteta and Rice have explained, Guimaeres has a fight on his hands to cement his place. His £75m price tag is no guarantee of a starting spot, having initially been kept out of Arsenal's line-up by Myles Lewis-Skelly.

‌



But Guimaeres has, quite literally, fought his way into the XI. The former Lyon star boasts the second-highest duel success rate among Premier League midfielders this season, winning 69.2 per cent of them. That's only bettered by Chelsea's Romeo Lavia.

And you can bet your bottom dollar that Guimaraes will need to win some more on a frosty yet fiery night at St James' Park. "It's not easy to switch clubs after nearly five years, when you were already completely used to the routine, to everything," Guimaeres added ahead of Saturday's 5:30pm kick-off. "But I think this is a huge challenge and I'm ready for it."

Sports.title: Man Utd CEO Omar Berrada breaks silence on Man City charges with firm message
Sports.content:
Man Utd CEO Omar Berrada breaks silence on Man City charges with firm message

Omar Berrada's time at Manchester City covered most of the years in which the Premier League club have now been found to have committed serious financial breaches

View 2 Images Omar Berrada has spoken publicly about Manchester City's charges for the first time (Image: Sky Sports)

Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada insists that he is "not concerned" about being caught up in the case against former employers Manchester City.

‌



‌



An independent commission recently found City guilty of breaching more than 100 of the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018, having artificially inflated their revenues by £830million using 'sham' commercial agreements. The club deny any wrongdoing and have appealed the verdict.

‌



Berrada joined City in 2011 and worked in the club's commercial and international business departments. He was then appointed chief operating officer in 2016 and worked closely with City CEO Ferran Soriano.

‌



Having moved to United in 2024, one year after the charges were brought against City, Berrada has now spoken about the case in public for the first time. "I'm not concerned," he told Sky Sports.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"I want to be very clear about this: I wasn't involved in any wrongdoings. I wasn't involved in the proceedings. There are no allegations against me. In that sense, there will be no surprises."

It was put to Berrada that should City fail in their appeal, he could lead United in a compensation claim against his old club. "I don't want to comment on that because right now, it's an ongoing process," the 48-year-old added.

‌



"When it runs its course, then we'll take a view of what is our position as Manchester United."

Across town at the Etihad Stadium, City manager Enzo Maresca says that his club are 'convinced' they'll be successful in their appeal. "The reason why I joined this club is I completely trust 100 per cent, the owner, the sporting director, the CEO - all the organisation. I have no doubt about that," Maresca affirmed last month.

‌



View 2 Images Omar Berrada left Manchester City to join United in 2024 (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

"I spoke with the club for sure. Probably the right moment to speak about that is when we're going to win this appeal."

‌



Soriano has also told supporters: "The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began.

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies."
