Sports.title: F1 Las Vegas GP: Rain drowns out FP1
Sports.content:
"If we're on a track like Vegas and it rains, honestly, I think we're in trouble," Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson predicted after sampling this year's rain tyres in Brazil.

His comments reflected the general mood in the paddock as the Pirelli tyres are difficult to bring up to temperature, especially at a circuit with low corner speeds and glacial temperatures like the 6km street circuit in the gambling haven.

Lawson's comments proved relevant as the heavens opened up intermittently in Nevada on Thursday morning, and more rain arrived right before the start of FP1 at 4:30 pm local time.

With little rain expected for the remainder of the weekend, it naturally led to an action-starved session, leaving fans forking out the event's eye-watering ticket prices to look for action at the blackjack tables instead.

Venturing out on the low-grip surface, with the walls looming large, felt like a gamble, too. But as if intent to at least offer the home fans something, Sergio Perez of US-owned team Cadillac was first to brave the conditions on full wet tyres for an exploratory lap. He was later joined by Haas duo Rafael Camara and Ryo Hirakawa, the latter completing a rookie FP1 session instead of Oliver Bearman.

The second Cadillac of Valtteri Bottas also explored the inclement conditions, celebrating his 2027 confirmation with a huge tank slapper on his one lap, showing the two US-owned teams certainly couldn't be accused of not chipping in.

Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

While TV audiences and punters intent on analysing lap times and long runs were also left wanting, FP1 actually became one of the most picturesque sessions of the year. The Las Vegas Boulevard is photogenic at the best of times, but the rain further drowned the Strip in neon-tinted reflections, hues Hunter S. Thompson would have approved of.

"Amazing, it's a lovely Strip," gawked Ferrari reserve driver Dino Beganovic as he replaced Lewis Hamilton for the session.

"Enjoy the sightseeing... but we'll box this lap, please," came the perfunctory reply from Ferrari.

Beganovic may as well have enjoyed it, as staying tucking inside the garage was not an option to begin with for the Swedish-Bosnian driver. For any of the teams' four mandatory rookie FP1 sessions to count, drivers must at least leave the garage once.

It explains why all three rookie runners went out, including Jak Crawford who deputised for Fernando Alonso at Aston Martin, though they will be ruing the lack of actual mileage the rare opportunity was able to provide.

As world champion Kimi Antonelli reported aquaplaning, several more tenured drivers had close shaves with the walls. Alex Albon went straight at Turn 11 at the end of the Strip , while Audi's Nico Hulkenberg also locked up at the drenched left-hander.

"It's almost like an ice rink," reported Red Bull's Max Verstappen, The Dutchman a rather cool admirer of street circuits at the best of times.

Eventually, all but five drivers sampled the conditions, with the four cars from McLaren and Racing Bulls thinking better of it, and Aston's Lance Stroll also not feeling particularly motivated.

Camara and Alpine duo Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto were the only three drivers to venture out twice, with the Argentine nearly reliving the scenes of his high-speed qualifying shunt in 2024 for Williams as he momentarily lost control over his car on the straight.

For the avoidance of doubt, no laptimes were recorded.

Sports.title: Nike joins F1 as apparel partner
Sports.content:
Athletic apparel giant Nike has joined F1 as its official partner and uniform supplier, taking over from Puma at the start of 2027.

As was long rumoured, Nike will start supplying F1 personnel with apparel and footwear from the start of next season, a partnership that also extends to F1 Academy, which had both been using Puma kit until this year.

The athletic company will also come up with F1-inspired retail collections, the first of which will go on sale on Friday and be centred around the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

"Nike will bring new energy to the pinnacle of motorsport through capsule collections with a focus on style, performance, and lifestyle including footwear, apparel, and accessories, as well as performance innovations, and race-weekend experiences for the next generation of athletes and fans," the announcement promised.

"Fans will get a first look on 20 November, when the limited Las Vegas Grand Prix x Nike capsule collection drops at the F1 Hub and Nike Las Vegas stores.

Nike CEO Elliott Hill said: "Formula 1 is driven by competition, speed and a constant push to innovate. That’s an athlete mindset, and it’s one we share at Nike. Together, we have an incredible opportunity to bring new energy to the sport, serve its athletes and inspire fans around the world.”

Sports.title: FIA to phase in full-time F1 stewards from 2027
Sports.content:
The consistency of stewards’ decisions has been a topic of discussion in the Formula 1 paddock for years. While the complexity of the sporting regulations and racing guidelines is one factor, another question keeps coming up: would a permanent panel of stewards improve consistency?

From 2027, the FIA will take a step in that direction. The governing body announced on Thursday that it will gradually move towards full-time stewards, with the first phase beginning in 2027.

The intention is to recruit a panel of 12 to 15 full-time stewards, although that number will only be reached over time. The first full-time stewards will be recruited during the 2027 season, who will be joined at each race by the usual part-time stewards and a driver’s steward, whose specialist knowledge and perspective as a former racing driver will remain part of the process.

The main objective is to improve the consistency of decisions, although according to the FIA, the initiative goes beyond that. By making the role full-time, these stewards can also be deployed outside race weekends, for example “to identify emerging trends and areas requiring regulatory clarification” and to train FIA officials.

That would allow for shortcomings in the sporting regulations and racing guidelines used by stewards to be addressed more effectively. The aim is therefore not only to improve consistency during races, but also to make the rules and guidelines themselves more robust in the first place.

Start action Photo by: Clive Rose / Getty Images

This move is in line with what FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has been advocating for some time: further professionalisation of the stewarding panel. The FIA believes moving beyond the current voluntary, rotating system will help improve continuity and consistency.

And that is precisely one of the key areas the FIA wants to improve, while emphasising that the move also complements the FIA Remote Operations Centre, which recently opened at Biggin Hill.

“This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to delivering the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport. The recruitment of full-time stewards is a significant step in our longstanding mission of building a dedicated officiating ecosystem in the FIA Formula One World Championship, it is also an investment in the future of our sport,” Ben Sulayem said.

“This development will help to build greater expertise and continuity within our stewarding structure, strengthening our ability to review and improve regulations, support the development of future officials and ensure the highest standards of consistent officiating across all our championships.”

The FIA is now setting up the recruitment process for the phased introduction in 2027, with plans to expand the group in 2028 and subsequent years until it reaches the target of 12 to 15 full-time stewards.

Sports.title: Hamilton insists there are no "trust" problems at Ferrari
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has insisted there are zero “trust” problems at Ferrari despite him overruling strategic calls becoming a repeated occurrence across recent Formula 1 grands prix.

The seven-time world champion has ignored calls to pit in two of the last four rounds - Singapore and Brazil - with both backfiring on the Scuderia driver.

In Singapore he elected to keep track position under a virtual safety car, but on worn tyres he dropped from podium contention to sixth late on - for which he apologised afterwards.

Then in Brazil last time out, Hamilton stayed on slicks despite the rain intensifying and this led to a late spin at the final corner before pitting the following lap to eventually finish ninth.

Those instances came amid talk of fractious relations down at Ferrari but ahead of this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix, Hamilton confirmed all is well - particularly with his new-for-2026 race engineer Carlo Santi.

“It’s definitely not a trust thing, we’re constantly working on our communication,” said the 41-year-old.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"It's been a lot better this year. Carlo has done an amazing job and those particular two times, particularly the last time, was just I didn't have the information I needed.

“I got the call right at the last minute. We'll just continue to work on the processes. We're super united in what's working, in the right direction."

This year has been much improved for Hamilton, who is fourth in the standings with three rounds remaining, currently on 261 points compared to his total of 156 in 2025.

His first year in Ferrari colours was certainly underwhelming, but there have still been signs of improvement in 2026 despite it being a significant jump from last season.

Not only is that in reference to the strategic calls, but also his connection with team-mate Charles Leclerc, clashing on a few occasions and most notably in Mexico three weeks ago.

It cost Ferrari the win and Hamilton subsequently criticised Leclerc’s “do or die” attitude, before suggesting in Sao Paulo that the Monegasque races him harder than he does with other drivers.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Yuri Cortez / AFP via Getty Images

That led to an hour-long meeting between both Scuderia drivers plus team boss Fred Vasseur and Hamilton and Leclerc are now confident that the issue has been resolved.

“Charles is a great driver,” said Hamilton. “The detail we went into about stuff like that, in terms of when we close the visor, it's very clear, we understand each other, we understand each other's boundaries and the ultimate goal, which is to get the best result for the team.

“So I don't feel like that will be a problem moving forward. I have no concerns or worries about racing him, and I don't think he does for me either.”

The talk surrounding the Mexico clash was naturally high, but Leclerc reckons that is a consequence of driving for Ferrari and all focus is now on securing runner-up in the constructors’ standings.

“Everything has been taken out of proportion,” said Leclerc. “I'm kind of used to it now, driving for Ferrari for so many years. But things are very often taken out of proportion.

“The goal is not always to agree and that will never happen. We can have different opinions and that was the case, for example, in Mexico.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

“But just the fact of speaking eased all tensions and we were completely fine with it. It's not that we had to speak for an hour, even though it ended up lasting an hour, just because we had a good time.

“We started speaking about many other things in trying to bring the team and to help the team go forward.

“But the discussion about the tension was like maybe five or 10 minutes and then the air was clean and that's it.”

Ferrari heads into the Vegas race 95 points ahead of third-placed Red Bull and 142 behind Mercedes, who clinched its ninth title at Interlagos.

Sports.title: Gerald McClellan Needed 171 Seconds to Crush John Mugabi and Win First World Title
Sports.content:
It took Gerald McClellan 171 seconds to capture his first world championship. On November 20, 1991, inside London’s Royal Albert Hall, the 24-year-old Kronk product dropped John “The Beast” Mugabi three times in the opening stanza. Referee Roberto Ramirez Sr. stepped in at 2:51 of round one to award McClellan the vacant WBO middleweight title.

Thirty-five years later, the striking detail is how fast McClellan shut the door on a fellow knockout artist. Both fighters weighed 157 pounds at the scale. Either man possessed the kind of heavy hands that could end a night early, yet Mugabi barely threw anything of consequence before getting hurt. McClellan simply beat him to the punch with a crisp right hand that landed cleanly while the former junior middleweight champion was still trying to find his range.

Mugabi never got a second to breathe. At 31, he was five years removed from dragging Marvin Hagler into an eleven-round war for the undisputed middleweight crown in Las Vegas. He had captured Olympic silver for Uganda in 1980 and later claimed the WBC 154-pound belt when Rene Jacquot tore his ankle in the first round. Terry Norris then obliterated Mugabi in one round in March 1990 to strip that title away. Two tune-up wins brought Mugabi into London at 38 and 3, with every single victory coming by knockout.

None of his 41 professional bouts had ever reached the judges’ scorecards. On paper, that meant trouble for any young contender willing to trade in close quarters. In reality, Mugabi was worn down from years of brutal wars and could no longer absorb a clean shot from a fresh puncher. Once the first knockdown landed, Mugabi had to recover on unsteady legs against a sharper, faster fighter who reloaded his right hand immediately.

McClellan entered the ring at 22 and 2 with 20 knockouts. Prior decision losses to Dennis Milton and Ralph Ward left genuine questions about how the Detroit fighter would handle an experienced veteran if the bout dragged into the middle rounds. Mugabi lacked the durability to test that theory. Three trips to the canvas in under three minutes forced Ramirez to wave the contest off with nine seconds left on the clock.

The Royal Albert Hall promotion was built around Frank Bruno’s comeback against John Emmen. McClellan was competing for a WBO strap that Chris Eubank had recently vacated, back when the organization was still fighting for recognition alongside the established WBC, WBA, and IBF belts. Still, destroying a recognizable name on British soil gave Emanuel Steward’s prized pupil instant credibility across the Atlantic.

McClellan vacated the WBO belt without making a single defense to chase bigger money in the established sanctioning bodies. In May 1993, he survived massive punches from Julian Jackson to score a fifth-round stoppage for the WBC middleweight championship, then wiped out three consecutive challengers inside the opening round. The Jackson fight proved McClellan possessed a chin to match his firepower. The Mugabi demolition proved he rarely needed to use it.

Sports.title: WBA Says Teofimo Has No Permit for Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez still needs WBA approval to fight Ryan Garcia in a welterweight unification before facing Jack Catterall. WBA president Gilberto Mendoza said no special permit had been granted after Oscar De La Hoya said the WBA had already ruled in Lopez’s favor. Lopez co-manager Keith Connolly said the process was still ongoing.

“No special permit has been granted to Teófimo Lopez,” Mendoza wrote on X. In a reply to the post, Connolly wrote, “He was just correcting Oscar the process is still ongoing.”

“It has already been worked out. The WBA has already ruled on it,” said De La Hoya, Garcia’s promoter, to Fight Hub TV. He said the WBA was giving Lopez an exemption because the fight would be a unification.

De La Hoya rated the chances of the fight happening as “great” and said February 6 was the target, with Las Vegas and New York in the running to host it.

Lopez holds the WBA Super title at 147 pounds. Garcia holds the WBC belt. A special permit would give Lopez a way to put his belt up against Garcia before satisfying his mandatory obligation to Catterall. Mendoza’s statement addresses whether a permit has been granted, and Connolly’s reply leaves open the possibility that the WBA could grant permission later. The exchange leaves the formal filing status unclear.

The WBA reaffirmed its order for Lopez to face Catterall on November 11 after considering a request from Lopez’s team. In that ruling, the organization said Lopez’s team had yet to submit a formal special-permit request for a unification. It also asked the Lopez and Catterall camps to resume talks and gave them ten days from the ruling to submit an agreement on a date for the mandatory fight.

Catterall earned his place by beating Shakhram Giyasov for the WBA’s other welterweight title. The WBA had already allowed Rolando Romero to make an optional defense before facing the winner of Catterall and Giyasov. Lopez beat Romero by majority decision in August and took on that obligation when he won the Super title. A permit for Garcia would mean Catterall has to wait through another fight for his shot at the Super belt.

There’s an obvious reason for Lopez and Garcia to pursue the unification. They can sell the fight on their names alone, and putting both belts up gives the winner a unified title at 147 pounds. Catterall has a simple argument of his own. He won the fight the WBA told him would put him next in line, and the WBA has already reaffirmed his position once.

That leaves De La Hoya talking up a fight the WBA has yet to clear. If the permit comes through, the next question is what timetable the WBA gives Catterall. In the meantime, the mandatory order remains in place, and Lopez’s camp is still pursuing a route to Garcia with the WBA belt on the line.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder Looks Relieved After Jai Opetaia Pulls Out of Cardiff Fight
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder called Jai Opetaia’s withdrawal a “blessing” and wished him well in his bid to become undisputed cruiserweight champion.

The former WBC heavyweight champion (45-4-1, 43 KOs) still has no announced replacement for the December 11 Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua undercard in Cardiff, though his sudden cheerfulness looks a whole lot like relief after dodging a dangerous southpaw who was supposed to test his legs in front of a massive Netflix audience.

“I’m not mad at Jai at all. Actually, it was a blessing for what’s to come after this,” said Wilder on the Heavyweight Truth channel. He was smiling and seeming way too happy for what should have been bad news. Wilder didn’t say what he had in mind or name anyone he expects to fight at Principality Stadium.

A normal fighter would be angry about their well-known opponent pulling out, but not Wilder. His behavior betrays his inner workings. He didn’t want to hit that hill, going up against a fighter who could wreck what’s left of his sagging career. Getting stopped by a cruiserweight would have been it for Wilder. Coming back from that loss, especially if it were a knockout, would be next to impossible at his age.

Derek Chisora has confirmed he was contacted about taking the fight, and he’s also stirring the pot over why Opetaia really pulled out. Chisora told talkSPORT he would accept a rematch if the money was right and said the offer had yet to meet his asking price, while also claiming Opetaia wasn’t actually hurt and simply walked out of the gym after getting worked over by a heavyweight sparring partner.

Wilder beat Chisora by split decision in London in April, dropping him twice in a fight that still went all 12 rounds and showed how hard it is for the 41-year-old Alabama puncher to finish durable heavyweights who keep walking forward.

Richard Riakporhe has also put his name forward. Like Opetaia, he made his name at cruiserweight, though he has already fought at heavyweight and doesn’t carry the same undefeated aura as the 31-0 Australian. Jarrell Miller (28-1-2, 22 KOs) said he received a call about facing Wilder, although he’s already scheduled to fight 2016 Olympic gold medalist Tony Yoka on December 20 in Accra, Ghana, on a Matchroom DAZN show where Miller enters as the WBA’s top-ranked contender.

Opetaia was due to make his heavyweight debut in Cardiff. His co-promoter, Mick Francis, said he injured his hand against Noel Mikaelian in September and aggravated it in training, though plenty of observers suspect Opetaia also realized he had everything to lose before his planned Cinco de Mayo 2027 unification clash with David Benavidez, who first has to get past Michal Cieslak on December 5.

Getting clipped by one Wilder right hand at heavyweight would kill that Benavidez payday on the spot and send Benavidez straight toward Oleksandr Usyk instead. Opetaia apologized to Wilder and his team after withdrawing and reaffirmed his goal of becoming undisputed at cruiserweight.

“We understand, Jai. We understand, bro. That’s all I got to say,” said Wilder. “I wish you nothing but the best moving forward with your career. Undisputed, baby. I’m rooting for you. Let’s go.”

The appeal of Wilder vs. Opetaia was seeing how an unbeaten cruiserweight would handle Wilder’s right hand in his first fight at heavyweight, especially with gym rumors already questioning how he handled heavyweight size in sparring.

A Chisora rematch would offer a different question, especially since fans already paid to watch that exact fight eight months ago without seeing a knockout. Wilder put him down twice in April and still had to settle for a split decision. Chisora has already shown he can get back up and make Wilder work the full distance, which is the last thing Wilder wants if he’s trying to look explosive on the Fury vs. Joshua broadcast.

The organizers have three weeks to fill the chief support slot. Chisora has made his price a condition of taking the fight, Riakporhe has volunteered, and Miller says he has been approached with another bout already on his calendar. Wilder’s response settled how he feels about Opetaia pulling out. Who he’ll fight in Cardiff is still open, and right now every available replacement brings either a recycled April rematch or a short-notice fill-in that won’t replace the buzz Opetaia brought to the card.

Sports.title: David Morrell Takes a Huge Step Backward Against Rodriguez
Sports.content:
David Morrell should beat Julio de Jesus Rodriguez on Saturday in Santo Domingo. The trouble is that even a quick knockout of the 44-year-old veteran will do little to repair the damage from Zak Chelli stopping him in the tenth round in May. For a fighter who was facing David Benavidez less than two years ago, this is a long way back.

Morrell (12-2, 9 KOs) is scheduled for ten rounds at light heavyweight against Rodriguez (27-10, 24 KOs) on Shuan Boxing’s card at the Coliseo Carlos “Teo” Cruz. Rodriguez has knocked out 24 men, but he’s on a long losing streak and has been stopped by James Metcalf and Ismael Villarreal. At 28, Morrell should have the speed to get his punches off first and the power to end it early.

The Benavidez defeat was easier to take. Morrell went the distance in a competitive fight against one of the best men in the division. His split decision over Imam Khataev five months later was a harder result to read. He got the win, but it was close enough that he still had something to prove when he went to Manchester to fight Chelli. Getting stopped there took away the argument that he was only a step behind the very best.

Morrell has been out since May, and there’s value in getting him back in the ring. He can get his timing back, put combinations together, and see how comfortable he feels throwing the left hand. Rodriguez’s recent form makes an early finish the expectation. If Morrell struggles to put him away or has trouble keeping control of the fight, those questions about his form will follow him out of Santo Domingo.

The next opponent will tell us more. Morrell needs someone who can make him work into the later rounds and still bring something back at him. That’s where the Chelli loss leaves the biggest question, and Saturday’s opponent is unlikely to make Morrell answer it.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Claims Jai Opetaia Dodged Deontay Wilder Risk for Benavidez
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley is not buying the hand injury story that knocked Jai Opetaia out of his December 11 heavyweight fight against Deontay Wilder in Cardiff.

Bradley thinks the Australian cruiserweight and his team finally had a reality check about what happens when a smaller fighter steps up to take bombs from a natural heavyweight. Mick Francis of Tasman Fighters claimed Opetaia aggravated the hand in training while getting ready for the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua undercard, but Bradley says he needs to see actual proof before he believes it.

“I truly believe that Jai had a reality check, man, and really thought about what the hell he was doing, him and his team,” said Bradley on his channel.

Bradley is saying what every boxing fan already figured out the second the withdrawal news broke. Wilder might be past his prime, yet he still carries the kind of right hand that turns the lights out in a split second.

“All it takes for Deontay Wilder is one, and that’s it,” said Bradley.

As Bradley noted, Opetaia could have outboxed Wilder for ten rounds, only to get clipped with one clean shot and wake up looking at the arena lights. Had that happened, Benavidez already admitted he would have moved straight on to chasing Oleksandr Usyk instead.

Opetaia only took the Cardiff date because he stopped Noel Mikaelian in September and did not want to sit around until May waiting for Benavidez. Even if Opetaia had beaten Wilder, a cautious points win would have done nothing to build hype for the Benavidez fight.

Everything short of a highlight-reel knockout was a bad business move. Benavidez even admitted he was relieved when the Wilder fight fell apart. First, Benavidez has to get past Michal Cieslak on December 5 in Glendale, Arizona.

If Benavidez wins that unification bout and brings the WBA, WBC, and WBO belts to Las Vegas on Cinco de Mayo weekend, Opetaia gets his chance to win three world titles in one night.

Pulling out of the Wilder trap might look suspicious to Bradley, yet it easily saved Opetaia from ruining the biggest fight of his career.

Sports.title: Andy Hiraoka Signs With Zuffa, Moves to Welterweight
Sports.content:
Andy Hiraoka has signed a multi-fight deal with Zuffa Boxing and will move up to welterweight, the promotion announced. The Japanese southpaw enters the 147-pound division after pushing WBA light welterweight champion Gary Antuanne Russell hard enough in February to make a case that he deserved the decision.

Hiraoka (24-1, 19 KOs) went into that fight unbeaten and left with three scorecards that made Russell’s first title defense look comfortable. The Nevada commission recorded scores of 116-111 twice and 117-110 for Russell. Those margins were hard to square with what Hiraoka did in the second half, when he began hurting Russell to the body and forced the champion to give ground.

Russell had the better of the first five rounds in Las Vegas. He got his combinations off first and built a 60-36 edge in punches landed over that stretch, according to CompuBox. Hiraoka had landed only one body punch through five rounds. In the seventh alone, he landed 20. Once he started getting through downstairs, Russell had to spend more time fighting off his back foot.

Hiraoka landed 76 power punches to Russell’s 59 over the last six rounds. There were rounds in that stretch where Russell was still busy enough to give the judges a choice, but Hiraoka was landing the shots that changed how the fight was being fought. If you gave him one or two of the closer early rounds and most of the second half, you could get to a Hiraoka win. The point he lost for low blows in the 10th made his case harder, especially on a card where he was already giving away early rounds.

That fight against Russell put Hiraoka on the map in a way none of his domestic bouts in Japan ever could. Most guys who lose a decision on a big stage walk away with their stock dented, but Hiraoka actually raised his value because of how he broke Russell down in the second half.

You don’t often see a 140-pounder punish a champion to the ribs and liver like that, especially someone as physically strong as Russell. Watching Russell go from firing crisp combinations in the first five rounds to literally running out of room and looking desperate to survive down the stretch told the whole story. If not for that slow start and the point deduction in the 10th, Hiraoka walks out of Las Vegas with the WBA belt.

Before this signing, he was completely stuck in neutral. Fighting in Japan under Ohashi Promotions kept him off the radar for casual fans and made it almost impossible to lure top American or British names into the ring with him. Nobody wanted the risk for a low-profile payday.

“I feel like he was down on the scorecards and knew it, so he tried to pick up the intensity,” said Russell after the fight, as reported by The Ring. Hiraoka’s attack held up deep into the fight. He landed 13 power punches in the 12th, his second-highest total of the night, and finished just two behind Russell in power punches landed overall.

The move to 147 raises a question about how quickly Hiraoka can get that body attack going against bigger men. He found his way into the Russell fight by stepping close enough to hit the body after spending much of the opening rounds at a distance where Russell could get off first. A welterweight who can make him pay on the way in would put that adjustment to a different test.

Zuffa’s announcement named neither a debut date nor an opponent. The first opponent will tell us how much the promotion took from the Russell fight. A durable welterweight who can make Hiraoka work beyond the opening rounds would show whether the pressure he put on a champion at 140 comes with him to 147.

Sports.title: Senate Passes Ali Revival Act by Unanimous Consent
Sports.content:
The U.S. Senate passed the Muhammad Ali American Boxing Revival Act by unanimous consent Thursday, moving Zuffa Boxing’s league model a step closer to federal recognition. The bill would let leagues stage fights between boxers they sign and run their own title systems alongside the traditional sanctioning bodies.

The Senate Press Gallery confirmed that H.R. 4624 passed with a substitute amendment from Sens. Ted Cruz of Texas and Jacky Rosen of Nevada. The House, which passed an earlier version, must agree to the Senate’s changes before the bill can go to the president.

The bill’s biggest change is the creation of a legal path for Unified Boxing Organizations. Under the published Cruz–Rosen amendment, a league would match fighters under contract to it and could run its own rankings. It could also recognize titles and rankings from an independent organization. Fighters could choose to sign with a league or continue working with traditional promoters.

For Zuffa, the benefit is in the matchmaking. If two contenders are on the same roster, the league can put them together without first having to negotiate with a rival promoter. That could help keep a division moving when the best available opponents are already signed. The model is less helpful when the opponent fans want fights for somebody else. The league still needs enough depth in each division to make the fights it wants to sell.

For a boxer, the question is what happens when the league has the belt he wants and controls who gets the next shot. A contender can climb the rankings and still depend on the same company for a date, an opponent and a purse. The amendment addresses some of that leverage. It would generally cap promotional agreements at six years, limit a boxer’s first professional promotional agreement to three and allow talks with other promoters or leagues during the final 90 days of a deal. A boxer could sign a new agreement once the existing one expires.

The published amendment would also set a $200 minimum for each round a boxer participates in, covering traditional promoters as well as leagues. It would require at least $50,000 in medical coverage for injuries sustained during a bout and $15,000 in accidental death coverage. The leagues would also have to carry insurance for injuries sustained while training for a covered bout and use an independent third party to administer drug testing.

The test for Zuffa is whether it can sign enough contenders to make its belts worth chasing. A league can build a title fight from its own roster, but a belt is only as valuable as the competition behind it. For a fighter weighing a multi-year deal, the decisions that count are who he can fight, how often he gets booked and what he can earn by moving up.

Sports.title: De La Hoya Says WBA Cleared Teofimo Lopez for Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Oscar De La Hoya says the WBA is giving Teofimo Lopez an exemption to fight Ryan Garcia before mandatory challenger Jack Catterall. The proposed February 6 welterweight unification could put Eddie Hearn’s threat to sue the WBA to the test if the association confirms that Lopez can keep his title and fight Garcia first.

“It has already been worked out,” said De La Hoya on Fight Hub TV when asked whether the Catterall mandatory could hold up the fight. “The WBA has already ruled on it. They’re giving an exemption to Teofimo Lopez because he is the world champion and this will be a unification.”

De La Hoya called it an exemption and gave no details of the ruling or its terms. The WBA’s November 11 public decision reaffirmed that Lopez must defend his Super title against Catterall and gave the camps 10 calendar days to reach an agreement or propose another solution. Either side could request a purse bid if talks failed.

The same decision said the WBA can consider a unification under its special permit rule. Mike Coppinger reported on November 14 that the WBA had informed the parties that Lopez could apply for a permit to face Garcia, the WBC champion. De La Hoya’s account goes a step further. He says the WBA has made its decision, though the association has yet to publicly confirm that it has granted an exemption.

“I would sue them immediately,” said Hearn on Inside the Ring last week when asked what he would do if the WBA ruled against him. The Matchroom promoter has argued that Catterall was already owed a shot at the Super title before Lopez took it from Rolando Romero. Catterall holds the WBA’s Regular belt and earned the right to challenge for the top title by beating Shakhram Giyasov.

If the WBA confirms De La Hoya’s account, the terms of the exemption could determine how long Catterall has to wait. A written ruling could spell out whether Catterall gets the winner and when that defense would be due. Hearn has been pressing for Catterall to get his shot first. If he follows through on his threat, the WBA’s November order and the terms of any exemption would both come into play.

De La Hoya said Las Vegas and New York were under consideration and that a few details remained to be worked out for February 6. He also said he had never spoken to Floyd Mayweather about making a fight with Garcia. Later in the interview, De La Hoya said he believed the Lopez deal was close. For Catterall, the immediate question is what the WBA will put in writing about the title shot it ordered.

Ghana News.title: French Ambassador to Ghana warns of AI threats, urges Africa not to ‘wait for the West’
Ghana News.content:
French Ambassador to Ghana, Diarra Dimé-Labille, has sounded an alarm over the potential threats of Artificial Intelligence, warning that humanity could be approaching a crossroads where its ability to control the technology and determine its own destiny could increasingly come into question.

She believes the dangers are too significant to ignore, insisting that Ghana and the African continent must lead the charge in shaping the future of AI and establishing safeguards to protect humanity.

The Ambassador says the continent must not wait for global technology giants in the West to determine how a technology, whose consequences will affect every society, operates.

Speaking during a diplomatic visit to the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), she expressed concern about how quickly AI is evolving and whether humanity is adequately prepared to manage its potential risks.

“Ghana and the African countries, the European countries, and all those countries can do something together. We are responsible. There is no need to wait for others to do it for us. And it's not only the expert or the scientific that has to deal with it. It's also all of us as citizens,” she said.

The French Ambassador to Ghana and a delegation from the embassy paid a diplomatic visit to KNUST to acquaint them with the activities of the university in promoting AI education and deployment.

The visit is part of a two-day tour by the ambassador to the region to inspect projects and other infrastructure being rolled out and funded by the embassy to foster socioeconomic and technological advancements.

After touring the Responsible AI Lab (RAIL) at the university, the ambassador expressed hope that AI experts in the College of Engineering were also particularly concerned about the threats of the technology despite harnessing its benefits.

“It’s important for us to treat this carefully. I was definitely impressed and amazed visiting the AI lab in KNUST, and one of the first reflections when I saw all those young AI experts, they were talking about safeguard. They were talking about the need for humanity to really do the best possible to contain the threat of AI,” she said.

She continued: “You are an AI expert, are you not afraid? And, they told me, it's not because we failed to prevent this kind of threat yesterday that we cannot do it today. It's never late.

"So, seeing those young Ghanaian AI experts thinking about it, having this kind of hope, makes me, very hopeful. Those young people are definitely very committed to working in a very ethical and responsible AI."

The ambassador also participated in the opening session of the Winter School at KNUST, where she reiterated France’s commitment to strengthening scientific research, academic cooperation and innovation partnerships with African countries, particularly Ghana.

Ambassador Dimé-Labille highlighted that France considers Africa an important partner in scientific advancement and is keenly concerned about developing sustainable partnerships that would foster bilateral cooperation and provide practical solutions to pressing societal challenges.

Meeting with some faculty members and the governing council of the university, Ambassador Dimé-Labille emphasized deepening the cooperation between the university and the embassy.

“The cooperation between the French embassy and KNUST definitely needs to continue in this way. We know that we are having this cooperation and the partnership through different initiatives,” she said.

Representing the Vice Chancellor, Prof Samuel Asare Nkansah, who is a professorial member of the university council, highlighted some initiatives undertaken by the university to enhance AI education and its application.

He noted that the university is ready to explore AI applications in the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly ensuring social inclusion with a focus on physical challenges.

Ghana News.title: Maxwell Kudekor appointed World International Press Club International Affairs Secretary
Ghana News.content:
JoyNews journalist Maxwell Kudekor has been appointed International Affairs Secretary of the World International Press Club (WIPC), an international media organisation committed to promoting press freedom, journalists’ rights and professional cooperation.

The appointment was announced in a congratulatory message issued by the organisation’s International President, Ayrongozeb Kamal, who described Mr Kudekor’s appointment as a reflection of its confidence in his leadership, dedication and commitment to global journalism.

The organisation expressed optimism that his experience and contributions would strengthen its international activities and promote solidarity among journalists across different countries.

Press Freedom

In its congratulatory message, the WIPC said it expected the newly appointed International Affairs Secretary to contribute towards strengthening international cooperation and advancing the organisation’s objectives.

“We firmly believe that his experience, cooperation, and valuable contributions will help strengthen WIPC’s international activities and promote unity, solidarity, press freedom, journalists’ rights, and professional development worldwide,” the statement said.

The organisation also expressed hope that the appointment would create new opportunities for international cooperation among media practitioners, wishing Mr Kudekor success in his new responsibilities and reaffirmed its commitment to promoting unity and solidarity within the journalism profession.

Commitment

Reacting to the appointment, Mr Kudekor reaffirmed his commitment to defending the rights of journalists and promoting responsible journalism.

“Always ready to continue in the service of humanity. Defending the rights of journalists and responsible journalism,” he stated.

The appointment places the Ghanaian journalist in an international role involving the promotion of cooperation among media professionals and the advancement of the WIPC’s stated objectives.

About WIPC

The World International Press Club is a Bangladesh-based international professional organisation of journalists established in 2023 to build unity among journalists worldwide while protecting their professional rights, safety, dignity and welfare.

Its objectives include promoting press freedom, improving journalists’ working conditions, supporting journalists facing threats or persecution and encouraging professional development through training, conferences and international exchanges.

The organisation also advocates ethical journalism, fact-checking, legal assistance for journalists and cooperation with media institutions and human rights organisations.

WIPC’s constitution provides for international governing structures, national branches and regional coordination arrangements intended to facilitate cooperation among journalists across countries.

Ghana News.title: Mahama vows to protect Oti Region from illegal mining amid iron ore and nickel discoveries
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama says the discovery of iron ore and nickel deposits in the Oti Region presents a potential source of prosperity and job creation, but insists any decision to mine the resources must be done in a way that benefits the people of the area without destroying its serene environment.

Speaking during a courtesy visit by members of the Oti Regional House of Chiefs, the President said nickel was also discovered during the search for iron ore, a mineral he described as increasingly important in the green transition because of its use in manufacturing batteries for electric vehicles.

The President, however, stressed the need to protect the region's natural environment, saying the government would not want mining activities to destroy its serene surroundings.

He said, "While they were looking for iron ore, they found nickel, which has now become very important in the green transition because it's used to make the batteries for electric vehicles.

"And so, that is a potential source of prosperity and also of job creation in that area. But I want to make sure that if it is going to be mined, it is done in such a way that it will not destroy the serene environment that we have."

He said consultations would continue with traditional authorities and the youth on the discoveries.

President Mahama added that if the government decides to proceed with the exploitation of the deposits, it would be done in a manner that benefits the people of the area.

He also expressed satisfaction that the Oti Region had no galamsey, insisting that the government intended to maintain that status.

Ghana News.title: Mahama defends constitutional restriction on chiefs’ participation in partisan politics
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama

President John Dramani Mahama has defended the constitutional restriction barring chiefs from participating in active partisan politics, saying the provision is necessary to protect the dignity and respect of the chieftaincy institution.

He said traditional rulers must remain above partisan political contests while continuing to contribute to local governance and community development.

Speaking during a courtesy call by the Oti Regional House of Chiefs on Friday, November 20, 2026, the President argued that allowing chiefs to contest partisan political positions could undermine the status of the institution.

“The 1992 Constitution, for very good reason, decided that chiefs should not take part in partisan politics, and it was affirmed by the Supreme Court in its interpretation of what partisan politics is,” he said.

Mr Mahama questioned the appropriateness of traditional rulers competing in district assembly elections against members of their own communities.

“I believe that to maintain the respect of the institution, I believe that that particular clause is appropriate because can you imagine, let’s say we’re doing district assembly elections and the whole paramount chief is standing against some small student or some butcher or some teacher or something. It doesn’t all go very well,” he said.

The President, however, stressed that the restriction should not prevent chiefs from playing an active role in local governance.

He said the government had maintained the constitutional provision for appointed positions on district assemblies, which provides representation for traditional authorities and other groups.

Mr Mahama said the appointment criteria would ensure that chiefs, women, young people and persons with disabilities were represented in the assemblies.

He urged traditional authorities to nominate representatives who would participate in assembly discussions on their behalf and report back to them on decisions taken.

The President also encouraged chiefs to work closely with district chief executives and monitor how public funds allocated to district assemblies were utilised.

He said traditional authorities were well placed to identify the development needs of their communities and should help guide local authorities in selecting projects that respond to those priorities.

Ghana News.title: Bono Regional Minister warns MMDCEs against neglecting district security responsibilities
Ghana News.content:
The Bono Regional Minister, Joseph Addae Akwaboa, has warned Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) against neglecting their security responsibilities, urging them to prioritise the effective functioning of District Security Councils (DISECs) to prevent local security threats from escalating.

He said MMDCEs, as chairpersons of their respective District Security Councils, must ensure regular meetings, proper documentation of deliberations and prompt escalation of security concerns requiring regional or national intervention.

Mr Akwaboa gave the directive on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at a joint workshop for the Bono, Bono East and Ahafo Regional Security Councils (REGSECs) and MMDCEs in Sunyani.

The workshop, organised by the National Security Council Secretariat, was aimed at strengthening understanding and implementation of the Security and Intelligence Agencies Act, 2026 (Act 1168).

Addressing participants, the Bono Regional Minister stressed that security must be treated as an integral part of local governance rather than an issue left exclusively to security agencies.

He said development planning and implementation could not be separated from the security environment within which communities operate.

“I wish to emphasise that security must be mainstreamed into our local governance mandate. Development, planning and implementation cannot be divorced from the security environment within which they are expected to operate,” he stated.

Mr Akwaboa explained that MMDCEs occupied strategic positions in Ghana's decentralised security architecture because of their proximity to local communities, placing them in a position to identify emerging threats and facilitate timely responses.

He said District Security Councils remained important platforms for detecting warning signs, assessing local security dynamics and referring matters requiring higher-level intervention.

The minister consequently called for stronger institutional relationships between Regional Security Councils and District Security Councils through regular engagement, timely communication and structured information sharing.

He identified chieftaincy disputes, land conflicts, communal tensions and other localised threats as security vulnerabilities requiring continuous monitoring and proactive intervention.

Mr Akwaboa said the effective implementation of Act 1168 would further strengthen the country's security architecture by clarifying institutional mandates, operational responsibilities and accountability mechanisms.

He described the legislation as a landmark in Ghana's security sector reforms, providing a comprehensive legal framework for the organisation, coordination and oversight of national security and intelligence functions.

He maintained that a common understanding of the law among regional and district authorities was necessary to avoid institutional misunderstandings and operational lapses.

“A harmonised understanding of the legal framework will promote consistency in decision-making, enhance inter-agency coordination, improve information flow and minimise the possibility of administrative and operational lapses that could compromise our collective security,” he said.

The minister also urged participants to uphold confidentiality, professionalism, integrity and accountability in the handling of security information.

Meanwhile, the Deputy National Security Coordinator in charge of Operations, Major General Williams Azure Ayamdo (Rtd), called for improved intelligence sharing and coordinated responses to security threats across the three regions.

He warned that challenges confronting the regions could escalate when early warning signs are overlooked, information is delayed, or institutional responses are fragmented.

He urged REGSECs and assembly security councils to identify emerging threats, assess their implications and facilitate timely interventions before local incidents developed into wider security challenges.

He also called for greater cooperation among the three regions and encouraged traditional authorities and community leaders to support efforts at identifying local tensions and promoting peaceful dispute resolution.

Ghana News.title: St John’s Hospital CEO Dr Maame Yaa Afriye named Outstanding Corporate Woman at 2026 Ghana Women Awards
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of St John’s Hospital and Fertility Centre, Dr Maame Yaa Afriye, has been named Outstanding Corporate Woman at the 2026 Ghana Women Awards.

She received the award at a ceremony held at the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA) Auditorium on Saturday, November 14, 2026.

Dr Afriye was recognised for her leadership and contributions to healthcare management and service delivery.

The 2026 Ghana Women Awards brought together 23 women from various sectors, including healthcare, business, entertainment, media, engineering, sports and the security services, to recognise their contributions to society.

Other award recipients included the President of the Greater Accra Markets Association, Mercy Naa Afrowa Needjan, who received the Legendary Woman Award, and the Chief Executive Officer of Hasaacas Ladies FC, Dr Evelyn Nsiah Asare, who was named Changemaker of the Year.

Dr Afriye is a trained pharmacist with a Bachelor of Science degree in Pharmacy from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST).

She also holds a PhD in Health Policy and Management from the University of Ghana Business School, an MBA in Health Services Management, a Postgraduate Diploma in Business Administration and a Postgraduate Certificate in Supply Chain and Human Resource Management.

She has also co-authored research publications on customer relationship management and patient satisfaction, as well as the experiences of working mothers with exclusive breastfeeding in Ghana.

As head of St John’s Hospital and Fertility Centre, Dr Afriye has overseen efforts to improve the facility's operations, infrastructure, technology and patient care.

The hospital provides a range of general and specialist healthcare services, including fertility care, urology, surgery, dermatology, dental services, ear, nose and throat (ENT) care, home care and laboratory services.

The latest recognition adds to several honours Dr Afriye has received in the healthcare sector. In 2024, she was named Most Outstanding Female in Healthcare and Administrative Excellence at the Corporate Ghana Hall of Fame Awards.

Ghana News.title: ‘If a mother’s tears could bring back a child’ – Javits’ mother breaks down during tribute
Ghana News.content:
The mother of 15-year-old Badu Nkansah Frimpong, popularly known as Javits, broke down in tears during the reading of her tribute at his funeral in the Bronx, New York, as she struggled to come to terms with the loss of her only child.

The tribute, which was read on her behalf at the funeral on Friday, November 20, recounted her pain over the death of the son she had carried, nurtured and prayed for.

Standing beside the reader, Javits’ mother, Doris, became visibly emotional and broke down at the end of the reading.

In the message, she described Javits as her only son, her only child and her greatest blessing, saying that although distance separated them when he travelled to the United States to live with his father, their emotional bond remained strong.

She recalled their conversations and the dreams he shared with her, particularly his ambition to study hard, become a doctor and one day return to Ghana to take care of her and help less privileged people in their community.

“You told me that you wanted to study hard, become a doctor and return one day to take good care of me and help the less privileged in our community in Ghana,” the tribute read.

She said those words had become the foundation of her hopes and daily prayers, adding that she had imagined the day she would proudly call him “Doctor”.

'Mema mo yaakor' - New York City Major, Zohran Kwame Mamdani, in Akan language, pays tribute to 15-year-old Javits at funeral in the US. Full tribute of @NYCMayor. https://t.co/lu913DMo88 — Kenneth Awotwe Darko (@TheKennethDarko) November 20, 2026

The mother said she had looked forward to watching her son fulfil his ambitions and growing old with the comfort of knowing that he had achieved his dreams.

But his death, she said, had abruptly ended a future they had imagined together.

“My son, what hurts most is not just that you are gone, but everything you were yet to become. Your dreams, your laughter, your kindness and the beautiful future we imagined together have all been taken away,” she said.

In one of the most emotional passages, she expressed the depth of a mother's grief over the loss.

“If a mother’s tears could bring back a child, I would have cried you back into my arms. If love could defeat death, you would still be here,” the tribute read.

She ended by assuring her son that he would remain in her heart and that she would carry his dreams and memories for the rest of her life.

“Sleep well, my only son. My heart has lost its greatest treasure,” she said.

Javits was born on April 29, 2011, and moved from Ghana to the United States in 2025 to join his father and pursue his education. He aspired to become a doctor and serve in the United States military.

He was fatally shot in the Bronx on October 29, 2026, aged 15.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
