World.title: Zohran Mamdani unveils plan to close New York’s Rikers Island jail by 2032
World.content:
The plan would replace the jail complex with four smaller jails and reduce the number of people behind bars.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has unveiled a plan to close the notorious Rikers Island jail complex by 2032, setting out how his administration hopes to shut down a facility long criticised for violence, overcrowding and poor sanitation.

The plan, released on Friday, proposes closing the jail five years after a deadline of August 2027 that was set under then-Mayor Bill de Blasio.

With less than a year to go, the four smaller jails in four New York boroughs that are meant to replace Rikers are still under construction.

The jail complex mostly holds people awaiting trial rather than serving sentences after conviction.

“For decades, New Yorkers have demanded a correctional system that is safe and humane,” said Mamdani in a statement.

“We have a legal and moral obligation to close Rikers,” he said.

How does Mamdani plan to close Rikers Island?

The mayor’s strategy involves reducing the number of people held at Rikers from 6,700 to no more than 4,100 by expanding alternatives to detention, restoring online bail payments, investing in programmes that aim to reduce repeat offending, and shortening court delays.

Court delays can leave people “detained for years in what is essentially legal purgatory”, said Mamdani at a news conference on Friday. The city plans to set up a task force to deal with bottlenecks and improve how agencies share evidence.

Under the new timeline, the first replacement jail will open in Brooklyn in 2029, with the rest completed by 2032. The city plans to also make hospital beds available for people in custody who have serious mental health or medical needs.



“Any family member of someone held at Rikers will tell you how isolating that jail is, how it can take hours to visit a loved one,” Mamdani said, adding that the new jails would be closer to courts and public transport, and would help integrate imprisoned New Yorkers back into the city.

Why is Rikers Island notorious?

Rikers Island, near LaGuardia airport in New York’s East River, opened in 1932 and has long faced criticism over violence, abuse, and unsanitary conditions, with campaigners pushing for its closure for over a decade.

The facility has been tied to cases like that of Kalief Browder, who spent three years there awaiting trial before the charges against him were dismissed. He died by suicide in 2015 aged 22, two years after his release.

City lawmakers voted to close Rikers in 2019, and Mamdani has blamed the city’s inability to meet the 2027 deadline to build the replacement jails on the previous administration.

Once the jail closes, Mamdani said he wants the island to be used for renewable energy and projects to help the city withstand the effects of climate change.

“Our hope is that the new Rikers Island will be unrecognisable,” he said.

World.title: US tech sell-off continues as Anthropic tumbles after mega IPO
World.content:
Anthropic’s listing had been viewed as a potential boost for an industry struggling to regain its footing but that was not the case on Friday.

Anthropic’s much-hyped arrival on Wall Street has fizzled out a day later, as a dramatic unravelling of the artificial intelligence trade showed that even a blockbuster listing could not shake the gloom hanging over the sector.

On Friday, the stock, the biggest public stock offering ever and which surpassed $2 trillion in value at one point, was trading at $87.95, about 9.5 percent down from Thursday’s close, at about 11:30am in New York (16:30 GMT).

Widely seen as a proxy for the AI trade, Anthropic’s listing had been viewed as a potential boost for an industry struggling to regain its footing after a turbulent stretch. But the slump in price within a day of listing – though still higher than its offer price of $83.30 – while losses across other technology heavyweights suggested the IPO had done little to reverse the broader selloff.

“Investors still believe in AI but are becoming more selective about what they will pay for that growth,” said David Miller, chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds.

Among the Magnificent Seven stocks, Nvidia was down nearly 7 percent, Meta Platforms fell almost 4 percent, while Amazon and Microsoft dropped 2.1 percent and 1.7 percent, respectively.

Chip stocks also slid, with AMD down 11.2 percent, Sandisk down nearly 15 percent and Intel losing 4.3 percent.

More stocks were gaining ground within the S&P 500, but AI stocks with hefty market values have a much bigger impact on the market’s direction. They were responsible for Wall Street’s big gains this year and are now behind the big slide for the market.



AI stocks have been losing ground partly over worries that their big market values and heavy spending are unjustified. Fears of a bubble within the sector have also run up against the recent midterm elections, where there has been a shift in power after the Republican Party, seen as more friendly to the industry, suffered an electoral sweep.

Anthropic’s stock could find support later in the year; London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates index-tracking funds could account for purchases of up to 30 percent of Anthropic’s shares by year-end.

Market debuts for tech companies are often followed by a volatile period. SpaceX, which previously held the title for the biggest IPO, rose nearly 50 percent in its first three days, but fell below its IPO price a month later. On Friday, the stock was down about 7.4 percent.

World.title: Protests held across Europe over wages, services, high living costs
World.content:
Workers and students take to the streets as protests inspired by demonstrations in France show no sign of abating.

Protesters have rallied across 25 European countries amid a wave of public discontent over issues ranging from high living costs to military spending and the climate crisis, ramping up pressure on political leaders they accuse of ignoring the concerns of young people.

Inspired by demonstrations that have shaken France in recent months, thousands took to the streets in countries including the United Kingdom, Austria, Germany, Spain, Italy, Sweden and Croatia on Friday.

Tens of thousands of workers and students protested in more than 100 Italian cities to demand higher wages ⁠⁠and greater investment in public services.

The rallies coincided with a general strike by Italy’s largest trade union, CGIL, that involved workers in ‌‌both the private and public sectors, including schools and healthcare.

“Across Europe and among ordinary people, the demand for change is growing,” CGIL leader Maurizio Landini said at a rally in Rome.

Demonstrators in Rome threw objects at the Ministry of Education, while in Bologna some protesters clashed with police, news agency ANSA reported. In Milan, demonstrators set fire to a cardboard tanker as well as cardboard figures depicting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and United States President Donald Trump.

The Italian rallies ⁠⁠followed a nationwide mobilisation on October 17 that descended into rioting and looting and prompted the right-wing government of Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni to approve sweeping security measures and deploy the army alongside police in subsequent demonstrations.



Student groups have since continued protests and occupations at schools and universities, with opposition to higher military spending also emerging as a rallying cry.

Opposition leaders joining demonstrations on Friday criticised Meloni’s government and its budget policies amid rising living costs. Elly Schlein, leader of the centre-left Democratic Party, said the 2027 Budget Law “does not have a vision for the future of the country” as it does not help industries but slashes funding for public healthcare and education.

Meanwhile, in Germany, campaign group “Gen Z regelt” (German for “Gen Z sorts it”) said it ⁠⁠was organising protests in 73 cities and towns.

In Berlin, roughly 4,000 people attended a protest in the city’s ⁠⁠Alexanderplatz square.

The Cologne protest drew fewer than the 5,000 people expected, though ⁠⁠demonstrators still numbered in the thousands, police said.

Protesters gathered to call for greater education funding and to oppose a possible return to compulsory military service.

In Austria, several hundred people gathered outside the University of Vienna for a youth-led protest calling for more spending on education and less on weapons. Police dispersed the event after reported disturbances, saying officers used pepper spray and made several arrests.

In Croatia, students boycotted classes and staged protests in about a dozen cities, demanding greater investment in education, housing and public services rather than military spending.

Demonstrations across Europe were inspired by much larger protests in France that began in September and descended into violent confrontations with the police and looting.

On Tuesday, France’s Interior Ministry said a total of 146,000 people took part in protests across the country, with 28,000 in Paris alone. The CGT trade union put the nationwide total at just over 500,000 demonstrators.

The prices paid for everyday items such as food, energy, transport and bills have risen by between 59 and 78 percent since 2000 in France, Italy, Spain and Portugal, according to Eurostat – the European Union’s statistics agency.

Once inflation is taken into account, the average full-time wage in Italy fell by almost 5 percent between 2000 and 2025. Over the same period, real wages rose by 7 percent in Spain, 11 percent in France and 20 percent in Portugal, according to OECD wage data adjusted with Eurostat’s price index.

World.title: Top US Democrat warns Trump admin against destroying records
World.content:
In a new letter, Congressman Jamie Raskin says officials in the US government are ignoring federal recordkeeping laws.

A top Democrat, who will wield significant investigative powers in the United States Congress starting in January, has warned US law enforcement agencies to preserve records, including encrypted communications on digital messaging apps.

In letters sent on Thursday to the US Department of Justice and Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Congressman Jamie Raskin of Maryland, the next likely chairman of the US House Judiciary Committee, wrote to the cabinet-level agencies to remind their employees of a legal obligation to “safeguard” records against destruction.

Letters were also sent to the heads of three subagencies, including the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Bureau of Prisons (BOP).

Raskin disclosed he has obtained evidence that government officials in the Trump administration have been using non-government apps, like Signal, to send disappearing messages.

The Maryland Democrat, who is currently the Judiciary Committee’s ranking member, appended a screenshot of a Signal exchange between FBI General Counsel Samuel Ramer and Drew Lynch, an associate of President Donald Trump’s eldest son, Donald Trump Jr, showing a conversation where messages were set to automatically delete after one week.

“The FBI’s top lawyer should be ensuring that all 35,000 FBI employees are preserving government and law enforcement records”, Raskin wrote to US Attorney General Todd Blanche.

“Instead, he has conducted official business on a platform specifically configured to erase communications.”

The incident, Raskin wrote, is “just one of many” that have been reported to the Judiciary Committee, raising concern among Democrats that the Trump administration could be ignoring federal recordkeeping laws by destroying documents before likely congressional investigations.



“There is significant evidence that Trump Administration officials have engaged in the widespread destruction, mutilation, and concealment of government records”, Raskin wrote. “This attempt to evade transparency extends to the highest levels of federal agencies, including top-ranking law enforcement officials”.

Raskin instructed the federal officials to take “immediate action to recover these records” from data backups or “associated metadata,” asking them to comply by December 3.

The Trump administration has signalled it intends to fight any probes by US Democrats, who won control of both chambers of the US Congress earlier this month in the country’s midterm elections.

According to a letter viewed by Al Jazeera, the White House’s top lawyer, Will Scharf, wrote to US House Democrats on Wednesday, pushing back against demands from the incoming Democratic majorities, such as Raskin’s, because the new Congress has not yet been sworn in.

“Your demands do not reflect a request of the House, Senate, or a committee to which that body’s oversight authority has been delegated,” Scharf wrote. “As a result, Ranking Member requests in the 119th Congress do not trigger any obligation to ‘accommodate[e] … the needs of the conflicting branches'”.

In response to Raskin’s letter, a White House official told Al Jazeera the administration complies “with all federal record retention laws and regulations”.

The DOJ echoed the White House’s response, saying it “follows all legal requirements for the management of federal records involving its official functions and decisions.”

“The men and women of the DOJ who work tirelessly to arrest and prosecute criminals will not be intimidated by a congressman who once called 2020 riots ‘magnificent’ and ‘nonviolent'”, the agency said about Raskin.

Al Jazeera also reached out to DHS, FBI, ICE and BOP for comment but has not yet heard back.

World.title: UK far-right activist ‘Danny Tommo’ jailed for slashing migrant boat
World.content:
Daniel Thomas livestreamed himself slashing a dinghy used to bring migrants from France to the UK.

A British far-right anti-immigration activist has been jailed for 15 months for criminal damage for slashing a small boat which had brought migrants from France to the United Kingdom.

Daniel Thomas, also known as “Danny Tommo”, is the founder of the British anti-migrant Patriot Platform group, which mobilised hundreds of protesters earlier this year. He pleaded guilty to criminal damage earlier this month, after slashing the inflatable vessel while a French emergency responder was on board.

Sentencing Thomas on Friday, judge James Newton-Price said the offence “amounted to flagrant interference and a deliberate disruption” of French and British authorities’ important activities in the English Channel.

“They do necessary, highly sensitive and difficult jobs, and which should not be disrupted by a publicity-seeker slashing with a knife a boat they were attempting to recover,” he added.

Thomas livestreamed himself on September 22 as he followed a small boat ⁠⁠carrying migrants across the Channel, who were transferred ⁠⁠onto another vessel and taken ashore.

The 37-year-old later approached the dinghy and slashed it with a knife, soon after a French rescue worker had stepped on board. British police arrested him shortly after the incident.

Prosecutor Joel Smith told Portsmouth Crown Court that Thomas had shouted “get off the boat, you’ve got time to get off the ⁠⁠boat … take them back, no more ⁠⁠of these”.

‘Thuggish’

Thomas appeared in court via videolink from prison, with his head bowed and rarely looked up as footage of ‌‌the incident was played.



Judge Newton-Price accepted that “there was no immediate danger to the rescue worker”, but said Thomas’s actions were a deliberate ‌‌attempt ‌‌to disrupt rescue efforts.

The far-right activist had built a large online following and organised gatherings of protesters on the UK’s southern coast in response to the arrivals of small boats.

A government minister described the demonstrations as “thuggish”.

The court heard that Thomas had five previous convictions, including in 2016 for kidnapping.

Separately, he is set to stand trial in London next June accused of multiple offences, including entering a restricted zone at a migrant processing centre in Dover in March.

UK government data shows the number of people arriving in small boats to British shores has fallen, though the crossings remain a prominent political issue which has dogged successive governments. Right-wing opposition parties and anti-immigration activists have called for more action.

World.title: 10 years after divisive Brexit referendum, UK weighs a ‘Breturn’ to the EU
World.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham returns from the UK-EU summit with a potential new deal and a new start.

A decade after the narrow vote to leave the EU, the United Kingdom is showing every sign of buyer’s remorse.

For many, the bitterly fought contest over the referendum on whether to leave the EU was unpleasant and divisive.

Couples and families reportedly split over where they stood on the referendum. Each side of the debate – Leave and Remain – became a cipher for how people saw themselves and their country in a changing world.

As the campaign unfolded amid accusations of foreign influence and dirty tricks, the murder of a politician, a debate over economics and political sovereignty, a visceral fight intensified over identity, belonging and competing visions of what it meant to be British.

Critics and pro-Brexit slammed various exit deals that successive governments negotiated with Brussels as somehow a betrayal of what had originally been a binary choice.

The EU, the trading bloc the UK sat uneasily within for nearly half a century, remains the country’s biggest trading partner.

On Friday, in a joint news conference with Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission, following the latest UK-EU summit in Brussels, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham hailed the first in a series of expected deals with the EU as rebuilding “the bridges that were broken all those years ago”.

The agreements, which cover three main areas – easing trade restrictions, expanding opportunities for young people to live and work across borders, and addressing carbon levies – were characterised by Burnham as “a good deal for Britain” and regarded as first steps towards bringing the UK back into the EU’s orbit.

Does the UK want to rejoin?

Some in the UK believe that leaving the single market and customs union brought little tangible benefit while creating additional paperwork, border checks and barriers to trade with the UK’s largest export market. Others have no regrets about leaving the bloc.



According to polling expert Sir John Curtice, surveys show an average of 62 percent favour rejoining, against 38 percent for staying out, once undecided respondents are excluded.

“Whatever the nuances, the UK public are certainly in a different place on the EU than [they were] in 2016,” he told Al Jazeera.

Could the UK Breturn?

According to some analysts, the government – which is not bound by a single written constitution – could, with the EU’s agreement, begin the process of rejoining without holding another referendum, or even including the commitment in an election manifesto.

However, doing so would inevitably be politically difficult and, according to Professor Curtice, almost certain to be highly unpopular.

“The Brexit referendum in 2016 was not legally binding,” Sionaidh Douglas-Scott, the chair in Law at Queen Mary University of London, wrote by email. “Legally, it could have been ignored altogether. But it was thought to be politically unacceptable to ignore the public’s vote in the referendum. And political parties can ignore their election manifesto pledges at their peril,” she said, referring to parties’ reliance on public trust to support any agenda.

“I suspect Burnham might be tempted to have a referendum on the issue of rejoining the EU, feeling that public opinion had changed sufficiently to render a rejoin vote likely, although that’s by no means certain,” she said. “Some senior members of the [governing Labour] party … clearly feel that rejoining should be a manifesto pledge. So, politically, steps might be taken to make it more acceptable.”

Meanwhile, questions remained over the terms on which the UK might rejoin the bloc, whether it would be required to adopt the euro – a prospect it had previously resisted – and what form the EU itself might take following elections in some of its most influential member states, including France, Germany and Spain.

Polling suggests a distinction between support for closer relations with the EU as opposed to support for full membership.

While some surveys put support for rejoining at about 35 percent when closer ties were offered as an alternative, Curtice said support for closer relations was often less firmly held.

“Much of that support is soft – people say they somewhat support rather than strongly support” closer ties, he explained. By contrast, around half of those supporting rejoining the EU say they “strongly support” it, suggesting a deeper commitment to that option.



Similarly, at home, many of the more prominent figures of the original campaign to leave Europe have resurfaced and appear to be marshalling their forces against any return or realignment.

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, one of Brexit’s most prominent campaigners, returned to Brussels on Thursday to oppose the prime minister’s efforts.

Other figures associated with the Leave campaign have also re-emerged, including former Prime Minister Boris Johnson and his former cabinet ally, Michael Gove, now a magazine editor. They have revived loosely sourced claims about the financial cost of rejoining the EU – or even of having remained a member. The campaign group Stay Out, for instance, puts the annual cost at 39.3 billion pounds (approximately $51.4bn), equivalent to 750 million pounds (about $982m) a week.

“I think we should think about two things when we think about Brexit and the potential to rejoin: trauma and salience,” Anand Menon, professor at King’s College London and director of UK in a Changing Europe, said. “Some people felt traumatised by the first debate and don’t want to revisit it. At the same time, the issue has lost its salience. The public don’t consider it one of the main issues facing the country,” he said.

“If you cast your mind back to 2016, those supporting Leave, like Nigel Farage, took the EU, which the public never really thought about, and linked it in the public’s mind to something they absolutely did: immigration.

“If Burnham is going to try to get the sort of energy he’ll need to see the process through, he’s going to need to do something similar, though what, I don’t know.”

World.title: Qatar and Germany deepen strategic ties during emir’s Berlin visit
World.content:
German chancellor says Qatar pledged $16.5bn in new investments as the two countries deepen defence and technology ties.

Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani has held talks with German leaders in Berlin on expanding defence and diplomatic cooperation, broadening a relationship long focused on trade and investment.

At a joint news conference with the emir on Friday, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Qatar had pledged an additional 15 billion euros ($16.5bn) in investment, while the two governments planned closer cooperation on security and technology.

Merz said the investment would strengthen cooperation in artificial intelligence (AI), computer chips and aviation. He also expressed Germany’s interest in developing defence industry partnerships with Qatar, while the two countries agreed to work together to improve protection against cyberattacks.

The discussions come as Qatar continues pushing for a diplomatic solution to end the US-Israel war on Iran, which has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a major route for global oil and gas supplies.

Sheikh Tamim also held talks with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, who proposed a regional security conference for the Middle East.

Their meeting on Friday covered efforts to end the Iran war and restore maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, according to a joint statement by both countries.

Steinmeier suggested bringing regional governments together to build trust and address security disputes.

The emir invited him to the Doha Forum, an international policy conference in Qatar on December 5–6, to discuss the proposal further with other countries.



At the emir’s news conference with Merz, the German leader acknowledged Qatar’s role in mediating between the US and Iran and called for the Strait of Hormuz to reopen permanently. He also urged Tehran to halt its military nuclear programme.

Sheikh Tamim stressed that “peace and sustainable peace and security can only be reached through a political agreement”, adding that dialogue is the only way forward. He also described Germany as an important partner.

Sheikha Alanoud bint Hamad Al Thani, a fellow at the Middle East Council for Global Affairs, a regional research institute, told Al Jazeera in Berlin that the relationship had previously been driven mainly by commerce.

“But now we’re seeing a strategic dialogue,” she said, pointing to increasingly similar security concerns, including drone attacks on Qatar and hybrid warfare threats facing European countries.

That shift builds on a 2023 agreement to establish formal strategic talks between the two countries. Sheikh Tamim told Steinmeier on Friday that Qatar wanted the first round to take place, according to Qatar’s state news agency, QNA.

World.title: UK to explore even closer ties with EU after agreeing deal, says Burnham
World.content:
Andy Burnham said the UK will discuss possible options for even closer ties with the EU, after agreeing a deal covering British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme.

The prime minister said it was a "good day" for Britain and Europe, adding the Treasury believes the deal could boost the UK economy by up to Â£17bn a year.

European Council President AntÃ³nio Costa said the EU remains "open to have the closest possible relationship" with the UK.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the deal "isn't fair" - and Reform's Nigel Farage called it a "betrayal of the British people".

Legislation to implement the deal is expected to be introduced in the UK Parliament next week.

Burnham arrived in Brussels to finalise the latest stage of the government's post-Brexit "reset" of relations with the EU, which originally began under former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer.

The agreements announced on Friday included scrapping most of the checks on British food exports, in return for the UK following some EU regulations, from 2028.

The UK government believes the changes will cut costs for businesses and could bring prices down for shoppers, while critics argue the change will make the UK a "rule taker" from Brussels rather than a rule maker.

The new youth experience scheme will allow up to 100,000 18 to 31 year olds from the EU to travel, work and study in the UK for up to three years. The same number of young Britons will be allowed into Europe.

The two sides want to ensure that opportunities under the annual scheme will be available to young people by no later than January 2030.

A further six months is available to discuss a deal on tuition fees, which could prove to be a potential stumbling block.

There have been calls from the European side for fees to be reduced for EU students at British universities. The joint statement says any agreement would also be for UK students in the EU.

World.title: Russian missile hits Poland as Ukraine's allies hold military exercise, says Tusk
World.content:
Poland says a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that violated its airspace early on Friday, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk saying it did not appear to be an accident when Western military exercises were taking place in the region.

Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a "provocation" from Moscow.

Russia has made no comment about the violations, which took place during one of its biggest aerial attacks on Ukraine since the start of the full-scale invasion in 2022.

Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said the Kh-101 missile hit a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec in southeastern Poland about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border.

The cruise missile, designed for precision targets, crashed at about 06:30 (5:30GMT) and Natalie Szponar, a local resident, said she was getting her children ready for school when she heard a "whistle and a dull impact".

The moment of impact was caught by a camera on a farm, and officials later made clear there was no risk to residents.

Another suspected missile went down near Rudnik nad Sanem to the west of Nowy Lipowiec, and a jet-powered drone crashed to the south near MoÅodycz, said Kosiniak-Kamysz.

World.title: Russia targets Kyiv crossings days after Ukraine hits Crimean Bridge
World.content:
Russia targeted bridges in Kyiv and railway stations overnight in a major attack launched days after Ukraine badly damaged the strategically important Crimean Bridge.

Ballistic missiles hit key crossings in the capital during a nationwide assault which Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said was "one of the most massive strikes" of the war so far and left at least nine dead.

Russian President Vladimir Putin had threatened to retaliate for the attack on the Crimean Bridge, which the Kremlin built to link Russia and the occupied Crimean peninsula.

The latest Russian strikes coincided with talks around the war, and came as the Kremlin pushed back against a US claim that Russia could be open to Western-backed security guarantees for Ukraine.

The overnight attack against Ukraine was spread across several cities and regions, Zelensky said, with residential buildings and energy facilities also hit.

Air raid sirens lasted non-stop throughout the night and were ongoing into the morning.

Zelensky said over 110 missiles and more than 400 attack drones were launched by Russia, adding that "particularly insidious" tactics to launch the waves in 20 to 30-minute internals made it "more difficult to extinguish fires, clear debris, and restore services".

The three bridges targeted in Kyiv - the Podilsko-Voskresensky Bridge, the Darnytskyi Bridge and the Southern Bridge - were closed to traffic.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko urged people to "avoid travelling into the city by private car unless absolutely necessary", adding to the disruption around the capital following a first round of strikes against vital crossings earlier this week.

World.title: Anthropic shares fall after blockbuster opening as wider tech sell-off continues
World.content:
Anthropic's shares have dropped back towards their initial price after a soaring first day on the stock market, as a wider tech sell-off deepens.

The fall in tech stocks continued to weigh on markets, with the S&P 500 down more than 2% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average down 0.7% by lunchtime.

Both US indexes touched correction territory, a point where they are trading at 10% or more down from a recent high.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index also fell more than 3.4% by the middle of trading on Friday.

Despite a positive first day of trading, Anthropic's shares fell on Friday, dropping more than 12% to about $85 by lunchtime, close to its initial public offering (IPO) price of $83.

The artificial intelligence (AI) company's introduction to the Nasdaq stock exchange on Thursday was a crucial test for the industry and was largely seen as a success, with trading starting at $111.50.

The maker of the Claude chatbot raised a record $81bn in its initial public offering (IPO), but its share price moved significantly in the first day of trading.

The shares peaked at $115 on Thursday, before easing to end the day up 17% at $97.17.

Analysts said volatility was to be expected in the first days or even weeks of Anthropic's trading, as the company was the first frontier AI firm to go public so had no direct peers.

Some have also noted the similarities with Elon Musk's SpaceX, which at the time of its debut in June was the largest IPO on record. Shares in the rocket and AI company experienced large swings in its first few weeks of trading.

Ed Moya, a strategist at market intelligence firm AlphaSense, said Anthropic's blockbuster IPO did not appear to have restored confidence in the broader AI market.

While AI demand was still very strong, Moya told the BBC that investors were trying to answer the question of how much were they willing to pay for that growth.

"As we've gone through the past past few weeks, it seems that there's been more risks that have surfaced," he said.

"Right now you're starting to see Wall Street is trying to shift from rewarding growth at any price, to demanding stronger cash flow and a clearer path to profitability."

World.title: Nearly 600 women killed in South Africa within three months
World.content:
Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia said there needed to be "greater efforts to prevent... violence" against women and children.

According to police in Free State province, south of Johannesburg, three masked men opened fire on a family in the township of Botshabelo on Wednesday night.

The trio were allegedly looking for the owner of the house and when they realised he was not there, "forced their way into the house and started shooting at the people inside", police said.

The owner's wife was also shot in the stomach and was taken to hospital. No arrests have been made.

On Thursday, the police chief for Gauteng province said that eight people had now been arrested in relations to the 13 murders which sparked a national outcry earlier this year.

General Tommy Mthombeni said three of the arrests related to the murder of Elizabeth Moselakgomo, an avid runner whose disappearance prompted a highly publicised nationwide search for her.

The 38-year-old went missing while out for her daily run near her home in Kempton Park.

Her body was found badly bruised and partially clothed on 12 September.

The police chief said two other people had been detained in connection with the death of Jabulile Ntimba, 33, who was discovered half-naked and wrapped in a sheet on the side of a road in Boksburg on 17 September. Ntimba's was the ninth body found in the Ekurhuleni region.

He said another person had been arrested for one of the Kempton Park cases while a suspect was arrested over Ntombifuthi Nxumalo's death in Tembisa, north-east of central Johannesburg.

Nxumalo was discovered at a cemetery on 26 September. She was found naked with serious head injuries as well as stones near her body.

Another arrest was made back in July, in relation to the death of Busisiwe Mahlangu, whose body was found in Kempton Park on 15 July. Hers was the first of the 13 bodies discovered in the area.

In September, President Cyril Ramaphosa vowed that "no stone will be left unturned" to find those behind the killings.

Last year, he declared that violence against women was a "national disaster".

World.title: Texas death-row inmate screams as execution takes more than one hour
World.content:
A US death row inmate has screamed in apparent pain during his Texas execution which lasted more than an hour.

This is "not working the way it should be," Reinaldo Dennes, 70, said as he was being injected with the drug pentobarbital, according to witnesses.

A spokeswoman for the Texas Department of Criminal Justice said there had been unsuccessful attempts to find veins for the injections, but added that Dennes had reported pain in parts of his body where there were no attempted injections.

Dennes's case comes weeks after the botched execution of Christa Pike, who survived two lethal doses and is believed to be the only individual to have survived an execution attempt by lethal injection.

Dennes was sentenced to death over the 1996 murder of Janos Szucs, a diamond dealer who was found shot multiple times.

His execution came on the same day another inmate was put to death in Florida.

Executions with a lethal drug usually last from a few minutes to over an hour.

Michael Graczyk, an Associated Press reporter who has witnessed many such executions, described how they had waited for an unusually long time before being taken into the chamber. According to him, such delays are usually due to an inmate resisting the procedure or difficulty in finding veins.

When the witnesses were finally allowed in, Dennes almost immediately exclaimed, "The pain! Go! Go!", Graczyk said. He then uttered an expletive and asked "the father" to "take this pain".

He then shouted: "My right leg is killing me!", describing it as a cramp. After another expletive, he grunted and said, "I don't think this is normal."

Another witness, the reverend Jeff Hood, told USA Today that Dennes's execution was "by far the worst one" he had seen.

"He [Dennes] screamed out, 'my leg, my leg, my leg'," Hood said. "He screamed out twice, 'it's not working like it's supposed to.'"

World.title: Indian man sentenced to 19-plus years in plot to assassinate US-based Sikh separatist leader
World.content:
A federal judge sentenced an Indian man to 235 months, more than 19 years, in an attempted plot to kill a leading Sikh political figure in the US.

Nikhil Gupta, an Indian national, pleaded guilty to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering in February. On Friday, the judge said he likely will be deported or removed after his sentence.

US prosecutors alleged Gupta was directed by an Indian government official to kill Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, a leading figure of the Khalistan movement, which advocates for an independent homeland for Sikhs.

India has denied involvement. Its government has accused Pannun of being a terrorist, which he denies.

Pannun, an American citizen, is the spokesman for US-based Sikh separatist group Sikhs for Justice (SFJ), banned in India since 2019. He previously told the BBC, "Nikhil Gupta's guilty plea was judicial confirmation that India's Modi government orchestrated a structured murder-for-hire assassination plot on American soil".

India has opposed the Khalistan movement, and its political parties also remain opposed to the matter. Sikhs are a religious minority that make up about 2% of India's population. Some groups have long called for a separate homeland for Sikhs.

Prosecutors alleged that in May 2023, Gupta was recruited by Vikash Yadav, an Indian intelligence officer, to carry out an assassination of Pannun.

Yadav allegedly provided Gupta with personal information about Pannun, including his address in New York and information about his daily activities, prosecutors said.

At his handler's direction, Gupta contacted someone to facilitate the assassination, but that person was actually a US government informant, prosecutors said. The informant introduced Gupta to a "hitman", who was actually an undercover officer with the Drug Enforcement Agency.

Gupta was arrested in June 2023 at an airport in Prague, Czech Republic and extradited to the US. He has been held at a jail in New York pending his sentencing Friday at a Manhattan court.

"He thought that from outside this country he could kill someone in it without consequence, simply for exercising their American right to free speech," then-US attorney Jay Clayton said in a statement, after announcing Gupta's guilty plea.

Narinder Singh Randhawa, a Sikh separatist and successor of Hardeep Singh Nijjar as temple leader in Surrey, British Columbia, told the BBC the sentencing marks the "first time we see justice" against what he calls historic and systemic persecution of Sikhs by the Indian government in India and abroad.

Inderjeet Gosal, another Sikh separatist advocate based in Ontario, called the sentencing "a big community event".

"It's for all the community to finally witness someone getting caught red-handed."

World.title: Catherine Zeta-Jones' daughter says parents warned her about 'nepo baby' label
World.content:
Catherine Zeta-Jones's daughter has said her parents warned her people might have "preconceived notions" about her embarking on an acting career, as she shared her views on the "nepo baby" label.

Carys Douglas, 23, made her stage debut this year, playing the lead role of Nina in Anton Chekhov's The Seagull in Brooklyn, New York.

Zeta-Jones, who is married to Michael Douglas, son of Hollywood star Kirk, previously said the "nepo baby" term was "horrific". It refers to children of famous parents perceived to have achieved riches and success off their parents' backs.

But the young actor said her parents taught her to build her "own identity" and she has learned how to deal with the "pressure".

During an interview with Elle Spain, Carys Douglas said her parents "do not hide" from her that people would have preconceived ideas about her.

"They taught me that building my own identity depended on me and no one else. It was my responsibility, and it still is.

"As time has gone on, I've come to understand that there are different ways to deal with that kind of pressure," she said.

Her father, star of hit 1980s films such as Wall Street and Fatal Attraction, recently stated that he is not a fan of the "nepo baby" label, calling it an "unfortunate title".

"I guess you could say that about any business. The same thing with Hollywood royalty. My father's father was a junkman," Douglas, 82, said, referring to Kirk, who was considered a Hollywood Golden Age icon.

Zeta-Jones, 57, from Mumbles, Swansea, also criticised the phrase, saying it was "horrible because these kids didn't ask to be born into this, they're finding their own way in life".

"You have to go with your dreams, your passion," Zeta-Jones said.

She added: "But they love it, and they're good. Otherwise, Michael and I would be the first to go, 'you know what? Maybe law school looks really good'."

World.title: Tompolo, Okpebholo target 2.5m votes for Tinubu in Edo; group donates 25 vehicles for campaign
World.content:
The Grand Patron of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, and Edo State Governor Senator Monday Okpebholo have set a target of 2.5 million votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 16 January 2027 presidential election.

The duo made the declaration in Benin City, Edo State, during the inauguration of the state chapter of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, established to mobilise grassroots support for Tinubu’s re-election.

President Tinubu is the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate in the election.

Tompolo, represented by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, Kestin Pondi, also donated 25 campaign vehicles equipped with loudspeakers, generators and amplifiers to facilitate the mobilisation campaign across the state.

He said the vehicles would be deployed to take the message of Tinubu’s administration to households, markets, churches and communities, urging residents to support the president for another four years.

He said although Nigerians were experiencing economic difficulties, the reforms introduced by Mr Tinubu were beginning to yield results, adding that the benefits would gradually extend to small businesses and ordinary citizens.

According to him, the president needs another four years to consolidate the foundation his administration has already laid.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Big businesses are already benefiting from the reforms. In no distant time, the benefits will get to small businesses,” he said.

Tompolo urged members of the movement to engage their neighbours, relatives and community members, explaining the administration’s policies and persuading them to vote for Mr Tinubu.

Also speaking, Mr Okpebholo said the 2.5 million-vote target was a commitment to Mr Tinubu, stressing that the state would work to deliver promised votes.

He described Tompolo as a great leader for establishing a grassroots political mobilisation platform, adding that the initiative would strengthen support for Tinubu’s continuity in office.

The governor called on party members and supporters to take the campaign to individual homes and communities to ensure that the target was achieved.

Earlier, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Sunday Asuku, said the initiative was established to mobilise Nigerians for Mr Tinubu’s re-election, insisting that the president deserved another four years to consolidate his reforms.

Mr Asuku argued that the administration had improved allocations to states and local governments, strengthened their financial capacity and enabled state governments to meet salary and pension obligations while executing development projects.

Also speaking, the Edo State APC Chairman, Jarrett Tenebe, said the state party leadership was committed to delivering the votes the President promised.

Mr Tenebe cited Mr Tinubu’s support for the emergence of a South-south son as senate president and other appointments given to people from the region as reasons for the zone to reciprocate through massive electoral support.

He expressed confidence that the inauguration of the movement would strengthen the party’s grassroots mobilisation and help Edo State achieve the 2.5 million votes target.

World.title: Police arrest nine over alleged N8.6 million robbery in Ibadan
World.content:
The Oyo State Police Command has arrested nine suspects over an alleged robbery in Ibadan, during which valuables worth N8.62 million were reportedly stolen from a motorist and his friends.

The suspects were arrested following an attack on a Toyota Camry occupied by Oyewole Wisdom and his friends in the Agugu area of Ibadan on 18 November.

The Police Public Relations Officer, Ayanlade Olayinka, disclosed this in a statement on Friday.

According to the police, the incident occurred around 4 p.m. as Mr Wisdom drove his newly acquired, unregistered Toyota Camry around the Bus-Stop Gate area. A group of hoodlums reportedly chased the vehicle to the Adekile area, where they attacked its occupants and dispossessed them of their valuables.

“The stolen items include an iPhone 17 Pro Max, an iPhone Air, an iPhone 16 Plus, an 11-gram gold necklace, a 2.5-gram gold ring, two power banks and a Dell laptop, with a combined estimated value of N8,620,000. In addition to the robbery, the assailants inflicted extensive damage on the victim’s vehicle, valued at N10,000,000,” the statement said.

After receiving a report of the incident, operatives of the Agugu Police Division visited the scene and launched an investigation that led to the arrest of nine suspects.

They were identified as Olaitan Adegbite, Oladayo Mohammed, Moruf Mufutau, Toheeb Taofeek, Segun Olalere, Animashun Ibrahim, Gbolarinwa Tajudeen, Ridwan Omotosho and Ajala Opeyemi.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The police said preliminary investigations indicated that the suspects had confessed to their alleged involvement in the robbery and were providing useful information to investigators.

Items recovered from the suspects included an iPhone 16 Plus, two power banks, a vehicle bumper, a car charger and the vehicle key.

The command said the suspects and recovered exhibits would be transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Iyaganku, Ibadan, for further investigation.

The Commissioner of Police, Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, urged residents to remain vigilant, provide credible information to security agencies and report suspicious activities.

He said the suspects would be charged in court after the investigation concluded.

World.title: Tinubu’s reforms make Nigerian passport processing easier – Oshiomhole
World.content:
Edo North Senator Adams Oshiomhole says Nigerians living in the country and abroad can now apply for, renew, and obtain international passports more easily because of reforms introduced by the Bola Tinubu administration.

Mr Oshiomhole, chairman of the Senate Committee on Interior, said there had been significant improvements in the passport application and collection processes, unlike in the past when citizens struggled to obtain the travel document.

He spoke on Friday at the groundbreaking ceremony for the National Passport Booklet Production Centre at the headquarters of the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) in Abuja. The facility will be Nigeria’s first domestic passport booklet production centre.

Mr Oshiomhole, a former governor of Edo State, referenced the experience of his grandchildren, who, he said, had been unable to obtain Nigerian passports despite several attempts in previous years.

He said the reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration have made it possible for them to obtain the passports.

“They (grandchildren) tell me, ‘Grandpa, now I have a Nigerian passport.’ So these are not in the advert; they are real stories that speak to what is changing, the real meaning of Renewed Hope,” he said.

The senator also recalled how Nigerians in the diaspora had been stranded and unable to visit their families in the country because their passports had expired and they could not renew them.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He commended the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, for his foresight in making passport applications and renewals easier for Nigerians living abroad.

“Within months of the honourable minister’s assumption of office, these issues were dealt with satisfactorily.

“If a man couldn’t get a passport, even as a Nigerian who wants to come home as a patriot, he couldn’t. He was being frustrated by the incompetence of the Nigerian state. And now that Nigeria is celebrating, has renewed his hope in our country, the Renewed Hope Agenda, I believe, is what is being translated here and now,” he added.

Mr Oshiomhole said the new facility would make passport production easier, more affordable and more efficient for Nigerians.

For years, obtaining or renewing a Nigerian international passport has been a frustrating experience for many citizens, with applicants frequently complaining about processing delays, difficulty securing appointments, shortages of passport booklets, and alleged demands for unofficial payments by some immigration officials.

The challenges have also affected Nigerians living abroad, some of whom have complained about difficulties renewing expired passports or obtaining new ones at Nigerian diplomatic missions. For some, the delays have disrupted travel plans, prevented them from visiting family members in Nigeria and created difficulties with immigration and residency requirements in their countries of residence.

These challenges have repeatedly raised questions about the efficiency of the Nigeria Immigration Service, which administers passports and other immigration-related services.

In recent years, the federal government has announced reforms aimed at improving passport application, processing and collection. These include efforts to simplify application procedures, reduce processing delays, improve access to passport services and expand the country’s passport production capacity.

Establishing a domestic passport booklet production centre is expected to further address challenges in the supply of passport booklets by reducing Nigeria’s dependence on foreign production and increasing the availability of the travel document.

However, the effectiveness of these interventions will ultimately depend on whether applicants can obtain their passports promptly and without unnecessary bureaucratic hurdles, both in Nigeria and at diplomatic missions abroad.

READ ALSO: How Tinubu transformed NIS in three years Interior Minister

Nigeria targets six million passports annually

In his remarks, Mr Tunji-Ojo said the passport booklet production centre would enable Nigeria to increase its production capacity to six million booklets annually.

He added that the government planned to expand capacity further to 10 million booklets annually.

“The requirement of Nigeria is roughly between 1.8 million and two million passports a year, but by May we will have the capacity for six million passports a year, which we are going to scale to 10 million passports a year,” he said.

World.title: Ekiti Poll: Parties adopt final addresses before tribunal as Oyebanji urges dismissal of petitions
World.content:
Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) on Friday asked the state Governorship Election Petitions Tribunal to dismiss the petitions filed by the Social Democratic Party (SDP) and the Action Alliance (AA) against the conduct of the 20 June governorship election.

Mr Oyebanji, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate in the election, and INEC, which conducted the poll, maintained that the petitions are incompetent, full of defects, and constitute gross violations of the provisions of the Electoral Act 2026.

They stated this through their counsel before the three-member panel led by Abubakar Kutigi during the adoption of final written addresses by parties in the two separate petitions.

Mr Oyebanji, who was represented by his lead counsel, Onyechi Ikpeazu (SAN), argued that the petitioners (SDP and AA) have not proved that his return as governor was invalid by reason of non-compliance with the provisions of the Electoral Act 2026.

The governor further contended that the petitioners failed to place concrete and convincing evidence before the Tribunal that his election was valid despite the alleged corrupt practices in their petitions.

Mr Ikpeazu, who adopted the written addresses on behalf of his client (Oyebanji) and relied on the contents of the addresses, urged the jury to dismiss the petitions and hold that the governor’s election was valid and satisfied the provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 and the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended).

In the SDP case, INEC lead counsel, Sulaiman Ibrahim (SAN), who also canvassed the dismissal of the petition, identified three major issues for determination in the petition.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Adopting his written address on behalf of the electoral umpire, Ibrahim maintained that the evidence of the petitioner’s witnesses brought to the tribunal by the SDP from PW 1 to PW 57 was hearsay, which has no basis in law urging the Tribunal to discountenance the said evidence.

Adopting INEC’s written address in the AA petition, Wendy Kuku (SAN), who urged the tribunal to throw out the petition “as far as the law can reach,” also urged the panel to do so with substantial costs.

But the SDP counsel, Nnamdi Chukwudebelu, who adopted the final written address on behalf of his client, urged the tribunal to uphold the petition in the interest of Justice.

Mr Chukwudebelu, who also appeared for AA and adopted its final written address, urged the tribunal to grant the petitioner’s prayers.

After all the parties had adopted their written addresses, the tribunal chairman, Mr Kutigi, who spoke on behalf of the other two panel members, Aminu Tukur and Maurice Okediya, reserved judgment till a later date to be communicated to the parties in the petition.

After Mr Oyebanji was declared the re-elected governor, the SDP and the AA filed separate petitions urging the tribunal to nullify the victory on grounds of non-compliance with the Electoral Act and allegations of corrupt practices at the poll.

The APC, with Mr Oyebanji as its flag bearer, won the election with 319,224 votes, while the SDP, which had Adebayo Alade as its candidate, polled 179 votes. Alade later withdrew from the petition, and the party continued the legal battle.

The AA, which had Olu Omotoso as its candidate, scored 126 votes. The People’s Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Wole Oluyede, received 40,543 votes and had earlier withdrawn his petition from the Tribunal.

World.title: SIIPS Report: Nigeria’s payment system retains status as Africa’s only “mature” system
World.content:
Nigeria’s National Instant Payment (NIP) system has retained its status as the only “mature” instant payment system (IPS) in Africa, according to the 2026 State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems (SIIPS) report released on Thursday.

The SIIPS report is an annual flagship publication of the AfricaNenda Foundation that assesses the inclusivity of instant payment systems across the continent.

Instant payment systems are open-loop retail payment platforms that enable irrevocable, low-value digital credit transactions in near real time, 24 hours a day, year-round.

The report assesses all operational instant payment systems annually and classifies them into four categories based on their level of inclusivity: unranked, basic, progressed and mature.

Last year, Nigeria’s NIP became the first and only instant payment system in Africa to attain the mature status, during the launch of the 2025 edition of the report in Eswatini.

At the launch of the 2026 edition on Thursday, AfricaNenda’s Deputy Chief Executive Officer, Sabine Mensah, announced that Nigeria had retained the status.

Ms Mensah said the NIP system had sustained public trust, incorporated an identification system for user verification and maintained a strong consumer recourse mechanism.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

A year after Nigeria’s system attained the matured category, no other instant payment system on the continent has reached that level.

According to the report, eight systems remain unranked, while 19 are classified as basic and 11 as progressed.

The unranked systems are KWiK (Angola), EPS (Eswatini), LeSwitch (Lesotho), Natswitch (Malawi), GIMTEL Switch Mobile (Mauritania), PCVI (Morocco), SIPS (Somalia) and PAPSS (pan-African).

Systems classified under the basic inclusivity category include Switch Mobile (Algeria), BurundiPay (Burundi), Meeza Digital (Egypt), Gamswitch Interbank Transfer (The Gambia), NimbaPay (Guinea), Kenya Mobile Money, PesaLink (Kenya), Pay Na-Na (Liberia), LYPay (Libya), Madagascar Mobile Money, SWAM (Morocco), SIMOrede (Mozambique), eNaira (Nigeria), SaPS (Sierra Leone), PayShap and RTC (South Africa), Tunisia Mobile Money, Uganda Mobile Money and TCIB (SADC).

At the progressed level are IPN (Egypt), EthioPay (Ethiopia), Ghana Mobile Money Interoperability, GIP (Ghana), MauCAS (Mauritius), eKash (Rwanda), TIPS (Tanzania), National Financial Switch (Zambia), ZIPIT (Zimbabwe), GIMACPAY (CEMAC) and PI-SPI (WAEMU).

Fraud concerns

Speaking on the report, AfricaNenda CEO Robert Ochola raised concerns about increasing fraud levels across the continent.

He said many customers do not report fraud incidents, possibly because several payment systems lack effective consumer recourse mechanisms. He suggested that this weakness partly explained why Nigeria’s NIP remained the continent’s only mature system.

Mr Ochola urged regulators and payment system developers across Africa to collaborate, noting that Nigeria had established a benchmark other countries could adopt.

“There are different efforts that are happening at different levels across the continent. What we want to believe is that there’s a baseline where we should all be at that minimum baseline, and therefore it calls for more conversations, for countries to understand that they shouldn’t be making the same mistakes other countries have made. So we have a best, best in class in NIP today,” he said.

He also warned that artificial intelligence had significantly increased the threat of fraud, urging leaders across the continent to abandon isolated approaches to developing payment systems.

Methodology

The report draws on several primary sources of data and analysis, including information on instant payment systems collected directly from central banks and system operators between January and July 2026.

It also incorporates demand-side survey data from 1,403 individuals and micro, small and medium-sized enterprise (MSME) users of digital payment services across 15 African markets.

In addition, the researchers interviewed payment system operators, regulators, and technical experts.

World.title: 2027: INEC selects 598 Delta polling units for mock accreditation
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it will deploy 598 polling units across Delta’s 25 local government areas for mock accreditation and result upload ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The INEC’s Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Delta, Etekamba Udo-Umoren, disclosed this at a news conference on Friday in Asaba.

Mr Udo-Umoren said the exercise, scheduled for 28 November, would test the reliability of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and assess INEC’s operational preparedness.

He explained that two polling units would be selected from each Registration Area across the state to provide broad geographical coverage for the exercise.

According to him, polling units will open at 7:30 a.m., with accreditation commencing at 8 a.m. and closing at 2:30 p.m.

The REC emphasised that the exercise is strictly a simulation, not an actual election, and stressed that no winners or losers would emerge.

He said the exercise would also evaluate accreditation, voting, result recording, transmission and other relevant election-day procedures.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Udo-Umoren added that INEC would assess personnel preparedness, logistics, transportation and timely deployment of election materials and equipment.

He said that identified technical, operational and logistical challenges would be documented and addressed before the 2027 general elections.

The REC noted that election officials would be assessed on professionalism, discipline, neutrality and compliance with established electoral guidelines.

He urged political parties, security agencies, civil society organisations, community leaders and other stakeholders to support the exercise.

Mr Udo-Umoren particularly called on the media to educate the public about the exercise and report its activities accurately.

He also appealed to politicians, youths and community leaders to maintain peace and cooperate with electoral officials.

The election official said INEC would collaborate with security agencies to ensure the exercise is conducted peacefully and in an orderly manner.

He explained that feedback from officials, observers, stakeholders and technical personnel would guide improvements in electoral procedures and operations.

Mr Udo-Umoren reaffirmed INEC’s commitment to conducting free, fair, credible, transparent, inclusive and peaceful elections in the country.

He described the mock as an important step toward strengthening the commission’s preparedness for the 2027 elections.

(NAN)

World.title: Hypo donates 20 cartons of Hypo Bleach to NCDC in support of efforts against Ebola
World.content:
Hypo Homecare Products Limited, makers of Hypo household hygiene products, has donated twenty (20) cartons of Hypo Multi-Purpose Bleach to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) in support of the Centre’s efforts to prevent and contain the spread of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in Nigeria.

The donation, which was formally presented to the NCDC, was received on behalf of the Centre by Tajudeen Arowolo, Head of Department, Health Emergency Preparedness and Response. The gesture reflects Hypo’s commitment to supporting public health efforts and promoting better hygiene and sanitation practices across Nigerian communities. The NCDC welcomed the contribution as Hypo reaffirmed its commitment to playing a role in the collective effort to protect public health.

As a household hygiene brand with a longstanding commitment to keeping homes and shared spaces clean and hygienic, Hypo recognises the importance of proper hygiene and environmental sanitation in supporting public health. Through its range of cleaning and disinfection products, the brand continues to encourage consumers to maintain cleaner and more hygienic environments.

Speaking on the donation, Ifeoluwa Adeyemo, Senior Brand Manager, Hypo, said:

“At Hypo, we believe that protecting public health is a collective responsibility. As a brand committed to providing effective cleaning and disinfection solutions, we recognise the importance of supporting efforts that promote healthier and safer communities. This donation is our way of contributing to the ongoing efforts against Ebola Virus Disease and demonstrating our commitment to the well-being of Nigerians.”

Acknowledging the contribution, Dr Odianosen Ehiakhamen, Incident Manager for Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in Nigeria, said:

“We’re grateful for the support we have just received from Hypo, providing us with IPC commodities to strengthen IPC practices, especially in health facilities. These 20 cartons of 500ml hypochlorite solution will go a long way in supporting health facilities in the states, particularly through the state preparedness and response systems for EVD and other outbreak diseases. Thank you so much, Hypo, for the support.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Beyond the product donation, Hypo is also committed to supporting broader public awareness efforts through hygiene education. The brand recognises that access to effective hygiene solutions must go hand in hand with the knowledge and adoption of appropriate hygiene practices.

Through planned public awareness and hygiene education initiatives, Hypo aims to encourage better hygiene habits, promote responsible sanitation practices and reinforce the importance of maintaining clean and hygienic environments in homes and communities.

The donation underscores Hypo’s continued commitment to making a positive contribution to society, extending its role beyond providing household cleaning and disinfection products to supporting initiatives that promote healthier living.

World.title: Tinubu appoints new commissioner for National Assembly Service Commission
World.content:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has approved the appointment of Agboola Dabiri as Commissioner representing the South-West in the National Assembly Service Commission (NASC).

Mr Dabiri replaces Taiwo Oluwa, who resigned her appointment on 30 March 2026, to contest in the 2027 General Elections for the Irewole/Isokan Federal Constituency of Osun State.

Until his appointment, Mr Dabiri served as Commissioner for Youth and Social Development in Lagos State. He also previously served as Mandate Secretary for Economic Planning, Revenue Generation and Public-Private Partnership in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

The appointment is part of the president’s efforts to ensure effective representation and inclusivity in the National Assembly Service Commission.
