World.title: 2027: Court sacks ADC governorship candidate in Adamawa
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday ordered the removal of Tukur Ribadu as the 2027 Adamawa governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

Justice Obiora Egwuatu, in a judgment, held that Mr Omar Suleiman, who won the majority of the valid votes cast in the primary election of the party, was unlawfully substituted by Ribadu.

Justice Egwuatu ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately restore Suleiman as the rightful candidate of the party.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Suleiman, a cousin of former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Babachir Lawal, was said to have initially emerged as the ADC’s candidate in the Adamawa primary.

However, he was later replaced by Ribadu.

Dissatisfied, Suleiman filed a suit marked FHC/ABJ/C’S/1751/2026 before Justice Egwuatu to challenge his unlawful substitution.

He prayed the court to order the ADC to forward his name to the electoral umpire as a valid candidate of the party.

He also prayed the court to compel INEC to publish his name as the candidate of the party.

Delivering the judgment, Justice Egwuatu held that Suleiman could only be replaced as a candidate if he had formally and voluntarily withdrawn from the race or died.

He ruled that since Suleiman had neither withdrawn nor died, his replacement was illegal, null and void.

The judge consequently ordered INEC to immediately restore his name as the ADC governorship candidate for Adamawa State in the forthcoming governorship poll. (NAN)

World.title: Vandalism, illegal connections threaten Kano water supply
World.content:
Over 45 pipeline repairs completed, says commissioner

By Hadiza Yusuf

KANO — The Kano State Government has warned residents against vandalism, illegal connections and other activities capable of damaging public water infrastructure and disrupting the supply of drinking water across the state.

The Commissioner for Water Resources, Dr Dahiru Muhammad Hashim, gave the warning at a press conference in Kano on Friday while briefing journalists on the progress of ongoing rehabilitation of water facilities and restoration of supply to communities.

Hashim said the ministry had identified cases of unauthorised connections to water pipelines, vandalism, indiscriminate drilling around major water lines and improper handling of distribution valves.

He added that some water pipes had also been damaged by construction activities, refuse burning and other activities around drainage channels.

“We appeal to the general public to cooperate with the Ministry in protecting water infrastructure. Our assessment has identified cases of unauthorised tapping of pipelines, vandalism and damage to pipes crossing drainage channels,” he said.

The commissioner urged residents, contractors and those executing construction, road and drainage projects to consult relevant authorities before embarking on activities that could affect water pipelines.

He also called on residents to promptly report burst pipes, leakages, suspected vandalism and illegal connections to the appropriate authorities.

According to him, the restoration of water supply has exposed weaknesses in some old pipelines, many of which had remained without regular water flow for several years.

He explained that the return of water pressure to the distribution network had resulted in leakages and pipe bursts in some locations, necessitating urgent repairs and replacement of damaged infrastructure.

Hashim disclosed that the ministry had completed more than 45 repair and replacement interventions across different parts of the metropolis.

The affected areas include Goron Dutse, Jakara, Kofar Ruwa, Kurmi, Dukawa, Kofar Wambai, Fagge, Club Road, Tudun Wada, Gidan Zakka, Gabari, Koki, Mandawari and Sharada.

He said the interventions involved replacing damaged asbestos-cement pipes, fixing leaking PVC pipelines, installing valves and repairing faulty connections.

The commissioner further disclosed that water had been pumped from Challawa Water Works to the Goron Dutse reservoirs, which have a reported capacity of 42.5 million litres, before being released into the distribution network.

He listed communities that had received water to include Goron Dutse, Gwammaja, Jakara, Kofar Mazugal, Muskwani, Kofar Wambai, Mandawari, Fagge, Tudun Wada, Gama, Kofar Ruwa and Alfindiki, among others.

Hashim said the government was also working to improve access through the installation of public standpipes in communities where household water connections had yet to be fully restored.

“Protecting water facilities is a responsibility we all share, and the cooperation of residents is vital to sustaining the improvements made in restoring water supply across Kano,” he said.

World.title: Tinubu Must Stay group set to unveil presidential library, reform observatory
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation TMS, popularly known as Tinubu Must Stay, has announced plans to establish a National Reform Documentation and Impact Observatory, a public digital policy archive and a possible future presidential library for President Bola Tinubu.

Chairman of the Board of Trustees and National Coordinator of the group, Malam Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, disclosed this on Friday during the commissioning of its National Secretariat in Abuja.

He said the records would start with Tinubu’s years as Governor of Lagos State between 1999 and 2007, then cover policy developments under successive administrations, his national political career and his presidency from 2023.

According to him, the archive would span public revenue administration, infrastructure, investment, education, economic management, digital transformation and institutional development. Students, researchers, historians, policymakers and ordinary citizens would be given access to original documents, implementation records, economic data and independent assessments.

Inuwa said the library, the observatory and the archive remained long-term aspirations that would need feasibility studies, sustainable funding, proper governance and professional archival standards.

“History serves future generations when it preserves evidence, not merely admiration,” he said.

He added that the documentation must make room for achievements, implementation difficulties, independent criticism and lessons learned.

The announcement came with a membership claim. Inuwa said the group, formally launched on October 1, 2026, had recorded 61,093 validated members within seven weeks across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

He said the group had representation in 730 of the country’s 774 local government areas, about 94 per cent geographical coverage. Its digital database also captures 4,750 wards and 22,584 polling units.

Inuwa said 65 per cent of members, roughly 40,000 people, were aged between 18 and 34, while the membership was 65 per cent men and 35 per cent women.

“The most remarkable feature of our membership is its youthful composition. This is not merely a demographic statistic. It places a profound responsibility upon our institution,” he said.

He said young Nigerians needed more than a seat in political conversations, naming quality education, employable skills, technology, finance and markets as what would turn the country’s demographic potential into prosperity. To that end, the group would run grassroots entrepreneurship workshops, digital skills training, mentorship programmes and policy dialogues.

“Today, we are not merely opening an office. We are opening a new chapter in our responsibility to Nigeria,” he said.

Inuwa said the secretariat would serve as a centre for research, civic engagement, youth empowerment and the documentation of policies and institutions shaping national development.

He insisted that the group intended to outlive the 2027 general elections, even though it openly backs the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda. He said it would encourage evidence-based assessment of government policies, including their implementation challenges and social consequences.

He acknowledged that the administration’s changes to petrol subsidies, foreign exchange management and fiscal policy had drawn mixed reactions, with some Nigerians seeing them as necessary to fix long-standing structural weaknesses and others worried about implementation and hardship in households.

“Reform is not an end in itself. Its purpose is to improve the lives of people,” he said.

On voter readiness, Inuwa said the group’s records showed that 81 per cent of respondents already held Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), 11 per cent had yet to collect theirs and six per cent were not registered to vote. The remaining two per cent, he said, required reconciliation.

He cautioned that large membership figures did not automatically translate into effective grassroots structures or measurable results.

“Our responsibility is to convert organisational reach into meaningful public value. We must move from membership registration to meaningful participation, from participation to capability, and from capability to opportunity,” he said.

Inuwa said the group would spend its first 90 days assessing operational capacity, developing programme standards and setting realistic targets before publishing measurable commitments. He stressed that it was independently established, with its own leadership, governance structures and membership system, despite its declared support for the President.

He urged the public to judge the organisation by its contributions to civic education, economic empowerment and sustainable development, not by membership figures or political declarations.

“A building can be completed with bricks, cement and steel. An institution must be built with integrity, competence, discipline, trust and a commitment to service,” he said.

Turning to the approaching elections, Inuwa expressed concern over reports of political intimidation, attacks on political gatherings and inflammatory public rhetoric. He condemned political thuggery and violence, irrespective of who was involved, and asked security agencies to investigate incidents impartially.

He called on political parties, civic organisations, the media and security institutions to promote peaceful participation, accurate information and respect for opposing views, and urged members to reject intimidation and misinformation.

“Political differences must never become a justification for violence. No political ambition is worth the life of an innocent Nigerian,” he warned.

World.title: Trump urges Nvidia to give Jensen Huang ‘second chance’
World.content:
(FILES) Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Photo by Philip FONG / AFP

US President Donald Trump on Friday called for AI giant Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang after he was ousted as CEO over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

“I would love to see him be back. You have one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world, and where is he going to go? I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance,” Trump told reporters.

World.title: Nasarawa attracts $2.3bn investments in seven years — Abdullahi
World.content:
Records 21 reforms, 11 PPP projects worth ₦93bn

By John Alechenu

ABUJA — Nasarawa State has attracted more than $2.3 billion in investments over the past seven years following reforms and institutional development aimed at making the state more competitive and investor-friendly.

The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nasarawa Investment and Development Agency, Ibrahim Abdullahi, disclosed this at the 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja.

Abdullahi said the investments cut across agriculture, solid minerals, retail, commercial activities, manufacturing, agro-processing and education.

He added that the state also implemented 11 public-private partnership (PPP) projects valued at about ₦93 billion within the period.

According to him, the achievements were the outcome of seven years of reforms and deliberate institution-building under Governor Abdullahi Sule, rather than publicity campaigns or political slogans.

Recounting the beginning of the process, Abdullahi said he was invited into the Nasarawa State public service seven years ago, when Governor Sule appointed him as economic adviser.

He said the assignment was to develop the state’s investment profile and position it as an attractive destination for investors.

He thanked the organisers of the forum for recognising Governor Sule with an honour presented a few days earlier.

Abdullahi said one of the first lessons from the assignment was the need to establish the necessary structures before embarking on investment promotion.

“So we could not go out and invite people to come to Nasarawa State without building any framework around it. That is to say that you cannot communicate something that is not there. You cannot communicate something that hasn’t been built. So, we put our heads down and began to build,” he said.

He explained that the state’s vision, as contained in the Nasarawa Economic Development Strategy, was to make it one of Nigeria’s most competitive states through improved and accelerated economic growth that would translate into better living conditions for residents.

Under the strategy, he said, the government implemented more than 21 reforms focused on improving the business environment and making the state attractive to investors.

He said the reforms were designed to guarantee a conducive business climate, competitive returns on investment and improved general welfare for residents.

According to him, the measures included the digitisation of revenue administration and improvements in the state’s fiscal and financial management framework.

Abdullahi said the reforms provided the foundation for the state to confidently promote its investment opportunities to local and international investors.

He noted that investors were attracted not by impressive speeches but by predictability, transparency, good returns and a government that honoured its commitments.

The investment agency chief said the experience offered important lessons to other state governments and public relations professionals, stressing that investment attraction should begin with building the necessary structures rather than merely branding a destination.

He also highlighted the importance of purpose in communication, saying communicators must be clear about the objectives they seek to achieve.

“Do I want to communicate to build or destroy? Once you have that conviction and a sense of purpose, it guides how you even communicate your message,” he said.

On reputation management, Abdullahi said credibility was essential to attracting and retaining investors, adding that reputation required deliberate efforts to establish and sustain.

“Your reputation is not just earned, you have to build it,” he said.

He identified courage and collaboration as other important ingredients for success, noting that people and institutions seeking meaningful progress must be willing to pursue new ideas and take bold decisions.

“There is no price tag for the best idea. Everywhere around the world, everyone who is succeeding has had to show a remarkable amount of zeal and courage,” he said.

World.title: MDGIF delivers 25 operational CNG stations nationwide
World.content:
Fund backs 31 projects, as FG expands university initiative to 20 institutions

By Uzoma Marvellous

The Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF) has supported the delivery of 25 operational Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) stations across the country in two years, with its investment portfolio expanding to 31 projects comprising 205 infrastructure assets.

The Executive Director of MDGIF, Mr Oluwole Adama, disclosed this during the commissioning of CNG refuelling facilities at the University of Lagos (UNILAG), University of Ibadan (UI), Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA) and Federal University Oye-Ekiti (FUOYE) on Thursday.

Adama said the achievements reflected the Federal Government’s efforts to deepen domestic gas utilisation, expand infrastructure and make natural gas more accessible to motorists and transport operators.

“In just two years, MDGIF has supported the delivery of 25 fully operational CNG stations nationwide, bringing cleaner, more affordable fuel closer to motorists and transport operators,” he said.

Established under Section 52 of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA), the fund supports investments in midstream and downstream gas infrastructure.

Adama disclosed that the UNILAG facility was the 11th CNG station being commissioned in Lagos State, adding that nine additional university stations, mostly in Northern Nigeria, would be commissioned within weeks.

“Eleven stations in one state is a clear signal that CNG is no longer a promise for tomorrow. In Lagos, it is becoming part of everyday life,” he said.

Meanwhile, the Federal Government is expanding its university CNG initiative to 20 institutions, with 11 stations already commissioned under the programme.

The Chief Executive Officer of Femadec Energy Limited, Engr. Fola Akinnola, said the company planned to complete six additional stations before the end of 2026, while the remaining three would be commissioned early in 2027.

The programme began with facilities at the University of Abuja, Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, and Federal University of Technology, Owerri.

Four other facilities were subsequently commissioned at the University of Uyo, University of Calabar, Federal University of Petroleum Resources, Effurun, and University of Nigeria, Enugu Campus.

Akinnola said the 20-campus initiative was designed to reduce transportation costs for students, lecturers and other university employees while promoting cleaner energy adoption.

“Campus communities are dynamic hubs of daily movement, where high transportation costs directly impact students, faculty and support staff alike. By systematically delivering this 20-campus network, we are providing immediate, practical relief—cutting campus transit fuel costs while significantly lowering carbon emissions,” he said.

He added that the facilities would also serve as practical training centres, exposing engineering and technical students to gas infrastructure management, vehicle conversion, maintenance and international safety standards.

“Each of these stations is designed as a living laboratory. Consistent with our commitment to technical capacity building, these facilities serve as hands-on training and conversion hubs,” he said.

The Minister of Education, Dr Maruf Tunji Alausa, said the programme, known as the Special Palliative Relief on University Transportation (Project SPROUT), was designed to address the high cost of commuting among students and university workers.

“Through the Special Palliative Relief on University Transportation, known as Project SPROUT, we are addressing one major concern students raise with us directly: the cost of getting to class,” Alausa said.

He explained that the initiative would cover 20 federal universities, beginning with a pilot phase involving one institution from each of the six geopolitical zones.

The minister urged university managements and transport operators to ensure that savings from the lower operating costs of CNG-powered vehicles translated into affordable fares and reliable campus shuttle services.

“The switch to CNG reduces running costs. I therefore urge university managements and transport operators to work together so that students share in those savings through affordable fares and dependable shuttle services,” he said.

Alausa also highlighted the employment and skills-development opportunities offered by the facilities, urging universities to expose students to vehicle conversion, equipment maintenance and station operations through supervised practical training.

He, however, stressed the importance of regular equipment maintenance, personnel training and compliance with safety regulations.

“Commercial operations must begin only after the required regulatory approvals are in place,” he cautioned.

Also speaking, the National President of the National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS), Comrade Akinteye Babatunde Afeez, said transportation remained one of the major daily expenses confronting students in tertiary institutions.

He noted that many students spent a significant portion of their upkeep on commuting, sometimes at the expense of other basic necessities.

Afeez said the success of the initiative should be measured by its direct impact on students through affordable fares, reliable transportation services and improved mobility within campuses.

“However, as an organisation whose primary responsibility is to protect and advance the interests of Nigerian students, we want to emphasise that the success of this programme must ultimately be measured by its direct impact on students,” he said.

World.title: FCT traders, artisans pledge Tinubu 200,000 votes
World.content:
Credit Wike’s roads, markets for endorsement

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA — Traders, market women and artisans in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) have pledged to mobilise at least 200,000 votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections, citing infrastructure and market development projects executed under the FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike.

Chairman of the Amalgamation of Market Associations in the FCT, Chief Raphael Okorie, announced the pledge at a mini-rally in Abuja on Friday, saying the association had more than 300,000 members across the territory.

Okorie said the decision to support Tinubu’s re-election was based on what the group described as improvements in trading conditions and infrastructure across the FCT.

According to him, the decision to back the President “did not come easily or lightly”, but was informed by “what our eyes have seen and what our pockets have felt.”

The association consequently declared its “full and unreserved support” for Tinubu’s re-election bid.

“We are not politicians. We are people who wake up before dawn, open our shops, light our fires, and carry our wares to the market,” Okorie said.

He said the association would immediately commence grassroots mobilisation, urging members to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and participate in the election.

“We will go from person to person and house to house. We will make sure every member collects a permanent voter’s card, and we will make sure every member comes out to vote,” he said.

Okorie commended Wike for what he described as improvements in trading conditions through road construction, market development and the relocation of trading activities to designated areas.

He specifically mentioned roads in Gwagwalada, Dei Dei and Saburi, the Old Keffi Road linking Kado to Dei Dei, and the Kugbo International Market.

He also cited the relocation of the Apo Mechanics Village to Wassa as one of the initiatives aimed at improving trading and business activities in the territory.

“Let us speak about roads, because for a trader, a road is not a luxury. A road is life. These are not promises on paper. These are roads you can drive on and markets you can walk into,” he said.

The association chairman argued that improved roads and street lighting would enhance security by making communities more accessible and reducing hiding places for criminals.

“When roads are good, the area becomes safer. When streets are lit, when roads are open and busy, criminals lose their hiding places. A well-planned city is a safer city, and we feel the difference,” he added.

While acknowledging that traders still had concerns, Okorie said the FCT Minister had shown willingness to engage with their association and address their demands.

“He has promised regular interaction with traders, and we will hold him to that. But we are fair people, and fairness demands that we say plainly: this administration has done more for our markets and our trade than any we can remember,” he said.

Reaffirming the group’s commitment to Tinubu’s re-election, Okorie said the 200,000-vote target represented an expression of appreciation for the administration’s interventions in the FCT.

“We promise this nation and this city that we will deliver no fewer than 200,000 votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the Federal Capital Territory.

“That is our gift to the President, and our word of honour to the Minister. We are repaying kindness with loyalty,” he said.

World.title: 2027: Adeola unveils ₦17trn Ogun development blueprint
World.content:
Promises 50,000 annual jobs, 2,500km roads, 200MW additional power

By James Ogunnaike

ABEOKUTA — The governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ogun State, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, has unveiled a development blueprint featuring plans to generate more than 50,000 formal jobs annually, construct and rehabilitate 2,500 kilometres of roads and provide an additional 200 megawatts of electricity if elected governor in 2027.

Adeola unveiled the blueprint, tagged ITESIWAJU: Governance That Works for Everyone, at its formal launch at the June 12 Cultural Centre, Abeokuta, on Friday.

The manifesto, which outlines his proposed development agenda up to 2031, is anchored on nine policy pillars covering infrastructure, tourism, education, security, healthcare, women and youth empowerment, agriculture, industrialisation and urban renewal.

Addressing political leaders, traditional rulers and other stakeholders at the event, the senator said the document was developed following consultations with communities across the state’s 20 local government areas.

He described the manifesto as a social contract with the people, urging residents to scrutinise its contents and hold him accountable for the commitments should he emerge governor.

“Today, I place that agenda, built on your voices, back in your hands. This agenda is a plan, not a performance. Read it as you would read a contract, because that is exactly what it is,” he said.

Adeola pledged to sustain and expand the infrastructure and economic development initiatives of Governor Dapo Abiodun’s administration, stressing that he would not abandon ongoing projects or policies yielding positive results.

He commended successive administrations in the state, including those of former governors Olabisi Onabanjo, Olusegun Osoba, Gbenga Daniel and Ibikunle Amosun, for their contributions to Ogun’s development.

He particularly acknowledged Abiodun’s ISEYA Development Agenda, citing the Gateway International Agro-Cargo Airport, proposed Kajola and Ijebu-Ode dry ports, planned Gateway Deep Sea Port, road construction and housing projects as investments capable of strengthening the state’s economy.

According to Adeola, Ogun’s economy is currently valued at approximately ₦17 trillion, while its internally generated revenue has increased significantly.

“ISEYA laid the foundation for economic growth. ITESIWAJU will build the foundation for more economic growth and prosperity for our people,” he said.

He described Ogun’s strategic location, bordering Lagos State, the Republic of Benin and other Nigerian states, as a major advantage for industrialisation, trade, logistics and regional economic integration.

The senator proposed positioning Ogun as the “New Jersey” to Lagos, arguing that improved transportation, reliable electricity, planned residential communities and an investor-friendly environment would enable the state to accommodate businesses and workers seeking opportunities around Lagos.

However, he acknowledged that the benefits of economic growth had yet to reach many households, citing unemployment, unreliable electricity, inadequate agricultural storage facilities and pressure on healthcare services.

On employment and empowerment, Adeola promised to establish a ₦10 billion Enterprise and Empowerment Fund to support 60,000 businesses owned by women and young people.

He also pledged to train 100,000 youths in digital skills, including coding, data analysis, graphic design and digital marketing, as well as another 100,000 women in practical and entrepreneurial skills.

The manifesto further proposes reserving at least 30 per cent of senior government appointments for women.

He promised to establish sports hubs, youth academies and an annual Ogun State Sports Festival to identify and develop sporting talents.

A social safety net would also be introduced to support 20,000 widows, elderly citizens, persons living with disabilities and low-income households.

On infrastructure, Adeola pledged to construct and rehabilitate 2,500 kilometres of roads by 2031, with emphasis on rural, urban and border communities.

He said the programme would improve connectivity between farming communities and markets, facilitate access to essential services and stimulate economic activities across the three senatorial districts.

On electricity, he identified an estimated 600-megawatt power deficit in the state and promised to address it initially through 200 megawatts of embedded and renewable energy generation.

The proposed projects include the Oke-Mosan Independent Power Project, renewable energy investments around Oyan Dam, power development around Ewekoro and solar mini-grids for underserved communities.

He also pledged to advance the development of the Gateway International Agro-Cargo Airport, Kajola and Ijebu-Ode dry ports, the proposed Gateway Deep Sea Port and Blue Marine Special Economic Zone in Ogun Waterside.

On transportation, Adeola promised to introduce between 50 and 100 compressed natural gas-powered buses within 12 months of assuming office.

The buses, he said, would operate along priority routes, including Abeokuta, Sango-Ota to Lagos, Mowe-Ibafo-Berger, Sagamu to Abeokuta and Sagamu to Lagos.

He also proposed establishing a Gateway Metropolitan Area Transport Authority to coordinate public transportation and introducing OgunRide, a regulated ride-hailing service covering cars, tricycles and licensed motorcycles.

“No one in Ogun State should wait under a tree for a bus again,” he said.

On industrialisation, the APC candidate promised to strengthen industrial estates, establish export-oriented industrial clusters and transform border communities such as Idiroko, Imeko and Ipokia into commercial and logistics centres.

He said his administration would introduce an Ogun State Local Content and Skills Development Law to encourage businesses operating in the state to employ and develop local talent without imposing additional taxes or levies.

He also promised to create 12,000 apprenticeship and internship opportunities by his fourth year in office, including placements in the energy, minerals and petroleum supply chain sectors.

On agriculture, Adeola said only about 30 per cent of Ogun’s estimated 1.2 million hectares of arable land was currently cultivated.

He promised to increase the proportion to 60 per cent through a programme tagged “Grow Ogun, Feed Nigeria”, which would focus on mechanisation, irrigation, improved extension services, agricultural financing and market access.

He also proposed developing cocoa production hubs in Ogun East, cashew hubs in Ogun West and oil palm hubs in Ogun Central, linking them to Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones.

In education, the senator pledged to rehabilitate 2,000 classrooms, construct 500 new educational facilities and train more than 35,000 public-school teachers.

He also set a target of achieving 95 per cent primary school completion through improved learning facilities, technology integration, curriculum modernisation and better teacher welfare.

On healthcare, he promised to equip and adequately staff primary healthcare centres across the state’s wards and establish a Centre of Medical Excellence in each senatorial district.

He further pledged to expand the Ilera D’ero health insurance programme to cover two million residents by 2031 and reduce maternal mortality to below 200 deaths per 100,000 live births.

On security, Adeola promised to strengthen the Amotekun Corps, reposition the State Security Trust Fund and establish a Joint Intelligence Fusion Centre.

He also proposed deploying CCTV surveillance and drones in major towns and border communities within three years, while preparing the state for a possible transition to state policing, subject to the necessary national legislation.

The APC candidate identified tourism and the creative economy as additional sources of revenue and employment, promising to develop 12 flagship tourism destinations to attract 500,000 visitors annually and generate a projected ₦15 billion in revenue by 2031.

Among the attractions he highlighted were Olumo Rock, Bilikisu Sungbo Grove, the Ojude Oba Festival, Lisabi Festival, Oronna Festival and the coastal attractions of Ogun Waterside.

He also proposed establishing an Ogun Film Village to promote film production, fashion, music and the state’s indigenous Adire textile industry.

On natural resources, Adeola promised to maximise opportunities in oil, gas and solid minerals, expressing optimism about prospective commercial oil production around Eba Island.

He said his administration would pursue the state’s constitutional entitlement to 13 per cent derivation when applicable and proposed establishing a naval base on Tongeji Island to strengthen maritime security.

He also identified gold, tantalite, kaolin, limestone and bitumen as mineral resources that should be processed locally to create employment and generate greater economic value.

Under urban renewal, the senator promised to attract ₦500 billion in private investment into urban development, identifying the Ota-Agbara, Mowe, Sagamu, Lagos-Ogun border, Sagamu-Ijebu and Abeokuta-Owode corridors as priority areas.

He also proposed preparing physical development master plans for all 20 local government areas and establishing physical planning offices in each council.

On environmental management, he pledged to strengthen the Ogun State Waste Management Agency, introduce performance-based contracts for private waste operators, establish waste-to-energy facilities and expand recycling programmes.

He also promised to eliminate open defecation by 2031.

Beyond the nine policy pillars, Adeola identified six strategic enablers for implementing the manifesto. They include fiscal discipline and revenue mobilisation, justice sector reform, legislative reform, civil service reform, optimisation of government assets and local government autonomy.

He proposed a Single Window Revenue Collection System to improve transparency, reduce revenue leakages and eliminate multiple taxation.

According to him, the state’s revenue increased by 136 per cent to ₦238.5 billion in 2025, while federal allocations still account for approximately 40 per cent of government expenditure.

He promised to expand the state’s revenue base without imposing additional taxes or double taxation on investors.

On justice administration, he proposed mobile courts, fast-track courts and electronic justice systems to reduce delays and improve access to justice.

He also pledged merit-based recruitment, improved pension administration, digital workflows and sustained implementation of the minimum wage in the civil service.

Adeola further promised to ensure that statutory allocations reach the 20 local government areas directly, fully and promptly, in accordance with constitutional provisions.

To ensure accountability, he pledged to establish a Governor’s Delivery Unit within 30 days of assuming office.

He said commissioners and heads of government agencies would sign performance agreements tied to specific targets, while a public performance dashboard would track progress quarterly.

The indicators would include secondary school completion, household electricity access, youth unemployment, maternal mortality, internally generated revenue as a proportion of total revenue and access to primary healthcare facilities within five kilometres.

He also promised that citizens would be able to report service delivery failures and receive responses within 21 working days.

An independent panel, he said, would assess government performance twice yearly, while an annual State of Ogun Report would be presented to the public.

“We will measure progress not by the ribbons we cut, but by the lives we change,” he said.

Adeola outlined four major economic and social targets for 2031, promising to increase per capita income from approximately $1,740 to $2,500, raise annual economic growth from about four per cent to between six and seven per cent, and increase revenue per resident from ₦39,600 to ₦66,000.

He also pledged to reduce the proportion of households living in multidimensional poverty from 68 per cent to below 45 per cent.

The senator acknowledged that some proposals, including state policing, the extension of Lagos rail lines into Ogun and the realisation of oil derivation benefits, would require cooperation with the Federal Government.

He nevertheless promised to pursue the necessary partnerships and keep residents informed about their progress.

Adeola urged residents to scrutinise the manifesto and hold him accountable for its implementation if elected, saying the document should serve as a basis for assessing his performance in 2028, 2029 and 2031.

“I do not ask you to believe me. I ask you to hold me to this covenant,” he said.

He added: “We are not coming to rule over you. We are coming to work beside you. We will listen closely. We will learn with humility. We will act with the fear of God and with decisive resolve.”

World.title: Borno Children Demand Security, Legal Reforms, Warn Insecurity Threatens State’s Future
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Michael Olugbode in Abuja

Children in Borno State have challenged government at all levels to strengthen security around schools and communities, reform child protection laws and translate their concerns into concrete policy actions, warning that insecurity and disruption of education could undermine the state’s future prosperity.

The children, who spoke at a 2026 World Children’s Day accountability forum in Maiduguri, said protecting their lives, securing their education and guaranteeing their rights must become priorities in government’s response to the challenges confronting the state.

Leading the call, 17-year-old Phoebe Musa Dibal warned that the continued exposure of children to insecurity, including abductions, was threatening both educational development and the economic future of Borno.

“When our security and education are disrupted, there is no way the state is going to continue to prosper, and there is no way the economy is going to grow,” Dibal said, appealing to President Bola Tinubu, the Borno State Government, parents and community leaders to act decisively on children’s concerns.

The children’s intervention came at a forum convened by Plan International Nigeria, the Borno State Government and members of the Joining Forces coalition, where young people confronted policymakers, humanitarian organisations and civil society actors on the need to move beyond promises of child protection to measurable accountability and lasting reforms.

The gathering, held on Friday at the auditorium of the Borno State Ministry of Women Affairs and Social Development in Maiduguri, brought together about 300 participants, including 200 children and 100 policymakers, development partners, civil society representatives and journalists.

Under the theme, “My day. My rights. My future,” the forum provided a platform for children to articulate their concerns about safety, education, healthcare, neglect and exploitation, while demanding greater involvement in decisions affecting their lives.

Beyond the call for improved security, the forum exposed the need for stronger institutional mechanisms to protect vulnerable children, particularly those affected by insurgency, displacement, family separation and poverty.

Delivering a goodwill message on behalf of the Joining Forces Nigeria Coalition Chair, Eghosa Erhumwunse, the Deputy Director of Advocacy, Media and Communications at Save the Children, Badar Musa, urged the Borno State Government to review its Child Protection Law to align it with the ongoing national review of the Child’s Rights Act.

He also called for the adoption of the National Alternative Care Guidelines and the institutionalisation of the Borno State Children’s Parliament as a permanent mechanism through which children could engage government, influence policies and demand accountability.

Musa said children’s participation must not be reduced to ceremonial appearances at public events but translated into policies, institutional commitments and actions capable of addressing their concerns.

Representing the Commissioner for Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajiya Zuwaira Gambo, the ministry’s Director of Child Protection and Development, Falmata Kaumi Alkali, reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to enforcing the Borno State Child Protection Law and ensuring children’s access to quality education and safety at home and in schools.

She said the government was implementing interventions to return conflict-displaced and out-of-school children to formal education, while street children, including those orphaned by insurgency, had been identified, placed under state care and sponsored through secondary and tertiary institutions.

Alkali added that runaway youths had also been traced and reunited with their families, describing the interventions as part of efforts to address vulnerabilities that expose children to abuse, exploitation and street life.

She credited the First Lady of Borno State, Dr Falmata Babagana Zulum, with supporting livelihood empowerment schemes for mothers and widows through tailoring skills and starter kits, saying economic empowerment of women was critical to reducing child street hawking and keeping children in school.

The UNICEF Chief of Maiduguri Field Office, Francis Butichi, said the Children’s Accountability Forum demonstrated that young people were actively engaging in shaping their future, while highlighting ongoing collaborations to address acute malnutrition, improve immunisation and expand alternative learning opportunities.

Butichi, however, warned that gains from humanitarian interventions were being undermined by harmful practices, calling for an end to the open-market sale of ready-to-use therapeutic foods meant for severely malnourished children, diversion of educational materials intended for vulnerable pupils and vandalism of public water infrastructure.

He urged communities to protect public resources and humanitarian assistance, warning that the diversion of essential supplies could deprive vulnerable children of interventions designed to save lives and restore their wellbeing.

The Protection Coordinator of Unique Care and Support Foundation, Osawa Stephen, stressed that children’s rights must remain protected despite the security challenges facing the region, insisting that physical and emotional abuse, neglect and exploitation must not be tolerated.

He said safeguarding children also required guaranteeing their access to healthcare and education, particularly in communities where conflict and humanitarian crises had heightened their vulnerability.

Plan International Nigeria supported the participation of 60 children alongside their chaperones at the forum, which was organised with members of the Joining Forces coalition, including Save the Children, SOS Children’s Villages and Terre des Hommes.

Other partners included the International Rescue Committee, Life at Best Development Initiative, Unique Care and Support Foundation, and Grow Strong Foundation.

The commemoration, held on November 20 to mark World Children’s Day, ultimately placed the burden of accountability on government and institutions, with children insisting that their security, education and rights could no longer be treated as peripheral concerns but as fundamental to Borno’s recovery, stability and development.

World.title: Ogun 2027: The Egba Declaration, Yewa’s Moment And Politics Of Continuity
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

By Kayode Akinmade

As the political temperature gradually rises ahead of the 2027 governorship election in Ogun State, a significant political development has emerged from Egbaland, one that could shape conversations around power, political understanding and the future direction of the Gateway State.

At the palace of the Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Gbadebo, prominent Egba political leaders, traditional rulers and stakeholders made a declaration that has added a new dimension to the unfolding political calculations ahead of 2027: their support for the aspiration of Yewaland to produce the next governor of Ogun State.

More than an ordinary political endorsement, the declaration, as explained by former Secretary to the Ogun State Government and Nigeria’s former Ambassador to the United Kingdom, Ambassador Sarafa Tunji Ishola, represents a collective understanding among influential stakeholders in Egbaland.

And at the centre of that understanding is Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate.

For Yewaland, the aspiration to produce the next governor carries considerable historical and political significance. Fifty years after the creation of Ogun State, the possibility of producing a governor for the first time has become a major issue in the state’s political discourse.

What makes the latest development particularly significant is the disclosure by Ishola that he personally had to abandon his own governorship ambition following consultations with the Alake and other prominent leaders of Egbaland.

Ishola, himself a former APC governorship aspirant, explained that the intervention of the Alake and the Chief Imam of Egbaland persuaded him to support the Yewa aspiration.

According to him, the argument was that Yewaland had demonstrated an uncommon level of unity behind its preferred candidate, and Egbaland should respect that political aspiration.

“You all know that some time ago, I also wanted to run as governor of our dear state. The Alake and other prominent people of Egbaland called me and said we should leave it for Yewaland because, since democracy returned, this is the first time Yewaland is coming out with one voice, and we shouldn’t take that opportunity away from them,” he said.

He added that the Chief Imam of Egbaland also advised him to respect the position communicated by the Alake.

For Ishola, the message was clear: the political future of Ogun State should accommodate a sense of fairness, understanding and mutual respect among its constituent communities.

His declaration that Egbaland was firmly behind Yewaland and Adeola gave further expression to the position he described as a collective decision.

It was a significant moment in the unfolding political conversation, particularly because it came from a former governorship aspirant who had to reconsider his personal ambition in deference to the position of traditional and community leaders.

But beyond the Egba declaration, another important political development is taking shape within the APC: the emergence of Yayi as the candidate around whom the party’s succession arrangement is being organised.

THE ABIODUN FACTOR AND THE POLITICS OF CONTINUITY

While the Egba declaration has brought the Yewa aspiration into sharper focus, Governor Dapo Abiodun’s position on the 2027 succession question introduces another critical dimension: continuity.

In Nigerian politics, transitions between administrations often come with uncertainties about existing policies, projects, investment commitments and the direction of government.

However, Abiodun has consistently argued that the orderly identification of a successor within the same political party, without rancour, bitterness or violence, is important not only for political stability but also for economic development.

At the meeting with the Egba Traditional Council, where he presented Adeola to the traditional institution, the governor described the relationship between his administration and the APC governorship candidate as unprecedented in the political history of Ogun State.

He maintained that the peaceful process surrounding the emergence of Adeola had reinforced confidence in the state’s political and economic future.

“Where a sitting governor is unveiling his successor in the same party in a manner where there was no rancour or bitterness or violence, it has instilled confidence in investors and everybody continues to avail us the same confidence that they availed us since 2019,” Abiodun said.

His argument is that continuity is an important ingredient of socioeconomic development and that a change of administration should not automatically translate into the abandonment of policies and projects that have contributed to the state’s economic growth.

This position becomes particularly interesting against the backdrop of the continued inflow of investments into Ogun State, even as his administration approaches the end of its tenure.

INVESTORS AND THE CONFIDENCE QUESTION

Perhaps one of the most important arguments advanced by Abiodun at the meeting was the relationship between political stability and investor confidence.

The governor disclosed that his administration had attracted more than 6,000 companies to Ogun State in seven years, alongside investments in infrastructure, housing and education.

With more than 1,700 kilometres of roads constructed, about 8,000 housing units delivered and over 8,000 teachers recruited into public primary and secondary schools, Abiodun argued that the state had established an economic and infrastructural foundation that investors continued to find attractive.

He particularly pointed to the peaceful atmosphere in Ogun, noting that the absence of political violence, thuggery and wanton destruction of property had helped create an environment where businesses could operate with confidence.

The governor’s argument is that investors are not simply interested in the opportunities available today; they also want assurances about the stability of the environment in which they are committing their resources tomorrow.

That explains why the continued arrival of investors, despite the approaching end of his administration, has become an important talking point in the state’s political conversation.

The recent groundbreaking of the $1.8 billion LEE Group First Industrial Park is one of the projects cited by the administration as evidence of sustained investor interest.

For Abiodun, the orderly political succession arrangement within the APC provides an additional layer of reassurance that the state’s economic direction and investment-friendly policies will receive attention beyond his tenure.

He also acknowledged the economic reforms of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, particularly the removal of fuel subsidy and foreign exchange reforms, which he said had created opportunities for governments to redirect resources towards infrastructure and economic development.

YAYI AND THE CONTINUITY AGENDA

For Senator Adeola, the political and economic arguments surrounding the 2027 succession question are closely connected.

His emergence as the APC governorship candidate has brought him into the centre of discussions about how Ogun should consolidate its development gains and position itself for the next phase of economic expansion.

At the Egba meeting, Adeola acknowledged the cordial relationship between himself and Governor Abiodun, pledging to sustain the administration’s development agenda.

“I will be seated as your governor to ensure that where Governor Dapo Abiodun stops, I will continue from there, and that is why we are preaching continuity,” he declared.

He drew attention to Lagos State, where successive administrations have operated within the same political structure since the return of democratic governance in 1999, arguing that policy continuity had contributed to its development.

Adeola also identified the Gateway Deep Sea Port, commercial oil exploration activities around Eba and Tongeji Island, and other strategic investments as opportunities that could significantly expand Ogun’s economic base.

He expressed the ambition of growing the state’s internally generated revenue from its present level of about N250 billion to N1 trillion.

His message is that the next administration should not begin governance from scratch but should consolidate existing investments, complete ongoing projects and explore new economic opportunities.

Former Governor Olusegun Osoba also lent his voice to the continuity argument, highlighting the industrial development taking place in Ogun Central and the expansion of educational institutions under the Abiodun administration.

Osoba urged the people of Egbaland to support the APC candidates in the forthcoming elections, while expressing confidence in Adeola’s capacity to lead the state.

BEYOND POLITICS: THE SYMBOLISM OF THE EGBA DECLARATION

The conferment of traditional titles on Adeola, his wife and the deputy governorship candidate, Alhaja Kudirat Abiodun-Balogun, added another layer of significance to the meeting.

Adeola was conferred with the title of Araba of Egbaland, while his wife, Temitope Adeola, received the title of Asiwaju Iya-Ewe, Egba. The deputy governorship candidate was conferred with the title of Asiwaju Iya-Abiye, Egba.

The titles represent an important traditional recognition of the political figures by the Egba institution and provided a symbolic backdrop to the discussions on the relationship between Egbaland and Yewaland.

Taken together, the declarations by Ishola, the position of the Egba traditional institution, the endorsement by Osoba and Abiodun’s presentation of Adeola point to the emergence of a political understanding that places considerable emphasis on the Yewa aspiration and continuity in governance.

Of course, the 2027 election will ultimately be determined by the electorate across the 20 local government areas of Ogun State. Political declarations, endorsements and party arrangements will have to translate into wider public acceptance and electoral support.

But one thing is becoming clear: the succession conversation in Ogun is no longer simply about who occupies the Government House in Abeokuta after May 2027. It is increasingly about the political understanding among the state’s communities, the historical question of power distribution, the future of strategic investments and whether the next administration will sustain the policies and projects already underway.

For Egbaland, Ishola’s declaration has placed its position on the Yewa aspiration firmly in the public domain.

For Yewaland, it represents an important expression of support from influential Egba stakeholders.

For Abiodun, the succession process provides an opportunity to make the case for continuity as a pillar of economic stability.

And for Yayi, the challenge is to translate the political understanding, traditional recognition and APC platform into a compelling vision that resonates with the entire state.

As Ogun approaches another defining electoral moment, the intersection of the Egba declaration, Yewa’s historical aspiration and the politics of continuity is likely to remain central to the conversation about the state’s future.

*Hon. Akinmade is a Special Adviser to Governor Dapo Abiodun

World.title: Tinubu Names Ex-Lagos Commissioner, Agboola Dabiri, As Commissioner In NASC
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 



Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has approved the appointment of Agboola Lukman Dabiri as Commissioner representing the South-west in the National Assembly Service Commission (NASC).

Presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, in a release issued on Friday, described the appointment as part of the president’s efforts to ensure effective representation and inclusivity in the NASC.

He explained that Dabiri replaced Taiwo Olukemi Oluwa, who resigned her appointment on March 30, 2026, to contest in the 2027 general election for the Irewole/Isokan Federal Constituency of Osun State.

Until his appointment, Dabiri served as Commissioner for Youth and Social Development in Lagos State and also previously served as Mandate Secretary for Economic Planning, Revenue Generation and Public-Private Partnership in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

World.title: Shettima: Nigeria’s Economic Future Rests On Strong Institutions, Visionary Entrepreneurs
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

* Stresses capital, tech alone can’t sustain great institutions

* Celebrates his mentor, Jim Ovia’s 75-Year journey at Zenith Bank founder’s dinner

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

Vice-President Kashim Shettima has said the nation’s economic future depends on building strong institutions driven by visionary entrepreneurs, stressing that financial capital and technology alone cannot guarantee the survival of businesses without trust, integrity and sound leadership.

He noted that the country’s experience has shown that enduring enterprises can emerge even during periods of economic and political uncertainty when entrepreneurs demonstrate courage, discipline and confidence in the future.

The vice-president stated this Thursday at the Zenith Bank Founder’s Dinner 2026, held at the Eko Convention Centre, Lagos, in honour of the bank’s founder, Dr. Jim Ovia, who recently celebrated his 75th birthday.

Speaking on the theme, ‘The Man, The Vision and The Legacy’, Shettima described Ovia, his former boss and mentor, as an entrepreneur whose contributions to national development extend beyond banking to education, philanthropy and human capital development.

He recalled that when Ovia established Zenith Bank in 1990, Nigeria was passing through a difficult economic and political period, yet the entrepreneur recognised opportunities where others saw uncertainty.

His words: “When Jim Ovia founded Zenith Bank in 1990, Nigeria was navigating a difficult economic and political period. When many saw uncertainty; he saw possibility.”

The vice-president observed that the ability to build institutions in challenging circumstances remains an important lesson for Nigeria’s business community, particularly at a time when the country is pursuing economic reforms and seeking to strengthen private-sector participation in national development.

“This fact is very poignant and necessary as history teaches us that enduring institutions are often born in difficult times. The great builders of nations and enterprises have rarely waited for perfect conditions.

“They have acted on the conviction that tomorrow can be better than today. The great Jim Ovia made that conviction his life’s work, and Zenith Bank stands today as one of its most visible expressions,” he stated.

Shettima maintained that beyond capital investment, technology and sound business decisions, public confidence and institutional credibility remain indispensable to the growth and survival of financial institutions.

According to him, the enduring strength of Zenith Bank reflects the trust and relationships cultivated by its founder and successive generations of its leadership.

“A bank is built with capital, technology and sound judgment, but it survives through trust. Trust is a remarkable human investment: it takes years to earn, moments to lose, and constant attention to preserve.

“The enduring strength of Zenith Bank is, therefore, a tribute to the relationships Jim and those who have worked with him have cultivated over the decades. It is also a reminder that institutions become truly great when people believe in the values behind their names,” he declared.

The vice-president also underscored the importance of leadership succession and institutional continuity, urging the board, management and staff of Zenith Bank to protect the principles that have sustained the organisation since its establishment.

He said the true test of a founder’s achievement is the ability of an institution to preserve its founding values and remain relevant long after its original leadership has departed.

“To the board, management and staff of Zenith Bank, I offer a simple thought. The greatest tribute you can pay your founder is to preserve the values that made his vision possible,” he further stated.

Shettima further praised Ovia’s contributions to education and youth development, describing investment in human potential as one of the most enduring forms of service to society.

He noted that the bank founder’s support for scholarships and educational opportunities had helped expand the prospects of young Nigerians, demonstrating that the benefits of successful entrepreneurship should extend beyond personal wealth.

“Such generosity is an act of faith in humanity. It reminds us that the most enduring legacy is often carried by people whose names may never appear beside ours,” the vice-president said.

Reflecting on his longstanding relationship with Ovia, under whom he worked during his banking career before entering politics, Shettima described the Zenith Bank founder as a mentor whose humility, warmth and commitment to personal relationships have remained constant despite his professional accomplishments.

The vice-president said his personal experience with Ovia had reinforced his belief that lasting relationships, humility and genuine concern for others are as important as professional success.

He explained that the dinner provided an opportunity to celebrate Ovia’s contributions while he could personally appreciate the gratitude of those whose lives and careers he had influenced.

“We have not gathered merely to applaud Jim’s achievements. We have gathered to tell him, while he is here to hear us, that his efforts have mattered. We should never become so accustomed to extraordinary people that we forget to express our gratitude for the ordinary kindnesses that make them dear to us,” Shettima said.

In her welcome remarks, Managing Director of Zenith Bank, Dr. Adaora Umeoji, recalled the visionary leadership and commitment of the bank’s founder, Ovia, which have transformed the banking system in Nigeria and across Africa.

She said the founder’s determination and investment in people, technology and service have inspired generations of banking professionals and continue to promote integrity, hard work and philanthropy.

Umeoji thanked the bank’s partners, shareholders and customers, as well as regulators in the banking sector, for their trust and steadfast commitment to the bank’s growth and the development of the entire African banking ecosystem.

Highpoint of the occasion was the cutting of the anniversary cake by the founder, accompanied by Ghanaian President John Mahama, Vice-President Shettima, former President Olusegun Obasanjo, governors and other dignitaries present at the event.

World.title: Only Education Can Defeat Terrorism, Says Buratai
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Linus Aleke, Abuja

An asymmetric warfare veteran and former Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Tukur Yusuf Buratai (rtd), has emphasised the critical role of education in addressing terrorism and insecurity, declaring that “a bullet can kill a terrorist, but only education can kill terrorism”.

He maintained that education is a powerful instrument for combating ignorance, poverty, radicalisation and the social conditions that make individuals vulnerable to extremist ideologies.

General Buratai stated this while delivering the 14th convocation lecture to the graduating class of 2026 at Nile University of Nigeria, Abuja.

According to him, “A bullet can kill a terrorist. Only education can kill terrorism. I stand before you not merely as a former Chief of Army Staff, but as a soldier who has spent a lifetime confronting a proposition that the world has been slow to accept: that the security of a nation is not measured solely by the strength of its armed forces, but by the strength of its classrooms.”

In a lecture titled ‘Nexus Between Education and Security: Implications and Lessons for Sub-Saharan Africa,’ the Chairman of the Tukur Buratai Research Centre (TBRC) said: “Let me begin with a confession. When I was invited to deliver this lecture, I asked myself: ‘What does a soldier have to say to a university?’

“I have spent most of my life in barracks, on training grounds and in theatres of war. You have spent yours in lecture halls, libraries and laboratories. We seem to live in different worlds.

“But the longer I thought about it, the more I realised that we live in the same world. We fight the same war. Only our weapons are different. Mine was a rifle. Yours is a pen, a computer, an idea. And I have come to tell you today, from the battlefield of the North-east to the classrooms of the Sahel that your weapon is more powerful than mine.”

To further buttress his argument that the pen is mightier than the sword, Buratai recounted a memorable experience from the height of the war against Boko Haram.

“Let me begin with a story. A story I have never forgotten. In 2016, during the height of the war against Boko Haram, I visited a liberated community in Borno State. The soldiers had done their job. The terrorists had been pushed out. The market was slowly coming back.

“A boy, perhaps 12 years old, walked up to me. He was barefoot. His clothes were torn. He looked up at me and said, ‘Soldier, I want to go to school’.

“I asked him, ‘Where is your school?’

“He pointed to a heap of burnt rubble. That was his school. Boko Haram had burnt it two years earlier.

“Then he said something I have never forgotten. He said ‘If I do not go to school, they will come back for me.’

“He was 12 years old. And he understood what many policymakers in Africa still do not understand: that when a school dies, a terrorist is born. That when a child is denied education, an insurgent gains a recruit.

“That boy is the reason this lecture is not about guns. It is about books. I do not know where he is today. I pray he is in school. But there are millions like him across sub-Saharan Africa, in Niger, Mali, Burkina Faso, Chad, Somalia, Mozambique, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Sudan.

“Millions of children are asking the same question: ‘Will anyone give me a school, or will the terrorists give me a gun?’

“How we answer that question will determine whether Africa rises or burns in the next thirty years,” he said.

Buratai explained that his lecture argues that education and security are not separate domains to be traded off against one another, but two dimensions of a single struggle.

“It examines the environment in which this struggle unfolds, the actors who shape it, the reciprocal nexus between learning and violence, the implications for sub-Saharan Africa, and the practical lessons that follow. It draws on published research, official data and the testimony of practitioners, and it concludes with recommendations addressed to policymakers, institutions and the graduating class before whom it is delivered,” the retired Army Chief concluded.

World.title: Middle Belt Forum Distances Itself from Anti-Tinubu Statement, Denies Leadership Claims
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Yemi Kosoko in Jos

The Middle Belt Forum (MBF) has distanced itself from a statement issued by Emmanuel Zopmal, who claimed to be the organisation’s National Youth Leader and criticised President Bola Tinubu’s administration while rejecting reports of Middle Belt support for the president’s political ambitions.

In the statement, Zopmal questioned a recent visit by some Middle Belt leaders to President Tinubu and argued that it did not reflect the views of the region’s communities.

He also expressed support for opposition figures, Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso, ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

However, the MBF, in a response signed by its National Spokesman, Luka Binniyat, denied that Zopmal holds any position within the organisation, describing his claim to the youth leadership as falsehood.

“We do not recognise Zopmal as having held any national leadership position in the Middle Belt Forum. That is pure impersonation,” Binniyat said.

The Forum stated that its recognised National Youth Coordinator is Brent Kane and reaffirmed its confidence in its President, Dr Pogu Bitrus, and Chairman of the Board of Trustees, Gen. T.Y. Danjuma (rtd.).

According to the MBF, the recent visit to President Tinubu was an officially sanctioned engagement carried out after consultations within its leadership and aimed at presenting the interests and demands of Middle Belt communities.

The organisation further said that leadership changes must follow its established procedures and urged the public to disregard statements issued in its name by unauthorised persons.

The exchange highlights differing views within sections of the Middle Belt political space over engagement with the Tinubu administration and the region’s political direction ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: Atiku Loses Bid to Amend Suit Seeking to Bar Tinubu from 2027 Poll
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Alex Enumah in Abuja

The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, has lost in his bid to amend his suit seeking to disqualify President Bola Ahmed Tinubu from the January 16, 2027 presidential election.

This follows the dismissal of his application for amendment by Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court, Abuja, on Friday.

Atiku had approached the court for an order disqualifying Tinubu from participating in next year’s presidential poll, on the grounds that he (Tinubu) forged the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) discharge certificate, submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in aid of his qualification for the presidential election.

However, after President Tinubu, his party, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the electoral body had responded to the suit, Atiku subsequently applied to amend his originating summons, a request which was opposed by the defendants.

Delivering ruling on Friday, Justice Ekwo declined to grant the request for amendment on the grounds, among others, that Atiku by the application intended to bring fresh evidence in the suit, which must be done within 14 days stipulated by Section 285(9) of the 1999 Constitution, being a pre-election matter.

Justice Ekwo agreed with Tinubu and other defendants in the suit that if Atiku is allowed to bring fresh evidence, the character of the initial case would change and would be in breach of the 1999 Constitution.

Ekwo noted that the former vice-president by the application attempted to mislead the court when he claimed that he would not present fresh issue in the amendment sought, adding that Atiku, through the motion, sought to substitute old evidence for a new one which, if allowed, would over reach Section 285(9) of the Constitution which says such evidence must have been provided within 14 days.

According to the judge, a fundamental injustice would be done to the defendants if Atiku is permitted to bring fresh evidence through the back door against them.

“This is a time bound suit and the law makes it mandatory for all exhibits to be filed in court within 14 days of occurrence of the event being challenged. Anything outside the prescribed 14 days is null and void and of no effect.

“I find no merit in this application to bring fresh exhibit, it is hereby refused for being against the express provision of the law.

“I hereby make an order dismissing this application and is hereby dismissed,” Ekwo held.

He subsequently fixed December 2 for hearing of the substantive matter.

Atiku had told the court that he needed to make substantial amendment to his case challenging the eligibility of Tinubu to participate in the 2027 presidential election.

Atiku and ADC had, in the main suit, asked Justice Inyang Ekwo to disqualify President Tinubu and APC from the 2027 presidential election.

They had questioned Tinubu’s NYSC discharge certificate submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) by APC.

The plaintiffs, who sued the president, APC and INEC as first to third defendants in the originating summons marked: FHC/ABJ/CS/1888/2026, alleged that APC submitted the president’s forged NYSC discharge certificate to INEC.

They, therefore, prayed the court to compel INEC to remove Tinubu and APC’s names from the list of candidates and parties for the presidential poll.

But President Tinubu and APC, in their joint counter affidavit filed on September 9, prayed the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety for being incompetent and that the plaintiffs lacked the legal right to institute the case.

They denied submitting any forged certificate to INEC either for the 2023 or 2027 presidential elections.

The duo, through the APC’s Director of Legal Services, Mr Sanusi Samaila, averred that they did not submit any Form CF001 to INEC for 2023 or 2027 poll as claimed by the plaintiffs.

They stated that the NYSC has never denied issuing the discharge certificate to the first defendant at the end of his service year.

World.title: Direct Selling Can Drive Jobs, Economic Growth, Says QNET
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The General Manager of QNET, Ayokunmi Solesi, has said the company’s direct-selling model is creating business opportunities and empowering Nigerians to participate in economic activities without the huge capital requirements associated with conventional businesses.

Solesi stated this Friday in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, during a media engagement ahead of the company’s EXPO ’26, where he also said QNET was expanding its presence in the state to create opportunities for youths and other residents.

He explained that the company’s model, which centres on the sale of health, wellness and lifestyle products, enables individuals to operate as independent distributors, while QNET handles major aspects of warehousing and logistics.

According to him, the model could contribute to Nigeria’s economic growth by strengthening small and medium-scale businesses and providing alternative income opportunities for individuals.

“Every nation that has thrived across the world has taken care of small and medium enterprises. We fall under that, meaning that we’re providing business opportunities to people,” Solesi said.

“We’re saying to you that you do not need to have capital at the beginning of your business. We’re providing this business opportunity where you can buy the product at a good price and you can also sell the product.”

He added that the company’s approach was designed to reduce some of the financial barriers associated with starting a business, noting that distributors do not have to maintain warehouses or independently handle logistics.

“What we do is deliver the products directly to your house. Which means that you do not need to take care of warehousing, neither do you need to worry about logistics,” he said.

Solesi said QNET’s economic contribution went beyond individual distributors, stressing that the activities of small businesses ultimately had an impact on the wider Nigerian economy.

He also clarified that the company’s direct-selling model should not be confused with pyramid schemes, saying distributors earn commissions from the sale of products rather than merely recruiting people.

“For us, you do not get commissions without selling our products because what we do is sell health and wellness products, and that’s our focus,” he said.

On QNET’s expansion into Port Harcourt, Solesi said the company was seeking to deepen awareness of its products and business opportunities among residents.

“We want you all in Port Harcourt and Rivers State to understand that QNET has come to create opportunities for our youths, not just for our youths, but for everyone in Port Harcourt,” he said.

Solesi disclosed that although QNET had operated globally for 28 years, it entered Nigeria in 2022 and was gradually expanding across the country.

He further urged Nigerians to verify information about the company and distinguish its legitimate operations from individuals allegedly using its name to offer fake jobs, visas or other services.
