Abdullahi says the ADC and its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, a former vice president, propose a production subsidy that would use domestic refining to bring fuel costs down. He pointed to the Act’s Domestic Crude Supply Obligation, set out in Section 109, which can require producers to supply crude to domestic refineries, under rules issued by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, the oil regulator.

Abdullahi noted that the Act was one of the longest-pending bills before it passed in 2021, and argued that any law that deepens citizens’ hardship must be reviewed. He also asked whether the president had weighed alternatives before acting.

Section 109 also says supply should normally run on a willing-seller, willing-buyer basis, at commercially negotiated prices that take international prices into account. Price is therefore negotiated between producers and refiners rather than set by the state.

Atiku’s candidacy is itself in dispute. A Federal High Court, a national trial court, in Abuja ruled on 5 November that the party’s leadership was invalid and nullified its nominations, including his; an earlier ruling on 2 July 2026 had upheld the same leadership, and the ADC says it is appealing.

Fashola also reminded viewers that the previous government was spending close to 90% of its revenue on debt service, which he said made removal inevitable. Abdullahi answers with federal budget figures that, he says, show debt service took about 91% of revenue in the first quarter of 2026, and he asks what has changed since the subsidy ended.

The stakes are fiscal as well as political. In 2022 the World Bank warned that subsidy payments were absorbing crude revenue that would otherwise go to the federation account, which funds federal, state and local governments.

Any subsidy has to be paid for from the same revenue pool, so the argument over the World Bank’s role is also an argument over who pays. The next public test is the campaign itself, with the presidential vote due on 16 January 2027.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a prediction market where users bet real money, gave Bola Tinubu a 70.0% chance of winning Nigeria’s presidential election, Peter Obi, a former Anambra governor, 25.0% and Atiku Abubakar 5.0% on 20 November 2026 at 13:56 ET, with about US$161,651 traded across the market. These are bets, not polls.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Frequently Asked Questions

Did the World Bank order Nigeria to end the fuel subsidy?

The World Bank urged it in public reports, and Fashola says the lender’s position was that financing depended on it. The ADC argues recommendations are not instructions.

What does the ADC want instead?

It proposes a production subsidy that uses domestic refining to cut fuel costs, and says the oil law already allows support for local refineries.

Sources: World Bank, Nigeria Development Update, June 2022 (press release); Petroleum Industry Act 2021, Section 109; Bolaji Abdullahi’s opinion article “Who Governs Nigeria, Tinubu or the World Bank?” (full text); Babatunde Fashola’s interview of 17 November 2026; Polymarket.

World.title: Mozambique Court Bars Mondlane Defence Aide
World.content:
The ruling ends the question of whether Mendes may speak in court, not the separate case against him. It narrows who can speak for Mondlane, not what he is charged with.

Maputo, the capital and main port, seen from the air. File photo, 2006. (Photo: AmigoDia, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

POLITICS · MOZAMBIQUE

A court in Mozambique has formally ruled that Shamir Mendes, a member of opposition leader Venâncio Mondlane’s defence team, may sit with the lawyers but may not speak for the defence at the trial. The Supreme Court in Maputo announced the decision at the start of the fourth day, Friday 20 November 2026, after the national bar association’s information showed he is registered only as a first-phase trainee lawyer.

The question has hung over the trial since its first day, because Mendes argued the defence’s first motion to throw out the charges. Mondlane, who ran for president in 2024, faces five charges including terrorism over the protests that followed that election.

Key Facts Who Shamir Mendes, also spelled Chamir, on opposition leader Venâncio Mondlane’s defence team.

What The court let him stay with the defence team but barred him from addressing it.

Why The court said the bar association lists him as a first-phase trainee lawyer.

As of 20 November 2026, 19:30 GMT.

The ruling ends the question of whether Mendes may speak in court, not the separate case against him. It narrows who can speak for Mondlane, not what he is charged with.

The dispute began on Tuesday 17 November, the first day, when Mendes argued the defence’s request to annul the indictment. A lawyer for a private party that has joined the prosecution objected and a deputy prosecutor questioned Mendes’s standing, but the presiding judge let him stay on the defence team that day.

On Wednesday the Public Prosecutor’s Office, the state’s prosecuting authority, said it had opened a separate criminal case against him over alleged unauthorised practice of law, after he appeared in a lawyer’s gown, the black court robe of registered lawyers. Reports from the courtroom that day said the court had provisionally withdrawn his right to speak.

Africa Intelligence One email, every weekday morning. African markets, politics and business — filed from our newsroom in Rio. Yesterday’s subject line: “Kabila's armed group seizes three South Kivu towns” Get the brief

On Thursday 19 November the Ordem dos Advogados de Moçambique, the national bar association, said he is not registered as a lawyer and holds no professional card, and that it had sent a complaint about him to its disciplinary council. On Friday the presiding judge made the court’s position formal.

The court said information from the bar association lists Mendes as a first-phase trainee lawyer, the first stage of the bar’s traineeship, a status that lets him assist registered lawyers but not act alone in criminal cases. It kept him with the defence team as an assistant, without the right to speak.

Mendes has said he acts as a defender of the accused rather than as a lawyer. He had worn a lawyer’s gown in court, which prosecutors and the party assisting them challenged.

The Administrative Court building in Maputo, one of the capital’s court buildings; the trial is at the Supreme Court. File photo, 2025. Photo: Salazar Sérgio, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

The hearing then moved on to other preliminary points and to questions for Mondlane from the prosecution. Mondlane says the case is political.

Leaving the court on Wednesday, he said prosecutors want to keep him out of the 2028 municipal and 2029 general elections, and that Frelimo, the party that has governed Mozambique since 1975, fears him. He alleged fraud in the 2023 municipal vote, when he stood in Maputo as a candidate of Renamo, the former rebel movement turned opposition party, and he never recognised the official results of the 2024 election.

He says prosecutors took no action on his complaints about electoral irregularities. On the first day he told reporters the indictment he received carried a clerk’s signature rather than a magistrate’s, a flaw he said should void it.

The charges are public glorification of crime, incitement to collective disobedience, public instigation of crime, instigation of terrorism and incitement to terrorism. Prosecutors filed the indictment in July 2025, and Mondlane says they held the file for almost 130 days, which stopped his team from asking for a preliminary hearing.

The prosecution answers that some defence objections came too late, Deputy Attorney-General Amabélia Chuquela, a senior prosecutor, argued on Tuesday. The defence’s written plea runs to 223 pages, and Mondlane presented a summary of it on Wednesday.

Mendes made the opening argument on the indictment on the first day. Registered lawyers appear to carry that role from now on.

A separate criminal case against Mendes is pending, and how it will end has not been reported. It is distinct from Mondlane’s own trial.

Sessions run from 10:00 to 15:30 Maputo time, which is 03:00 to 08:30 US Eastern. A verdict date has not been announced.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why was Shamir Mendes barred from speaking?

The court said the bar association lists him as a first-phase trainee lawyer. Under that status he can assist registered lawyers but cannot act alone in criminal cases.

Is Venâncio Mondlane still on trial?

Yes. The hearings continue at the Supreme Court in Maputo, and the court has not announced a verdict date.

World.title: Exxon Backs US$4 Billion Angola Oil Revamp
World.content:
Block 15 now has both the money and the licence to keep producing into the 2030s. The new discovery adds possible upside.

Cargo ships and cranes at the port of Luanda, seen from the bay in June 2015, with hillside housing behind. Photo: XEON / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0)

ENERGY · ANGOLA

ExxonMobil and its partners in Angola’s offshore Block 15 have approved a redevelopment of the Kizomba A and B oil fields that the country’s oil regulator values at about US$4 billion. The regulator, the National Oil, Gas and Biofuels Agency (ANPG), announced the decision on Friday 20 November 2026 and said it was approved on 19 November.

ExxonMobil, the Texas-based oil major, operates the block. The same statement reported a new hydrocarbon discovery, the second in the block this year.

What A final investment decision, the formal go-ahead to spend, of about US$4 billion.

Where Deepwater Block 15, about 350 kilometres northwest of Luanda, Angola’s capital.

Block 15 now has both the money and the licence to keep producing into the 2030s. The new discovery adds possible upside.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Angola oil Email address Follow

The decision follows a contract change signed on 10 July 2025, which moved the end of Block 15’s production licence from 2032 to 2037. It let the Kizomba A and B floating production vessels, the ships that process oil offshore, run longer, subject to this very investment decision.

Azule Energy, Equinor and Sonangol, the state oil company, signed the change alongside ExxonMobil and ANPG. Azule is the Angolan joint venture of BP and Eni, and Equinor is Norway’s state-controlled oil company.

Africa Intelligence One email, every weekday morning. African markets, politics and business — filed from our newsroom in Rio. Yesterday’s subject line: “Kabila's armed group seizes three South Kivu towns” Get the brief

The redevelopment of a third field, Kizomba C, was approved in 2025. ANPG said the November decision completes the final investment decisions for the Block 15 Life Extension Project.

ExxonMobil says its aim is to get more from existing infrastructure. Brian Unietis of ExxonMobil Angola said the licence extension and nearly US$4 billion of planned new investment, including Likembe, a discovery in the Kizomba B area, leave the company “well positioned to continue generating value for Angola, our partners and our shareholders”.

ANPG’s monthly figures put its output at about 1.03 million barrels a day in December 2025, and the country left OPEC, the oil producers’ group, in January 2024 after a dispute over its quota.

The liquefied natural gas carrier Sonangol Sambizanga, named for Angola’s state oil company. File photo; the location is not stated. photo. The liquefied natural gas carrier Sonangol Sambizanga, flagged in Nassau, moored at a terminal. The location of the photo is not stated.

Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

For the Kizomba fields, the addendum allows the two vessels to stay in service until 2037. The approval also points to years of well and equipment work at an existing hub.

The new well, Tchihumba West-01ST1, was drilled by the drillship Valaris DS-9 in about 1,400 metres of water. It met 65.4 metres of sandstone holding hydrocarbons with good reservoir quality, and it is the 21st discovery in Block 15.

Hydrocarbons can mean oil, gas or both, and one well is only a first step. Companies usually drill more wells to size a find before they decide whether to develop it.

ANPG said the result shows significant remaining resource potential in the block. That is the regulator’s view, not a resource estimate.

ANPG puts the Kizomba A and B decision at about US$4 billion, while ExxonMobil speaks of nearly US$4 billion in planned new investment that includes Likembe. The two descriptions may not cover exactly the same projects.

For US readers, the mechanism is a production sharing contract: the company recovers its costs from the oil it pumps, then splits the rest with the state. A licence running to 2037 gives ExxonMobil more than a decade to earn back about US$4 billion.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did ExxonMobil approve in Angola?

A final investment decision, the formal go-ahead to spend, to redevelop the Kizomba A and B fields in Block 15. Angola’s regulator values it at about US$4 billion.

Does the new discovery mean more oil is coming?

Not yet. A single well shows hydrocarbons are present, and further drilling and study decide whether a find can be developed.

World.title: Justice Votes to Try Ex-Lula Minister
World.content:
A Supreme Court justice has voted that there is enough evidence to try a former Lula cabinet member over congressional budget earmarks, with three panel colleagues still to vote.

Politics: Brazil

Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino voted on Friday 20 November 2026 to put Juscelino Filho, a former communications minister under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, on trial for corruption. Dino, the judge leading the case, wants the court’s First Panel, one of its two chambers of justices, to accept in full the complaint that the Prosecutor General’s Office filed against Juscelino Filho and five other people.

Rio Times membership One dollar for your first month. All premium analysis. Enter your email and the link comes by mail. Privacy Send me the offer

Accepting a complaint does not convict anyone, but it turns the accused into defendants and opens a criminal trial. Three fellow Supreme Court justices on the panel, Alexandre de Moraes, Cristiano Zanin and Cármen Lúcia, have yet to vote.

Key Facts Who. Juscelino Filho, former communications minister from Maranhão in Brazil’s northeast, plus five others.

What. Justice Flávio Dino voted to accept corruption charges tied to earmarks, funds lawmakers direct to projects.

Where. Brazil’s Supreme Court, First Panel, voting online.

When. Dino voted Friday 20 November 2026; the session closes Monday 30 November.

As of. 20 November 2026, 18:00 GMT.

A Supreme Court justice has voted that there is enough evidence to try a former Lula cabinet member over congressional budget earmarks, with three panel colleagues still to vote.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Brazil corruption Email address Follow

The Prosecutor General’s Office, known as the PGR, made its complaint to Brazil’s Supreme Court public on Tuesday 8 April 2025, when Juscelino Filho was Communications Minister. He left the post that month, and Frederico de Siqueira Filho, then head of the state telecoms company Telebras, was named to replace him on 24 April 2025.

The PGR accuses the group of running a criminal organisation, rigging public tenders, embezzlement and active corruption, meaning bribery by the person who pays. The case centres on parliamentary earmarks, known in Portuguese as emendas, which are sums that lawmakers steer to projects in their home districts.

WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Juscelino Filho is also a member of the Chamber of Deputies, Brazil’s lower house of Congress, and Brazil’s constitution gives the Supreme Court jurisdiction over criminal cases against members of Congress. That is why a case about a small Maranhão town is being decided in Brasília by a panel of the country’s highest court.

Prosecutors say Juscelino Filho sent earmarked money to Codevasf, a federal agency that finances regional development works, to pay for projects in Vitorino Freire, a town in the northeastern state of Maranhão. His sister, Luanna Rezende, ran the town as mayor at the time, according to the complaint.

He denies wrongdoing and is presumed innocent until a final verdict. Prosecutors also accuse five other people.

A ministry building on the Esplanada dos Ministérios in Brasília. (Photo: Jefferson Rudy/Agência Senado)

Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

In his vote, Dino rejected the defence’s preliminary objections. He held that there is enough ground to open a criminal case.

The First Panel is deciding in a virtual plenary, a format where justices post written votes on an online system over several days instead of meeting in a courtroom. Dino posted his vote on Friday 20 November 2026, and the session closes on Monday 30 November 2026.

Moraes, Zanin and Cármen Lúcia have not yet voted, so the outcome depends on how the panel’s majority forms. Once the three have voted, the court’s online system will show whether the complaint is accepted.

Americans will recognise the problem as pork-barrel spending, but in Brazil the stakes are higher because Congress decides where billions of reais in earmarks go. The government’s draft budget bill for 2027 sets aside R$44.8 billion (about US$7.5 billion at R$5.95 per US$1, the 20 November 2026 market close) for mandatory earmarks, sums the budget law obliges the government to pay.

Dino has handled the court’s earmark cases since 2024, including a December 2024 order that the full court confirmed. A trial of a former Lula minister therefore tests how far the court will follow the money into the coalition that backs the government.

If the panel accepts the complaint, the six accused become defendants and the court will set the steps for evidence and testimony. Each defence will then be able to call witnesses before any verdict, and the next dated step is the close of the online vote on Monday 30 November 2026.

Brazil’s Supreme Court has no jury when it tries politicians, so the panel’s own justices would also decide guilt. That makes the votes of Moraes, Zanin and Cármen Lúcia the first thing to watch.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Juscelino Filho guilty?

No. Accepting a complaint only means the court sees enough evidence to hold a trial, and he is presumed innocent until a final verdict.

What happens if the panel agrees with Dino?

The six accused become defendants and a criminal trial follows. Only that trial can end in conviction or acquittal.

Why do earmarks matter so much in Brazil?

They give individual lawmakers direct control over public money, which strengthens Congress against the president. Cases like this show how that power is policed.

World.title: Brazil Lawmaker Sees Deal in Bolsonaro Law
World.content:
Brazil's Supreme Court has a date to judge a law that could shorten the sentence of a former president, and a government ally says the date is no accident.

File photo, 2012. A Gulfstream G450 business jet at Dubai International Airport; the flight in this story used a Gulfstream G400. (Photo: Aeroprints.com, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Politics: Brazil

Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes on Thursday 19 November 2026 cleared for judgment the challenges to a law that cuts sentences for the 8 January 2023 rioters who stormed Brasília’s government buildings. The court will vote on it online from Friday 4 December.

Rio Times membership One dollar for your first month. All premium analysis. Enter your email and the link comes by mail. Privacy Send me the offer

On Friday 20 November, Lindbergh Farias, who leads the Workers’ Party of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the Chamber of Deputies, Brazil’s lower house, said the timing looks like a political bargain. He says the vote is part of a wider deal among Congress leaders, the court and supporters of former president Jair Bolsonaro.

Key Facts Who. Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes and Lindbergh Farias, Workers’ Party leader in the Chamber of Deputies.

What. The court will judge the Dosimetria (sentence-calculation) law, which cuts sentences for the 8 January 2023 attack.

Where. Brasília, in the Supreme Court’s online (virtual) plenary.

When. Voting runs from Friday 4 December to Tuesday 15 December 2026.

As of. 20 November 2026, 18:00 GMT.

Brazil’s Supreme Court has a date to judge a law that could shorten the sentence of a former president, and a government ally says the date is no accident.

Rio Times membership Read everything we publish for US$1 in the first month. Then US$8.99 a month. Cancel anytime. Start for US$1

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Lindbergh Farias (Brazil) Email address Follow

The law is known in Brazil as the Lei da Dosimetria, meaning the law on how a sentence is calculated. It reduces penalties for people convicted over the 8 January 2023 attack on the capital’s government buildings, and it could help former president Jair Bolsonaro.

The Supreme Court’s First Panel, one of its two panels of justices, convicted Bolsonaro on 11 September 2025 of leading a coup plot and sentenced him to 27 years and 3 months. The court has given no figure for how much the new law would cut that term.

Latin America Power Index · November 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 74.2 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Congress passed the bill and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva vetoed it. Congress overrode the veto on 30 April 2026, and when Lula did not sign, Senate president Davi Alcolumbre promulgated (signed into force) the law on Friday 8 May 2026.

Moraes, the rapporteur (the justice who leads the case) of the actions challenging it, then suspended its application to prison sentences until the full court judges the merits. The suspension was meant to last until the full court rules.

Congress has pressed for speed. Hugo Motta, president of the Chamber of Deputies, and Alcolumbre asked Moraes on 17 November to release the cases, in a request that Congress’s leaders made together.

Court president Edson Fachin has said the plenary could judge the case this year once Moraes releases it. Moraes released the cases two days after the request.

The Supreme Federal Court building in Brasília, designed by Oscar Niemeyer. (Archive photo)

RT Ask Rio Times This story and the bigger picture. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesWhat this means, and what's next › RT Ask Rio Times This story and the bigger picture. × Economy impact Key players Stability What's next Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

Farias, who leads the Workers’ Party (PT) in the Chamber of Deputies, offered a different reading in a video on social media on Friday. He said it looks to him like a “global deal” (“acordo global”), struck on the eve of the votes in which each house elects its president.

He added that the Liberal Party (PL), Bolsonaro’s party, would drop the idea of impeaching, meaning removing, a Supreme Court justice, and that the court would in return approve an “unconstitutional thesis”. He accused Chamber president Hugo Motta and Senate president Davi Alcolumbre of being part of the deal, which he said also involves the court.

No official document or statement presented so far supports such an arrangement. Farias speaks for a party that backs the president and opposes the law.

Farias is a lawmaker, not a justice, and he has no vote on the law. His video turns a scheduling decision into a charge about the court’s independence.

The institutions describe the case in legal terms. Motta and Alcolumbre asked for a ruling on the law’s constitutionality, and Fachin spoke only of scheduling.

The law touches people already serving sentences for 8 January, so a ruling that lets it stand would change real prison terms. The court has not said how many people could benefit.

A ruling against the law would leave Congress to decide whether to rewrite it. A ruling in its favour would lift the suspension that Moraes ordered in May, the step that the court’s vote now decides.

The next dated step is the opening of the virtual plenary on Friday 4 December 2026. The court’s rules allow a justice to move a virtual vote to an in-person session, which would delay the result.

Because the court votes online, there is no courtroom debate to watch. Justices record their votes remotely while the session runs.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does the Dosimetria law do?

It lowers sentences for people convicted over the 8 January 2023 attack. It could also help former president Jair Bolsonaro.

Is a deal behind the vote proven?

No. The claim comes from one lawmaker who opposes the law, and the court and the Congress leaders frame the case as a question of constitutionality.

When will the court decide?

The online vote opens on 4 December and is due to close on 15 December 2026. A request by a justice to move the case to a courtroom session would delay the result.
