World.title: Former French premier de Villepin launches presidential bid, warns against Le Pen victory
World.content:
PARIS: Former French Prime Minister Dominique de Villepin announced his candidacy for president on Friday, invoking Charles de Gaulle’s legacy and pledging to strengthen France’s international standing and defeat political extremism.

The 73-year-old, who served as prime minister under President Jacques Chirac, announced his plans at a news conference in Paris. He condemned the country’s direction under President Emmanuel Macron, whose second and final term ends next year. He also described a potential victory by far-right leader Marine Le Pen next year as a grave threat to the nation.

He said France finds itself at a time of “social decay” and listed an accumulation of problems, including environmental backsliding and rising public debt.

“The coffers are empty,” he said.

A veteran of France’s traditional right, de Villepin has also appealed to voters on the left with his criticism of growing inequality and Israel’s war in Gaza.

Internationally, he is probably best known for an eloquent 2003 speech at the United Nations in which he declared French opposition to the US-led invasion of Iraq.

In order to stand, de Villepin must still gather 500 sponsorship signatures from elected officials, as required by French law.

France will pick its next president at a time of tensions and protests

Protest marches have been drawing huge crowds for weeks in Paris and elsewhere across France as demonstrators demand higher wages and back the country’s student protest movement.

De Villepin accused officials of ignoring protesters’ demands and of even using repression. He denounced Macron as a “ghost president” whose failure to address the country’s problems has strengthened Le Pen and hard-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon.

Polls have for months suggested that Le Pen is the front-runner and could possibly advance to the runoff on May 2 as the first-round vote leader, which would be a first for her. She trailed Macron in the 2017 and 2022 first-round voting and then lost decisively to him in round two.

De Villepin warns against a Le Pen victory

De Villepin said he does not view Le Pen’s National Rally and Mélenchon’s France Unbowed as equal threats, insisting Le Pen’s party carries a legacy of xenophobia, racism and antisemitism.

“Who can seriously believe that Marine Le Pen’s planned election next May would unfold peacefully?” he asked.

Detailing his priorities, De Villepin pledged to address France’s public debt, which has climbed to a record, unsettling investors and emerging as a defining issue ahead of next year’s presidential election. It now stands at 119 percent of gross domestic product, leaving the country’s strained public finances likely to dominate the campaign.

He also called for a new “night of August 4,” referring to the historic abolition of feudal privileges during the French Revolution, with the goal of tackling modern privileges by scrutinizing tax breaks and social exemptions.

“The French people need to be convinced that it is not a case of the richest 1 percent on one side and the remaining 99 percent, who are always the ones being asked to make sacrifices, on the other,” he said.

De Gaulle, who organized the French resistance movement during World War II, led the creation of France’s current constitution in 1958. De Villepin proposed to move away from the model of what he called the “hyper-president” embodied by Macron and to restore the head of state’s role advocated by De Gaulle as “an arbiter, a guide for the country.”

World.title: Estonia to close border with Russia, Moscow decries 'new Iron Curtain'
World.content:
VILNIUS: Estonia will close its road border crossings with Russia on security grounds for at least six months, the Baltic country's government said on Friday, prompting a warning from Moscow that it would respond with political and diplomatic measures.

NATO and EU member Estonia on Sunday accused Russian security services of staging an attempted arson attack on an Estonian defence company, ⁠in what it ⁠said was the second such incident this year.

The border closure is set to begin on December 1.

This would help address the wider security situation and limit Russia's ability to organise further attacks, Estonian Interior Minister Igor Taro told a press conference.

"Russian security services are intimidating and trying to recruit our citizens who are travelling through our border checkpoints. This is ⁠something we cannot tolerate anymore," Taro said.

The Kremlin has denied any involvement in the weekend arson attack.

Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova on Friday said that Russia would respond with political and diplomatic measures if Estonia went ahead with the closure.

"Such moves are tantamount to attempts to erect a new Iron Curtain under the false pretence of some sort of threat from the East," Zakharova said.

Estonia, a strong supporter of Ukraine, currently has five crossing points where travellers can enter or leave Russia, according to the government.

Estonia's northern neighbour Finland shut its Russia border crossings in 2023, and has ⁠kept them closed ⁠since then, while southern Baltic nations Latvia and Lithuania maintain open crossings.

Thousands of people living in Estonia have family in Russia or vice versa, as legacies of the Soviet era. The crossing at Narva, a majority Russian-speaking city on the Estonian side of the border, is also used by people travelling from further afield in Europe to reach St Petersburg a few hours' drive away.

Of the 760,000 people who crossed the Estonia-Russia border this year, 307,000 were Russian nationals, 175,000 were Estonian citizens and 54,000 held Finnish passports, Estonian police data showed.

Rail freight is not affected by the road closure, but remains subject to strict customs checks, Estonia said.

World.title: 19 crew members airlifted after cargo ship runs aground in southwestern France
World.content:
PARIS: A cargo ship flying the Maltese flag ran aground off the coast of the Landes region in southwestern France amid strong winds early on Friday, leading to the evacuation of 19 crew members by helicopter, local authorities said.



Three ⁠crew members stayed ⁠on board the MIRO G to help secure the ship, the Landes Prefecture said in a statement, adding it was ⁠considering the possibility of towing the cargo ship.



A formal notice was issued to the shipowner of the MIRO G to “take all necessary measures to eliminate any immediate and future danger and, in the event of ⁠pollution, ⁠to minimize the environmental impact,” the statement added.



The MIRO G had been due to load 30,000 metric tons of wheat for Libya at the port of Rouen, according to LSEG data.

World.title: France probes actor Depardieu, author Houellebecq over alleged rape
World.content:
PARIS: French police are investigating allegations actor and convicted sex offender Gerard Depardieu and author Michel Houellebecq gang-raped and assaulted a woman on camera during a 2018 film shoot, two sources following the case said Friday.



Depardieu, who has acted in more than 200 films and television series, is the highest-profile figure caught up in France’s response to the #MeToo movement.



The accusation is the latest in a flurry against the 77-year-old screen icon, who on Monday dropped his appeal against an 18-month suspended sentence for sexually assaulting two women during the filming of another movie in 2021.



Depardieu is to learn next week if he will stand trial for raping another actress, Charlotte Arnould, in 2018. A judge has ordered a trial, but Depardieu has rejected the allegations and appealed.



In the new case, the alleged abuse occurred in December 2018, during the shooting of “Thalasso,” a film starring the two men as versions of themselves.



Its director, Guillaume Nicloux, has been accused of complicity in the sexual abuse, one of the sources said.



The woman, an actor and dancer who was 32 at the time, told French investigative outlet Mediapart she was hired for a nude part but never given clear directions for the scene, which was not supposed to include any sex.



She said that during the filming, Houellebecq pulled her into a hotel room and onto a bed where he forcibly kissed her, then Depardieu digitally penetrated her while the author pinned her down.



Houellebecq also imposed an oral sexual act on her without her consent while the cameras were rolling, she told the publication, leaving her experiencing “profound humiliation” and “indescribable shame.”



The woman’s lawyer did not wish to respond to an AFP request for comment.

- ‘Not simulated’ -

Depardieu’s attorneys did not immediately respond, nor did Houellebecq, who was contacted via his publisher.



The 70-year-old, who is among France’s most translated authors, is also under investigation for alleged incitement to discrimination in France over comments he made in 2022 about Muslims.



Last week, Mediapart and another outlet, Le Media, reported that another woman had accused Depardieu of groping her private parts when she appeared as an extra standing next to him during the filming of 2013 movie “Turf.”



The casting director told Mediapart she had to crouch down between them to ensure he could no longer touch the woman in the final takes.



In April, Depardieu dropped legal action against public broadcaster France Televisions over the editing of an investigative report aired in late 2023 in which he repeatedly made degrading and sexual remarks about women during a trip to North Korea.



In one of cinema’s most notorious scenes, Marlon Brando simulated anal rape of Maria Schneider in the 1972 film “Last Tango in Paris” without the director Bernardo Bertolucci informing her of the plan.



“Except that this time, it’s not simulated rape that the actor is denouncing,” Mediapart noted.

World.title: Turkiye opposition slams ruling against Istanbul mayor as ‘cowardice’
World.content:
ISTANBUL: Turkiye’s main opposition leader has denounced as “cowardice” a reported court ruling against Istanbul’s jailed mayor which would block him from challenging President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in upcoming elections.

The pro-government Sabah newspaper and other media had reported Thursday that Turkiye’s highest administrative court had ruled a degree earned by the popular mayor, Ekrem Imamoglu, was invalid.

Under Turkish law, presidential candidates must hold a valid university degree, meaning that the ruling by the Council of State would bar Imamoglu from the next presidential election, which must be held by May 2028 but could happen in a year’s time.

The ruling has not yet been published in the official judicial database (UYAP), legal sources said.

“This is clear proof they are afraid of Ekrem Imamoglu, even in prison,” said opposition leader Ozgur Ozel, who heads the Yeni Parti, describing it as “cowardice.”

The popular mayor — long seen as Erdogan’s biggest rival — was arrested in March 2025 on graft charges widely seen as political, sparking Turkiye’s worst street unrest in over a decade.

He was jailed on the day he was named presidential candidate for the Republican People’s Party (CHP) — at the time Turkiye’s main opposition party.

Following Imamoglu’s arrest the pressure on CHP escalated, with a controversial court ruling in May ousting Ozel as leader.

He went on to found Yeni Party with around 90 other lawmakers, which is now Turkiye’s main opposition.

Hours before police stormed Imamoglu’s home, Istanbul University had revoked his degree, alleging it had been falsely obtained — prompting him to appeal.

He has argued he began studying in the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC) then transferred to Istanbul University to complete his degree.

Ozel said he had no doubt that the court had indeed rejected Imamoglu’s appeal, calling government media who leaked the decision “the system’s seismograph.”

Imamoglu was still the opposition’s pick for president, Ozel said, saying his supporters would press every legal avenue to challenge the court ruling.

“Turkiye will not be left without a candidate,” he added.

World.title: European troops from 11 countries hold a drill in Poland for a potential postwar Ukraine mission
World.content:
NOWA DEBA, Poland: Thousands of European troops are taking part in an unprecedented military exercise in southeastern Poland to prepare for a potential postwar mission in Ukraine aimed at helping to stabilize the country and rebuild its military once the war ends.

Meanwhile, as the drill was underway, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said a Russian missile had crashed early on Friday near Poland’s border with Ukraine, describing it as likely an intentional provocation by Moscow that was timed to the drills.

The crash site of the missile is about 75 kilometers (47 miles) from the exercises.

“This was not an accidental event. It was coordinated with our show of force, our show of unity,” Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said Friday during a news conference at the drills. “Our presence here shows that we cannot be frightened.”

Led by France and the United Kingdom, the multinational force is a non-NATO military initiative of the so-called Coalition of the Willing, a wider political group of 37 nations supporting Ukraine.

The two-week exercise, which began on Nov. 9, is for the first time checking this coalition’s ability to deploy in Ukraine once the war ends. It is aimed both at testing deployment plans and sending a message to Russia and the Trump administration that European countries are stepping up militarily.

European allies rally in support of Ukraine

Leaders from Ukraine and nearly 40 other delegations met in Berlin on Thursday to underline their support for Kyiv and explore Ukraine’s postwar security arrangements.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky wants to ensure that Russia doesn’t invade again. Moscow wants to keep NATO away from its borders.

US envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday he believes Russia is “comfortable” with NATO-like security guarantees for postwar Ukraine. He and fellow US envoy Steve Witkoff were in Berlin to reassure European leaders about US President Donald Trump’s discussions on ending the nearly 5-year-old war at his historic trilateral talks Thursday with Russian leader Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in China.

Trump called into the Berlin talks following his meeting with Putin, according to Kushner.

Ukraine has long sought entry into NATO, particularly for its common defense guarantee under the alliance’s Article 5, in which an attack on one member is considered an attack on all. It was not immediately clear what form potential security guarantees would take, and whether Russia and Ukraine would ultimately accept them.

After Thursday’s meeting, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the drill in Poland shows that the “Coalition of the Willing is ready to contribute with the United States of America to securing a peace.”

A multinational force would help regenerate Ukraine’s military

Around 2,800 personnel from Belgium, Estonia, France, Germany, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden and the UK are taking part in the exercise, with Poland providing the logistical backup. Turkiye was participating remotely from Istanbul.

French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that 1,100 troops from France were deployed, and that “we have terrestrial, air but also maritime operations, a dozen countries that are active in this coalition.”

The exercise in Poland follows 12 months of planning by the Multinational Force-Ukraine, or MNF-U, said UK brigadier Campbell Close, who serves as deputy commander for operations of the French Army’s 1st division. That division is in charge of the land part of the “Koalicja” exercise in Poland.

“This is a deployment exercise,” Close said on Monday at the Nowa Deba military training ground in southeastern Poland. “We are a defensive force.”

He praised Poland’s handling of the logistics of moving thousands of vehicles, people and their equipment for the drill.

If deployed once a ceasefire is in place, the force would help regenerate Ukraine’s armed forces, provide the reassurance needed to open the country’s skies and help clear mines in the Black Sea, Lt. Gen. Tom Bateman, commander of MNF-U, has said. It would not have peacekeeping or peace-monitoring functions.

Soldiers practiced anti-drone defense and tested new gear

Coalition troops arrived in Poland by sea, air and land, the Polish government said, before traveling by rail and road to the Nowa Deba training site.

They rehearsed transporting personnel and equipment, as well as joint command-and-control exercises, and flew fighter jets and an aerial refueling tanker. They also operated surveillance drones, drilled responses to drone attacks and trained in trench warfare.

The initial idea of the Coalition of the Willing was to provide Ukraine with security guarantees similar to NATO’s Article 5. In the absence of a NATO commitment to fulfill this function, France and the UK decided to go ahead with plans for a separate European proposal of countries willing to come to Ukraine’s aid if necessary.

Last year, Putin said that any foreign troops inside Ukraine would be considered “legitimate targets.”

The multinational troops may have a purely defensive function, but they would still need to be a “combat force for their own force protection,” said Ed Arnold, a senior associate fellow at the RUSI military think tank in London.

World.title: Trump says Putin ‘expressed his desire’ for end of Ukraine war
World.content:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Friday that his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin told him he wants a diplomatic end to the Ukraine war, after Moscow’s forces launched a wave of daytime strikes on Kyiv.

In a bilateral meeting, Putin “clearly expressed his desire to see the war between Russia and Ukraine end by diplomatic means,” Trump told journalists at the White House.

World.title: Treasury Secretary Bessent insists US will continue squeezing Iran’s economy
World.content:
LONDON: The United States will continue to squeeze Iran’s economy until Tehran “sticks to a deal,” US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday.

Washington has made the economic isolation of Iran a cornerstone of the conflict, which started in February with joint US-Israeli strikes against the country.



In an interview with CNBC, Bessent described Operation Economic Outcast against Iran as the “greatest economic isolation of any country in history.”

Along with a US Navy blockade of Iran’s ports, the Treasury Department has moved to sever Iran’s financial lifelines to the outside world with sweeping sanctions against aviation, shipping, banking and digital exchanges.

The conflict has halted Iran’s oil exports, which were a mainstay of its economy before the conflict started.

“For the first time in history since Iran has started producing oil, they have no oil on the water, so there is no Iranian crude for anyone to buy,” Bessent said.

“What we’ve seen is the world can live without Iranian crude.”

After the war started, Iran attempted to block the Strait of Hormuz, the critical entrance to the Arabian Gulf through which about one-fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas flowed before the conflict.

However, the US military and its allies in the region have used a shipping lane along the south of the strait to rebuild exports of crude oil back to pre-war levels.

“Last night was the biggest amount of crude that’s come through the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict started,” Bessent said.

The flow of tankers is taking place at considerable risk with Iran carrying out regular attacks on vessels attempting to transit the waterway.

Bessent has faced threats of his own and was forced to move out of his family home and on to a military base over fears that he could be targeted by Iran.

Asked whether he was still living on the base, the treasury secretary replied that he would not be cowed by Iran.

"If the Iranians are after me, it means that they are being squeezed. We're going to continue squeezing them,” he said.

Bessent recently accompanied President Donald Trump to China for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

He said there was a consensus between the three superpowers that Iran can never have a nuclear weapon and that freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz is paramount.

With China being one of Iran’s key oil customers and Russia having important ties to Tehran, some observers were looking for signs that the meeting could help push the two sides back to negotiations.

The last week has seen an increase in hostilities with Iranian attacks on America’s Gulf allies like Bahrain and Kuwait and daily strikes against shipping.

World.title: Gulf alternatives may save Excelerate Energy’s LNG project in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Iraq is witnessing rapid on-site progress amid efforts to overcome geopolitical challenges and navigation risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz.

According to project updates, the field team and the materials required for constructing the marine jetty and terminal infrastructure have arrived in Iraq, Attaqa News reported.

US-based Excelerate Energy, which is carrying out the project, expects the pace of work to accelerate over the coming weeks, with construction activities progressing at the marine terminal and the facility’s infrastructure.

The firm aims to complete and commission the project during the second quarter of 2027, following a delay in 2026 caused by the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

Once Iraq begins imports, it will become the sixth Arab nation in history to import LNG—joining Kuwait, Egypt, the UAE, Jordan, and Bahrain.

The consequences of the Iranian conflict have caused delays for Iraq’s LNG project, which had originally planned to open in the third quarter of 2026. As a result, Excelerate Energy has moved the Excelerate Acadia, its floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), to Jordan for nine months.

To overcome disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the company plans to utilize an FSRU already stationed within the region, eliminating the need to traverse the strategic waterway.

The company is likely to utilize the FSRU currently stationed in the UAE, known as Express.

The US firm indicated that it is working to arrange the import of LNG from countries within the Gulf region, a statement that strongly suggests Qatar or the UAE.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Iraq’s parallel market
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced a slight increase on Thursday in both Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,706.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,706 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,710 Iraqi dinars and 1,700 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also increased, fluctuating between 1,709.5 and 1,708.5 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following the cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Iraqi PM orders reopening of closed roads in Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, ordered on Thursday to expedite the reopening of all closed roads in the Jurf al-Sakhar district in the central province of Babil.

During his meeting with security officials, al-Zaidi emphasized that the army and security forces would uphold the authority of the state across all Iraqi territory, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister emphasized that the enforcement of state authority would be carried out in accordance with the constitution and the law. He affirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the lives and interests of citizens across the country and to preventing any violations or assaults on public and private properties.

According to al-Zaidi, the security forces operate as a unified entity, with their numerous branches and units cooperating with one another.

These directives come ahead of the deadline set by the government for Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed militant faction, to withdraw from Jurf al-Sakhar—a deadline expiring on Friday—paving the way for security forces to enter and redeploy in the area.

The deadline for the withdrawal from Jurf al-Sakhar, also known as Jurf al-Nasr, follows an investigation by a government committee, which Baghdad stated uncovered evidence of oil smuggling operations in the area.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Iraq’s trade exchange with China drops to $19.8 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Chinese Ambassador to Iraq, Xiang Bo, said on Thursday that the decline in trade exchange with Iraq—which fell to $19.8 billion—is due to the escalating security tensions in the region.

During a press conference in Baghdad, Bo projected that trade between the two countries would recover, reaching $26 billion by the end of 2026 or early 2027.

According to Bo, China is a trusted partner to Iraq. He noted that the two countries share deep historical and cultural ties, dating back thousands of years.

Bo emphasized that bilateral relations have seen significant development, with Iraq serving as a key trade partner. Trade volume between the two countries reached $51 billion in 2025, reflecting the strength of their mutual commitments and relationship.

Bo mentioned earlier that major Chinese firms are involved in the construction and development of several industries in Iraq, such as oil, energy, and infrastructure.

The Chinese diplomat expressed his hope that this collaboration will continue and grow into other sectors, contributing to the development of a complete partnership between Iraq and China.

Chinese companies have been heavily involved in the oil industry and in significant infrastructure projects, such as the construction of major bridges and schools, with more than 600 schools completed in several Iraqi provinces.

World.title: Iraq studies issuing electronic dinar to expand financial inclusion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is investigating an electronic dinar as a digital extension of the current national currency to modernize payments, increase financial inclusion, and lessen reliance on physical cash.

Prime Minister’s financial adviser Mazhar Mohammed Saleh highlighted the initiative in remarks to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) on Wednesday, though no launch date, technical specifications, or formal issuance decision have been announced.

The electronic dinar will serve as a digital representation equal in value to the physical paper dinar rather than a new currency issue. It will not automatically generate new liquidity but will improve the management and circulation of existing funds.

According to the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI), approximately 102 trillion dinars ($67.38 billion)—nearly 92 percent of all currency issued—is held outside the formal banking system.

The purpose of a digital currency is to direct the financial reserves into formal savings, lending, and profitable ventures.

Moving transactions onto official digital channels will help curb unregulated financial dealings, reduce cash-printing costs, and align Iraq with the CBI’s financial inclusion strategy.

The digital dinar plan is different from suggestions to eliminate zeros from the physical currency.

Although the CBI has expanded bank cards, digital wallets, and points of sale, it has not yet declared a formal launch date or technical introduction timetable.

World.title: Egypt expresses interest in Iraq’s Development Road project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Egyptian officials have renewed their push for national firms to participate in Iraq’s Development Road project and broader infrastructure initiatives.

Egyptian Minister of Transport Kamel el-Wazir said that Egyptian companies are ready to join the Development Road and railway projects with competitive pricing, quality standards, and fast delivery.

El-Wazir’s remarks took place during his meeting with the Iraqi Ambassador to Egypt, Qahtan Taha Khalaf, in Cairo, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Egypt’s Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs, Hussein Issa, also met with Khalaf to discuss expanding trade, investment, and Egyptian company involvement in Iraqi development and reconstruction projects.

During a regional transport summit held two weeks ago in Alexandria, Egypt, Iraqi Transport Minister Wahab al-Hassani said that Iraq is moving toward the early implementation of land transport agreements with Jordan and Egypt to boost regional trade and cross-border movement.

Al-Hassani confirmed that Baghdad has finalized several land transport agreements with Amman and Cairo that are expected to enter into force soon.

The deals build upon a previously signed memorandum of understanding between the Iraqi and Egyptian transport ministries covering the overland movement of both passengers and goods.

Alongside the deals with Jordan and Egypt, al-Hassani highlighted Iraq’s broader push to establish itself as a regional transit hub through the country’s strategic project of the Development Road.

The strategic corridor spans 1,200 kilometers from the al-Faw Grand Port in the southern province of Basra to the Turkish border, combining new highway and railway networks.

World.title: Baghdad replaces forces holding Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered on Wednesday the replacement of the forces holding Jurf Al-Sakher, following an investigation into alleged oil smuggling.

The move seeks to end the 12-year control of the strategic Babil province area by the Iran-backed armed faction Kataib Hezbollah.

Iraq’s Supreme Committee for Security Sector Reform, chaired by Al-Zaidi in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief, ordered the replacement of the current force stationed in Jurf al-Sakhar with joint units from the Iraqi army, federal police, and other Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) brigades.

The Energy Police, an Interior Ministry force, was officially assigned to secure the three branches of the strategic Basra-Haditha oil pipeline running through the area.

Findings from a government investigative committee alleging oil theft and pipeline tampering were referred to the judiciary for legal action.

Before Wednesday’s deployment order, al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior security, intelligence, and oil ministry officials—including the director of the Oil Pipelines Company—in connection with the smuggling investigation.

The orders follow escalating tensions between Baghdad and Kataib Hezbollah, which has controlled the area south of Baghdad since recapturing it from ISIS in 2014.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Najaf refinery expansion to raise Iraq’s refining capacity by 70,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil refining capacity is set to increase further as the expansion project at the Najaf refinery progresses.

The project aims to add 70,000 barrels per day to the country’s refining output, aligning with Baghdad’s broader plans to boost the production of petroleum products and reduce reliance on imports.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi visited the refinery expansion site on Tuesday to evaluate the progress made and to assess the technical and logistical challenges encountered during the project’s implementation.

The project is being carried out amid Iraqi efforts to improve the efficiency of its refining sector and increase its capacity to meet the domestic market’s fuel needs.

The expansion of the Najaf refinery will increase fuel production to meet the requirements of surrounding industrial projects, create new job opportunities, and boost economic activity within the province.

The Najaf refinery expansion project includes the construction of a new refining unit with a capacity of 70,000 barrels per day. This development encompasses the completion of essential facilities and services needed to support its operation.

The project includes the development of energy infrastructure, an industrial water treatment unit, oil storage tanks, and other facilities associated with the refining unit.

The refinery’s current processing capacity stands at 30,000 barrels per day. With the addition of 70,000 barrels per day from the new unit, the expansion plans aim to increase the total capacity to 100,000 barrels per day.

World.title: 'Don't reduce it to bilateral': Pakistan minister in Delhi for SCO ducks question on terror
World.content:
Pakistan's Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination Musadik Malik speaks to reporters on the sidelines of the First Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum

NEW DELHI: Pakistan minister Musadik Masood Malik, who is in New Delhi for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum, on Friday sidestepped questions on Islamabad's harbouring of terrorists and failure to act against terror networks. He, however, acknowledged that India has suffered terror attacks.Malik, who is leading Pakistan's delegation at the three-day forum, sought to steer questions on cross-border terrorism towards broader regional security concerns, arguing that the SCO platform should not be reduced to bilateral disputes, news agency ANI reported.The minister also called for an evidence-based mechanism to address terrorism, insisting that both sides should present evidence and that discussions should focus on regional challenges rather than accusations.He acknowledged that India, like Pakistan, had suffered terror attacks, but avoided directly addressing questions on terrorist networks operating from Pakistani soil. Malik instead stressed dialogue, mutual understanding and regional cooperation, saying the SCO framework could help address wider security challenges across the neighbourhood."I am here at a multilateral forum. I wish for the discussions at this forum to proceed in a proper and orderly manner.The issues we face are not limited solely to those between our two nations; they have become far broader and more extensive. As you have seen, challenges have emerged in our neighbourhoodâin Iran, in Central Asia, and in Afghanistan. I do not wish to reduce such a significant, wide-ranging dialogue to a purely bilateral context," Malik said.When pressed further on cross-border terrorism at a gala dinner following the forum, the Pakistani minister again avoided a direct response, emphasising the need for countries to understand each other's perspectives and engage in constructive dialogue."However, when the time comes to address the issue of terrorism, you are well aware that thousands of our people have been martyred and we must ensure transparency. Both sides must bring forward evidence. Our objective is to establish a transparent mechanismâa proposal we have put forward on several occasions. Such a mechanism would help restore trust and could lead to viable solutions. Often, the necessary evidence is never presented," Malik claimed.Malik also sought to project Pakistan as a constructive regional player, saying Islamabad was committed to participating in efforts aimed at restoring peace and addressing instability.The first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum is being hosted in New Delhi as part of efforts to promote cultural exchange, mutual understanding and people-to-people ties among countries in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.The three-day forum brings together representatives from SCO member countries for discussions on civilisational links, cultural cooperation and regional engagement. Malik's visit marks the first visit by a Pakistani minister to India in three years.Pakistan's delegation is participating in thematic discussions at the forum, which seeks to strengthen cultural and civilisational engagement among SCO countries amid regional geopolitical tensions.

World.title: NIA probes 'Indian footprint' in flydubai pilot stabbing case, seeks UAE assistance
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The National Investigation Agency (

) is probing possible Indian links in the mid-air stabbing of a flydubai pilot and has sought documents from the UAE as well as permission to question some people there, news agency PTI reported, citing NIA director General Rakesh Aggarwal.

The probe is examining whether the accused Omani first officer had any Indian connections, including people in his circle who could have been linked to the alleged attack, Aggarwal said on Friday.

"We have already sent a mutual legal assistance request to the UAE asking for copies of certain documents and also permission to examine some persons in the UAE. So, we are waiting for a response from them," Aggarwal said.

The request has been sent under the Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty (MLAT), which enables countries to cooperate in criminal investigations.



The NIA is also examining the first officer's background, including reports that he studied in Australia or the UK, and is looking into whom he came in contact with during his time there.

"So whom did he come in contact with? Are there any Indian footprints of his friend circle who could be lurky? So there are various issues," Aggarwal said, adding that the agency would proceed with its investigation once it receives the documents and information from the UAE.





The NIA registered a case in October to investigate the larger conspiracy behind the September 30 mid-air attack on Captain Smit Machchhar aboard flydubai flight FZ 1073, which was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv.

According to the agency's FIR, the Omani first officer allegedly stabbed Captain Machchhar mid-air in an apparent attempt to hijack the aircraft or cause it to crash. The incident took place in Saudi airspace near the Jordan-Saudi Arabia border.

The agency has invoked Section 3 of the Anti-Hijacking Act, 2016, and provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, including Section 16, which deals with punishment for terrorist acts.

Captain Machchhar sustained critical injuries in the attack. The aircraft, carrying 174 passengers and six crew members, was landed safely at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz Airport in Tabuk, northwestern Saudi Arabia, by the other pilots on board. The first officer was arrested by Saudi authorities.

The NIA's probe is now focused on establishing the larger conspiracy behind the attack, including whether there were any Indian links or individuals connected to the accused's network.

on Friday hailed the party's performance in Rajasthan's panchayat elections, taking a swipe at the

World.title: 'No complaint in Tihar': NIA chief rejects US citizen VanDyke's claim of torture in jail
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The National Investigation Agency (

) chief Rakesh Aggarwal has rejected allegations of custodial torture made by US citizen Mathew VanDyke, saying he never raised any complaint about his incarceration in Tihar jail during his judicial custody.

VanDyke, accused of using India as a transit route to train insurgents in Myanmar, appeared before a Delhi court six to seven times during his custody, the NIA chief said.

âHe never raised any complaint regarding his incarceration during judicial custody in Tihar,â the NIA chief said, adding that VanDyke left India after securing bail and has visited the country once since.

The NIA chief also said a case under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) would be filed against VanDyke if any insurgent he trained in Myanmar is identified as an Indian citizen.



VanDyke alleged in a handwritten affidavit submitted in August, about two weeks before a chargesheet was filed against him, that he was repeatedly assaulted during his nearly six-month stay in Tihar jail.

He claimed he was punched in the chest and denied medical treatment for nearly 24 hours when he needed immediate attention. The affidavit was reportedly sent to the US embassy.

The allegations resurfaced on Monday after VanDyke posted the affidavit on X.





âIndia threw me and several Ukrainians into prison for over six months. This was part of Russia's war against Ukraine,â he wrote.

âI will reveal shocking details about this story over the next few months, in both posts and media interviews,â he added.

In the affidavit, VanDyke urged US embassy officials to âmake it very clear to any Indian officialsâ that if he got âangryâ with the contents of the chargesheet the NIA was preparing to file, he would approach the media and courts with details of his alleged custodial torture.

He also sent a distress alarm to his family, describing what he called a âseries of attacksâ inside Tihar. He alleged that he was beaten with a police baton on his chest and arms. Tihar authorities declined to comment when contacted by TOI.

The NIA arrested VanDyke and six Ukrainians, Kaminskyi Viktor, Hurba Petro, Slyviak Taras, Ivan Sukmanovskyi, Stefankiv Marian and Honcharuk Maksim, in March at various airports.

The agency alleged they had travelled to Mizoram without the required permits and crossed into Myanmar.

The agency suspected their links with armed groups operating in Myanmar, several of which maintain bases in Northeast India.

The case was registered under the UAPA in April, but the NIA's chargesheet invoked only Sections 21 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025. The agency told the court that its investigation into the UAPA angle was ongoing and that a supplementary chargesheet could be filed if an offence was made out.

World.title: Rajasthan panchayat election results 2026: 5 takeaways as Congress beats BJP; RLP makes big gains
World.content:
Two months after a bad show in urban polls, Congress rides the rural wave in Rajasthan.

Here are five key takeaways from the results.

1. Congress reverses 2020-21 rural poll trend

2. BJP takes hits on turf of its own leaders

3. Former BJP ally RLP makes big gains

4. Congress claims Jaipur

5. Independents and smaller parties could decide rural power

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Congress has turned the tables on the BJP in Rajasthan's rural local body elections, securing a decisive lead in Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad polls just months after the ruling party swept the state's urban civic elections.According to State Election Commission figures reported by ANI, the Congress has won 2,990 Panchayat Samiti seats against the BJP's 1,795, while in Zila Parishads, it has secured 143 seats against the BJP's 83. The figures are for declared results.The elections have also seen former BJP ally Hanuman Beniwal's Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP) make significant inroads, winning 438 Panchayat Samiti seats and four Zila Parishad seats. Independents have secured 516 Panchayat Samiti seats, emerging as key players in several local bodies.The results come after the BJP won boards in 197 of Rajasthan's 301 urban local bodies and could signal a shift in the state's rural political landscape.The Congress has emerged well ahead of the BJP in the rural polls, reversing the trend seen in the 2020-21 Panchayati Raj elections, when the BJP held the upper hand.In the main December 2020 round across 21 districts, the BJP won 353 of 636 Zila Parishad seats against the Congress's 252. It also secured control of 14-15 district boards, while the Congress won five.The BJP had also edged ahead in Panchayat Samiti elections, winning 1,989 seats against the Congress's 1,852. While the Congress recovered ground in subsequent phases, including in Jaipur, the latest results mark a substantial improvement in its rural electoral fortunes.The comparison, however, comes with a caveat. Rajasthan's administrative reorganisation has expanded the rural governance map from 33 to 41 Zila Parishads and from 352 to 457 Panchayat Samitis, making direct comparisons with previous elections difficult.Rahul Gandhi took to X to thank the people of Rajasthan. "This response has come from a state where the BJP has its own governmentâa direct response to the double engine," he wrote."Itâs a Congress wave in Rajasthan! Bucking the trend of supporting the ruling party at the State level, the people of Rajasthan have delivered a strong verdict in the local body elections - against the BJP's complete misgovernance in Rajasthan and the Centre," said Congress Lok Sabha MP KC Venugopal."All over India, the anger against BJP is coming to the fore - first seen in July, then against Gyanesh Kumar and now with such statewide rejection of the BJP," he added.The BJP's setbacks in areas associated with prominent party leaders have added to the significance of its rural poll performance.In Sikar, Urban Development and Housing Minister Jhabar Singh Kharra's wife Shanti Devi and son Ajay Singh lost their Panchayat Samiti elections. His other son, Durga Singh, who contested as an Independent, was also defeated.In Jhotwara, represented by minister Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore, the BJP reportedly won just one of the 15 seats, pointing to a difficult electoral showing in the constituency.The results, however, offered contrasting fortunes for the Congress. State party chief Govind Singh Dotasra performed strongly in his home turf of Sikar, while Tonk, associated with Sachin Pilot, also emerged as an important pocket for the party.The state BJP chief took responsibility for the loss. "Today, the election results for various Zila Parishads and Panchayat Samitis across Rajasthan have been announced. We accept the public mandate. We will also review where we may have faltered; we will examine these aspects and remain, as always, deeply committed to public service," Rajasthan BJP president Madan Rathore said.The Rashtriya Loktantrik Party has emerged as one of the biggest gainers outside the two main parties, winning 438 Panchayat Samiti seats and four Zila Parishad seats.The performance marks a significant expansion from the 2020 rural elections, when the RLP, then allied with the BJP, won 60 Panchayat Samiti seats and 10 Zila Parishad seats in the main round.Party chief Hanuman Beniwal has claimed that the RLP has received more votes than the BJP in Nagaur and is poised to secure the Zila Pramukh post there.He has also pointed to encouraging results in Didwana-Kuchaman, Barmer, Balotra, Bikaner, Churu and parts of Jaipur, while claiming the party was heading towards a majority in Sanganer Panchayat Samiti, in Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma's assembly constituency.The results reinforce the RLP's regional presence and give Beniwal greater leverage in Rajasthan's rural political landscape, particularly among its youth and farming communities.The Congress has won 14 of the 22 Panchayat Samitis in Jaipur district, emerging as the dominant party in the rural local body elections.The BJP secured majorities in Chomu and Sambhar, while the RLP won Sanganer. Five Panchayat Samitis returned fractured verdicts, potentially setting the stage for negotiations.The results have also produced contrasting outcomes for political families. Senior BJP leader Rajendra Rathore's son Parakram Singh won Zila Parishad Ward 39 by 17,861 votes, while his daughter-in-law Kanika Singh secured Ward 23 by 2,384 votes.While the Rathore family registered victories, the losses involving Jhabar Singh Kharra's family underscored that political influence did not necessarily translate into electoral success.The strong showing by Independents and regional parties could prove crucial in local bodies where no party has secured a clear majority.Independents have won 516 Panchayat Samiti seats, followed by the RLP with 438. The Bharat Adivasi Party (BAP) has secured 215 seats, CPI(M) 50, BSP 44 and AAP two.In Zila Parishads, Independents have won five seats, the RLP four, CPM three and BSP one.With the posts of Pradhans and Zila Pramukhs elected indirectly by ward members, the results could trigger political negotiations and alliances in several districts.Elections for Zila Pramukhs are scheduled for November 25, while Panchayat Samiti Pradhan elections will take place on November 27. Counting in Kota, Baran, Karauli and Sri Ganganagar has been deferred to December 17.The results give the Congress a significant rural boost ahead of the 2028 assembly elections, put the BJP's grassroots connect under scrutiny and strengthen regional players such as the RLP. However, local body elections are shaped by candidate-level factors, caste equations and local issues, and are not necessarily a direct predictor of assembly electoral outcomes.

World.title: State govt. should clarify on dismissal of Guidance employees: Anbumani

PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss on Friday said that the dismissal of 15 employees of Guidance TN was “worrying” as the State government has remained silent.

In a statement, Dr. Anbumani said that the people of Tamil Nadu have a right to know the truth behind these reports after investments worth ₹1,614 crore from three South Korean companies that were expected to come to Tamil Nadu have moved to Andhra Pradesh

“The employees reportedly dismissed have offered a different version of events. They have claimed that the working environment in Tamil Nadu had become unfavourable for them following the change of government and that they resigned within a month of the new government assuming office. They have also stated that they had lodged a complaint with the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary about the deteriorating work environment at Guidance TN. World.title: Man arrested for sexual assault and murder of woman on train in Nagercoil
World.content:
Nagercoil junction railway police arrested a 31-year old man on Friday on charges of sexually assaulting and murdering an unidentified woman at a train stationed at Nagercoil yard.

The decomposed body of a woman was recovered from a train coach on Wednesday (November 18). The train had been stationed at the yard since November 11 for maintenance work. The body was found in a coach reserved for differently abled persons.

Following that Nagercoil junction railway police have registered a case and began their investigation.

A special team was formed under the leadership of Inspector Catherine Sujatha to apprehend the accused. The team examined footage from cameras installed across the Nagercoil junction railway station. The scrutinisation of footage from November 14 showed a man wearing a white dhoti and shirt and getting down from the differently abled persons coach of the train.

Police tracked down the suspect, identified as J. Ayappan, 31, from Chenbagaramanputhoor and arrested him on Friday.

According to investigators, Ayappan dragged the unidentified woman, who was walking on platform number 5, into an isolated differently abled coach at around 12:30 a.m. on Saturday (November 14). He allegedly sexually assaulted her and brutally attacked her that led to her death. Further investigations are on.

World.title: Safeguards against abuse of power essential to preserve critical institutions like ECI: S.Y. Quraishi
World.content:
I

Former Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) S.Y. Quraishi has expressed concern over the functioning of India’s constitutional institutions. Speaking on Friday (November 20, 2026), he warned that the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s credibility “may take years, perhaps decades, to repair”.

Opinion | The SIR and its error margin

Delivering the 17th V. M. Tarkunde Memorial Lecture in Delhi on the theme ‘Constitutional Institutions of India: Where Are They Headed?’, Mr. Quraishi said institutions such as the ECI, judiciary and executive needed strong safeguards against the misuse of power.

On the ECI, he said its credibility had come under strain since 2019. Further controversy over the 2024 Lok Sabha election turnout figures, former Election Commissioner Ashok Lavasa’s dissent, and concerns over the SIR did not help.

He pointed out that those who framed the Constitution probably did not anticipate a situation such as the one involving present CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

Referring to West Bengal, he said, “The experience of West Bengal exposes the frightening consequences of the SIR exercise. Of the 27 lakh voters deleted during adjudication, 22 lakh appealed for restoration. Yet before the Assembly election, only 1,607 names were restored because hearings had not been done, leaving the overwhelming majority unable to vote. Although I think the Supreme Court had the option of saying that since the number is so large, 2.7 million, let them vote.”

He said subsequent appellate tribunal decisions reportedly found 93% of more than 1.2 lakh exclusions incorrect, raising further questions about the exercise. He called for an independent audit of the SIR, disclosure of decision records and digital audit trails, and restoration of names deleted without lawful authority.

Government control of ECI

On the appointment of election commissioners, Mr. Quraishi criticised the 2023 law replacing the Chief Justice of India with a Union Minister nominated by the Prime Minister on the selection panel. He said this effectively gave the government control over two of its three votes and called for transparent appointments and an independent selection process.

Speaking on the current situation of the judiciary, he questioned the Chief Justice of India’s discretionary power in allocating cases and suggested that a panel of three senior judges manage the roster through a transparent, preferably computerised, system. He also flagged opacity in judicial appointments and delays in government clearances.

He said the Supreme Court’s decision upholding the ECI’s authority to conduct the SIR in Bihar had not addressed concerns about procedural fairness and the exclusion of eligible voters.

Questioning the inconsistent application of the principle that bail is the rule and jail the exception, he said, “In November 2020, a prominent television anchor’s bail petition received super urgent consideration, resulting in his immediate release. Meanwhile, another journalist, Siddique Kappan, was arrested while travelling to Hathras to cover a horrific crime.”

He also cited another example in which the courts turned a blind eye towards a minister, who said ‘goli maro salo ko’ but kept students in jail for six years for charges that are yet to be proven.

He also highlighted the backlog of nearly 5.6 crore cases across the country, calling for limits on adjournments and time-bound disposal.

Mr. Quraishi condemned the Government over the suspension of 146 MPs in December 2023, when three major criminal laws were passed, saying legislation affecting citizens’ liberty required meaningful Opposition participation.

He also questioned Speakers’ impartiality in deciding disqualification petitions, citing the delay in deciding cases following the 2022 Shiv Sena split in Maharashtra.

He cautioned Governors against delaying assent to Bills for political reasons and called for clearly defined powers and timelines. He also sought greater scrutiny of the CAG, particularly over alleged suppression of adverse audit findings, and warned against political considerations in UPSC appointments.

Concluding his address, Mr. Quraishi called for independent appointments, collective decision-making, recorded reasons and dissent, and stronger accountability. He said disputes involving electoral rights, government formation, and legislative disqualification must be resolved promptly to prevent irreversible damage.

Former Supreme Court judge Madan B. Lokur and senior Supreme Court advocate Raju Ramachandran spoke about Justice Tarkunde’s long fight for Constitutional values and civil liberties.

World.title: Holiday Expo showcases tourism destinations from India, abroad
World.content:
The two-day Holiday Expo, featuring tourism destinations from India and abroad, began at the Gadiraju Palace Convention Center in the city on Friday.

More than 75 exhibitors from over 10 States and five international destinations are taking part. Rajasthan Tourism and Delhi Tourism are the partner States. Andhra Pradesh Tourism is showcasing the State’s beaches, heritage sites, pilgrim centres and nature tourism.

The stalls cover hotels, resorts, airlines, cruises and travel technology. The expo is open to the travel trade and the public.

“Visakhapatnam is an important and growing travel market, and we are delighted to bring this platform to the city,” said Rohit Hangal, Director, Sphere Travelmedia and Exhibitions Pvt. Ltd.

Tours and Travels Association of Andhra Pradesh president K. Vijaymohan, Hotel and Restaurant Association of Andhra Pradesh president Pavan Kartheek and officials of the Rajasthan, Delhi and Andhra Pradesh tourism departments attended the inauguration.

The expo ends on Saturday. The next edition will be held in Coimbatore on January 29 and 30, 2027.

World.title: Ensure no household is left out in Census enumeration, officials told
World.content:
District Revenue Officer S.D. Anita on Friday directed officials to complete the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 accurately and within the stipulated time.

Addressing a two-day training programme for district and charge-level officers at the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) South Zone office at Suryabagh, she said that because the city is densely populated, officials should make sure no household is missed. Homeless people must also be counted, she added.

Ms. Anita said self-enumeration would be open to residents from January 10 to 24, 2027. The technical glitches in the app during the housing listing phase had been fixed, she said, and officials should make the public aware of the facility. She pointed out that citizens are legally required to provide information under the Census Act, 1948.

GVMC Additional Commissioner K. Ramesh suggested a target of at least 40% self-enumeration to reduce the burden on field staff. Census Joint Director S. Dayasagar also spoke.

World.title: One held in theft case; 40 grams gold recovered in Anakapalli
World.content:
Anakapalli Town police on Friday cracked a house break-in case within 24 hours of the complaint and arrested a 23-year-old habitual offender, recovering the entire stolen gold jewellery weighing 40.590 grams from him.

The accused was identified as K Rakesh, a catering worker and resident of Sarada Nagar Colony, Anakapalli.

According to the police, the accused Rakesh gained entry into a locked house in Sarada Nagar Colony. The owners, after returning home on November 19, found that the gold was stolen and lodged a complaint. The police used technical evidence to identify the suspect and apprehended the accused. Entire stolen gold of 40.590 grams was recovered

Police said Rakesh was a habitual offender and had been previously arrested in three theft cases at Anakapalli Town, S. Rayavaram and Munagapaka police stations.

The accused was subsequently produced before the court.

The installation ceremony of Ignatius Gonsalves, senior journalist and author, as a Pontifical Knight (Chevalier) will be held at Infant Jesus Church near the Kerala High Court on November 22.

Pope Leo XIV made him a Knight of the Equestrian Order of St. Sylvester on August 8, 2026, in recognition of his outstanding contributions to the Church and society. The honour was announced by Archbishop Joseph Kalathiparambil, Metropolitan of Verapoly, according to a release.

World.title: Freshwater fish species discovered in Western Ghats
World.content:
Researchers at Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies (Kufos) claimed to have discovered two new freshwater fish species from the Periyar-Cardamom Hills of the Western Ghats.

Mesonoemacheilus mannanorum, one of the two species, has been named after the Mannan community and is found in streams deep inside the Periyar Tiger Reserve. The second species, Mesonoemacheilus sabariensis, is named after the Sabari hills and is found in streams near Angamoozhi in the Pamba river system, according to a communication.

The discoveries were made by a team led by V.K. Anoop and Rajeev Raghavan from the Kufos and Neelesh Dahanukar from the Shiv Nadar Institution of Eminence, New Delhi. The research has been published in the Journal of Fish Biology, it said.

World.title: Anthropic mathematician claims to have solved 167-year-old Riemann Hypothesis using Claude AI
World.content:
A mathematician working at artificial intelligence company Anthropic has claimed to have proved the 167-year-old Riemann Hypothesis, one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics, with the help of the company’s AI model Claude, reported Scientific American.

Levent Alpöge said he had discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis while working with Claude, and that the method also extended to the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, a much broader mathematical conjecture.

“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote in a statement posted on his personal website on Friday.

The claim has not yet been independently verified by the mathematical community. Alpöge has made the purported proof available as code written in Lean, a programming language used to formalise mathematical arguments and check their logical correctness.

Scientific American described the Riemann Hypothesis as one of the most famous open problems in mathematics. Technology publication OfficeChai also reported that the proof had been released in 14 parts and that independent verification was still pending.

Alpöge said the formalisation of the argument was complete but acknowledged that the proof was extremely long and that he had not yet produced a readable mathematical paper explaining it.

What is the Riemann Hypothesis?

First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers, numbers that can be divided only by themselves and one.



Although prime numbers appear to occur irregularly along the number line, mathematicians have established patterns governing their distribution. The Riemann Hypothesis proposes a deeper relationship between these patterns and the zeros of a mathematical function known as the Riemann zeta function.

It also states that all the non-trivial zeros of the function have a real part of exactly one-half.

Proving the hypothesis would provide a much more precise understanding of how prime numbers are distributed. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems identified by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which offers a $1 million prize for a correct solution.

The institute’s website continued to list the Riemann Hypothesis as unsolved on Friday.



How did Claude help with the purported proof?

In his statement, Alpöge described the work as a collaboration in which he guided the research while Claude supplied several crucial mathematical ideas.

He said the breakthrough came from combining two different approaches in number theory. One of the central ideas involved adapting a technique known as Stepanov’s method, previously used to address an analogous version of the Riemann Hypothesis in the mathematical setting of function fields.

The challenge was to find a way to reproduce the role of multiplicity in ordinary number theory, where the conventional technique could not be directly applied.

Alpöge said Claude suggested using a sequence of mathematical operations known as theta lifts to address this difficulty. He described the AI model as having substantially outpaced him towards the end of the work.



“Tens of such occurred,” he wrote, describing the number of occasions when Claude came up with unexpected mathematical steps.

He also acknowledged that parts of the argument were beyond his own technical expertise and that the proof would need to be simplified and explained in a form that other mathematicians could understand.

The purported proof has been formalised in Lean, a proof assistant that allows mathematical arguments to be checked step by step by a computer.

A year of rapid progress in AI-assisted mathematics

The announcement comes after a series of developments involving Alpöge and Claude that have attracted attention in the mathematical community.



In August, Anthropic reported that an unreleased research version of Claude had improved a longstanding lower bound on the proportion of zeros of the Riemann zeta function lying on the critical line from 41.6% to 67.2%. That was progress on a related question, not a solution to the Riemann Hypothesis.

In September, Scientific American reported on Alpöge’s AI-assisted work on the 1947 Hopf problem concerning the existence of a complex structure on a six-dimensional sphere. The publication reported that mathematicians had begun reconstructing and examining the argument.

World.title: Post pilot event, Total Chess open to player feedback
World.content:
Magnus Carlsen suggested Champions League-style seedings for draws.

Praggnanandhaa didn’t understand why players were playing for classification spots at the end of the group stages after missing the semi-finals spot. Wesley So wanted the blitz games in the knockouts to count for two points. Some players like Ian Nepomniachtchi and Fabiano Caruana had sharp comments about Carlsen opting to pick and choose which games he will forfeit in a match.

The pilot event of Total Chess in Budapest has led to plenty of conversation about the format, the points system and the rules for players forfeiting games.

Almost every player out of the 24-player field has had their say about what they like and don’t at an event that is being held to test the rules for a full-fledged Total Chess tour the next year with three events that culminate into a world championship title.

Kjell Madland, the man behind Total Chess, believes that not “too many things will change” for the tour next season. But he has said that the organisers will hear feedback from a host of stakeholders, most importantly the players, before deciding on the final form that the next year’s four tournaments will take.

He did indicate that the organisers will tweak rules to prevent a situation where players forfeit games, something that world No.1 Magnus Carlsen did against Bibisara Assaubayeva (in fast classic games) and Vladislav Artemiev (in rapid games) before Richard Rapport and Abhimanyu Mishra followed suit as well.

“We didn’t expect that this (forfeits) would be a big discussion. But at the same time, it’s very good that it happened in the pilot event, and not in the first event of the World Championship tour next year, because it’s not possible to change something when you have started the tour. You need to have the same rules all the time throughout the tour. So now we have the possibility to discuss this in the working group,” Madland told The Indian Express.



“We are very happy about how the tournament has been so far. When it comes to rules and regulations and some adjustments, of course we need to look at that. We have asked players and others about what they think and I feel that there are just small things that need to be done,” Madland added.

Madland pointed out that at an event like the one that ended on Friday with 24 players competing, there was likely to be an avalanche of feedback from everyone involved.

Their job over the next few months before the start of next year’s tour would be to sort out the feedback.

“We want to see if there are things that many people feel. Because when you talk to people, it’s different things. Some have suggestions about the points system, some about adjustments in the group stage. We can change things if many people are saying something. But I don’t think there are very many things we need to change,” Madland added.



Some players have spoken about being exhausted by playing in the format, especially two fast classic games a day in the group stage and then playing seven games across fast classic, rapid and blitz in the knockout stages.

“We wanted it to be like this because when you want to find the best chess player overall, they need to fight. They need to have a very tough competition. If you are chasing a big title, then players should, of course, be tired. It’s the same when they are playing 14 games in the classical World Championship, where they play a game for maybe six or seven hours a day as well and are very, very tired,” he added.

The writer is in Budapest at the invitation of Total Chess.

World.title: Meta office premises vandalised in Hyderabad, Youth Congress workers detained
World.content:
About 20 Youth Congress workers were kept under preventive arrest for staging a protest at Meta’s office in Hyderabad’s Madhapur on Friday.

The protest was held with the Youth Congress workers alleging that Meta had withheld their social media pages. They also alleged that many of their posts were removed by the platform.

They were released after three hours.



Speaking to The Indian Express, State Youth Congress president Shiv Charan said they went to the office for a peaceful protest but were not allowed into the building. “META is in with the RSS and the BJP and have turned hostile towards the Congress’ content on social media. So we went to their office to give a representation. They did not let us in and the police arrested us,” Charan said.

World.title: Vijay Deverakonda, Rashmika Mandanna’s Japan vacation sparks wanderlust: How Indians can get a visa
World.content:
Vijay Deverakonda recently shared a series of pictures from his vacation to Japan on Instagram, offering a glimpse of sweet family moments. He and Rashmika were in the ‘Land of the Rising Sun’ on Diwali, and Vijay even shared a picture saying, “When you find a way to do GOMA (Homam) in Japan on Happy DIWALI.”

Cherishing the days spent in Japan, the Ranabaali actor shared another set of pictures, writing, “Celebrating Life with my favourite people. A few memories doing life right with those that are my life, Japan Nov 2026.”

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Vijay Deverakonda (@thedeverakonda)

Visa and passport rules for Indians who want to visit Japan

Japan is getting ready to embrace winter, and before that happens, you might be planning to see the vibrant colours during this fall, or the Koyo (Koh-yoh) season. But wait before you start packing your bags. Why?

Because Japan does not have a visa on Arrival for Indian nationals. Read on to learn the application rules and process for getting a visa before you set off.



ALSO READ | China visa rules: 6 documents Indian applicants need to keep ready

As per Vishesh Gakhar, Director, Visa Mitar Immigration Consultants, “You can apply for Japan’s visa either using Japan’s eVisa official website or through an accredited agency such as VFS. The application route depends upon the country of residence, not nationality.”

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.

Confused? Let’s understand this.

“Indian nationals residing in India are bound to go through VFS Global, while those living abroad, in countries like the UK, the US, Canada, and Australia, can use

Japan’s official eVisa portal. This eVisa is only for tourism purposes, with a permitted stay of up to 90 days. In case of any other visa category, application procedures and relevance changes apply,” Gakhar says.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Vijay Deverakonda (@thedeverakonda)

He also explains the steps to apply for a Visa:

Identify the correct Visa Type

Complete and sign the Japan Visa Application Form

Prepare Supporting Documents such as passport, photographs, travel itinerary, and flight schedule

Submit the application and documents at the designated VFS centre; no prior Appointment is required.

Pay the applicable fees

Track Application

“In terms of passport validity, Japan does not explicitly state that you need a minimum of 6 months’ validity on your passport when you’re applying for a visa, but it must stay valid during your intended stay,” he adds.

Documents required to apply:

This is what Gakhar mentions:



A valid passport; submit old passports as well (if any)

Photocopy of the bio page of the Current Passport

One passport-size photograph taken within the last 6 months

Cover letter, if any explanation is needed

Show flights/cruise schedule

Travel Itinerary

Latest ITR and bank statements for the last 6 months

However, he mentions that, in case of a dependent, consent from the parents/spouse, along with the latest Income Tax Return of the parents/spouse (6 months’ bank statements if the ITR is not available), is required. In addition, proof of relationship is required if the applicant is accompanied by any dependent (i.e., passport copy, Marriage Certificate, Birth Certificate), and the embassy may request an interview or additional documents based on your circumstances.

“Effective 19 October 2026, all visa applications for Mumbai, Pune, Ahmedabad, and Goa must be submitted by prior appointment, in accordance with instructions from the Consulate General of Japan in Mumbai. Walk-in submissions will not be accepted,” Gakhar adds.

Visa fees effective July 1, 2026:

On the fee structure, Gakhar says fees for single and multiple entry for Indian nationals are INR 500, while for other nationals they are: single visa at INR 8,650; multiple or Double visa: INR 17,350.
